I measured no problem on the suite or the journeys. An epoch or a reset when the cache and all documents are gone would bound it.
- `name_count` of a document can differ between a cache hit and a miss: selector parsing interns names into the document that builds the set.
- `dblclick` and `hover` aim once, like `click` did.

## P3 register VM, stage 2 slice 1: closures, inline calls and global cells (2026-11-14, `docs/design-js.md` phase P3)

Branch `t3/bytecode-closures-globals`, rebased on main `1e793d74`. The tree walker stays the default. The lane runs with `BARE_JS_EXEC=byte` or `auto`. The browser session now reads `BARE_JS_EXEC` too (`SessionConfig::new`), so the journeys can run the lane. With the variable unset the mode is `Tree`, as before.

### What I built

1. Captured variables (a function with inner functions is a register function with an environment). The call makes the stage 1 environment (`new_env` and `bind_call`). A variable that an inner function names stays a binding of that environment. All other variables are registers. A scope has a run-time environment only when an inner function lies inside it, so the hop count of `bc_resolve` stays right for the inner function, on the tree walker and in the lane. Boxed cells of a new kind were not needed: the existing `Env` layout is the cell.
2. Inline calls. A call from any lane code (stage 1, register function, register function with environment) to any compiled function of the same script runs in the same loop, with no Rust frame. A frame keeps its own environment depth (`Fr.depth`) and the environment of its call (`Fr.callee_env`). `bc_frame_exit` unwinds them. Default parameter values run in the callee environment and frame.
3. Global cells. A cell keeps the position of a global property, or the index of a binding of environment 0, with the count of those bindings. Environment 0 only gains bindings, so a cell stays valid while the count is the same. A script with `let`, `const` or `class` at top level (environment 0 not empty) uses the cell too.
4. Counters: `BARE_JS_STATS=1` prints, for each interpreter, the functions compiled, the calls that the lane ran, the calls that the tree walker ran because the lane refused the function, and the refusal reasons.

Order. The plan puts boxed cells first, then calls, then global cells. The task listed globals first. I followed the plan: a global cell gains nothing while environment 0 is empty (the `loop` row did not move), and the gain of a closure is larger (`closures` 1.23x to 1.35x, and every function with an inner function stops being stage 1).

Not built: inline `new`. `new` goes through `bc_call` and `construct` (Rust recursion). A call from a native function (`map`, `sort`, a callback) enters the loop again by Rust recursion. Both work and are covered by the differential tests.

### Numbers: `eval_load CASE 10`

`tools/js/instr.sh` method (`instructions:u`, large malloc cache), archMachine, 3 runs each, the three runs differ by under 0.01%. Tree is the same on main and on the branch (under 0.01%). "Main byte" is main `1e793d74` with `BARE_JS_EXEC=byte`.

| Case | Tree | Main byte | Branch byte | Tree / branch byte |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `loopfn` | 4,091.0 M | 841.0 M | 823.0 M | 4.97x |
| `fib` | 165.9 M | 53.2 M | 56.6 M | 2.93x |
| `loop` (globals) | 5,007.0 M | 2,515.0 M | 2,487.0 M | 2.01x |
| `calls` | 3,532.2 M | 2,109.3 M | 1,641.3 M | 2.15x |
| `closures` | 646.4 M | 522.5 M | 478.8 M | 1.35x |
| `objects` | 2,389.4 M | 2,329.0 M | 2,335.8 M | 1.02x |
| `throws` | 1,947.2 M | 1,496.2 M | 1,490.5 M | 1.31x |
| `webpack` | 38.5 M | 50.2 M | 50.5 M | 0.76x |

- `fib` costs 6.3% more than on main in the lane: 581 instructions for each call, against 546. The cause is the larger frame record and the two checks of the environment of a frame. I made `bc_frame_exit` inline (60.4 M to 56.6 M). A cold side for the environments made it worse (58.4 M), because of code layout, so I kept the first form. The spike gate of 3x on `fib` is now 2.93x.
- `webpack` is slower in the lane than in the tree walker: 502 functions compile, and each runs about 3 times. This is the compile cost. `auto` gives the same number as `byte`, because it compiles at the second call. A start of the lane in `byte` mode costs 0.3 M instructions more than on main (`fib 1`: 7.20 M to 7.50 M).
- `loop` is limited by the script body, not by globals. The body of a script runs as stage 1 (a stack code), about 600 instructions for each iteration. `loopfn` is 410.

### Numbers: ramps and journeys

- JS ramps of the benchmark round (`/data/bare-tmp/bm/b/pages`, `bare-drive`, 3 runs, spread under 0.01%). `steps_1000000` (a loop in a script body): tree 1,812.5 M, lane 959.5 M (1.89x). `steps_10000000`: 18,057.5 M and 9,527.5 M (1.90x). `nest_100`: 7.7 M and 7.9 M. `nest_1022`: 10.7 M and 11.0 M (+2.8%: the compile cost of the first call is not paid back). All pass in both modes.
- 47 journeys on the recorded virtual-clock corpus, lane on against off (`/data/bare-tmp/slice1/jrun.py`, 3 runs each, spread 0.4% or less): the sum of instructions goes from 89,935 M to 89,871 M (-0.07%), median row -0.08%. No journey is over +5%. The best rows: `crates-io-home` -48.4% (132 M to 68 M), `docs-rs-home` -22.6%, `duckduckgo-html-search` -16.5%, `rust-lang-org-home` -12.3%. The worst: `rust-book-sidebar` +2.8%, `nodejs-org-home` +2.3%, `rust-book-chapters` +2.1%. PSS sum 1,315 MiB to 1,320 MiB (+0.4%). PSS is a poll every 20 ms in the first run only, so single rows (for example -99% on `crates-io-home`) are noise. `nextjs-docs` fails in both modes (it is flaky on main too).
- **The lane runs 34.9% of the function calls of the 47 journeys** (1,090 k of 3,127 k). The tree walker runs the other 65.1% after the lane refused the function. The reasons, in calls: `no scope` 1,629 k (80% of the refused calls: the body of a lazy function, which the lane never runs), `wide form` 276 k (13.5%), `destructuring` 65 k, `spread` 39 k, `for-in or for-of` 17 k, `regexp literal` 6 k.
- Answer for the owner: the lane is not ready to become the default. On the journeys it gives -0.07% instructions and +0.4% memory. The cost of compiling is paid by cold pages, and the gain is on the pages that run a hot loop in a function. Two designs move the share: run lazy bodies in the lane (80% of the refused calls), and compile the script body as a register function (the `steps` ramps and `loop`).

### What went wrong on the way

- A first journey run showed -10% instructions in total, with `react-docs` -55% and `mdn-reference` -24%. It was wrong: `function f(a, b = a + 1)` and `function f(a, ...r)` failed in the lane ("a binding that the code generator expected"), because a call from the loop evaluated the default values before the callee environment was current. The page swallowed the error and ran less code. A journey that passes only shows that its steps pass, not that the JS result is the same. `exec_diff.sh` found it (2 differences). With the fix `react-docs` is -2% and `mdn-reference` +0.9%.
- The same run showed `go-dev-home` at 46.3 G instead of 3.2 G. Cause: `bc_resolve` built the list of bindings of a scope for each site of a function, so a function with many sites in a large scope cost sites times statements. The list is now the cached template of the scope (`bc_tmpl`). The old code is on main and runs in `byte` mode there too. I did not run main on the journeys: main ignores the switch in the browser.
- `local_at` found a variable of an outer scope when a captured variable of an inner scope had the same name (`var x; { let x; { const x; return (() => x)() } }`). A captured name now stops the search.

### Checks

- `cargo test --release -p bare-js --lib`: 951 pass. New tests in `bc_gen_tests.rs`: 33 programs that run on tree, auto and byte and must agree (closures, loops that make closures, blocks and switch, arrow `this`, TDZ, `arguments`, default and rest parameters, throw through frames, `Error.stack`, call depth 200, shadowed names), global cells that follow a later script (a `let`, a deleted and made name, a `const`, a name in its TDZ), a listing of a function with a closure.
- `cargo test --release --workspace --no-fail-fast`: 3,917 pass, 8 fail. They are the 7 known openssl TLS tests and `a_hidden_iframe_download_is_saved`. Two other known flaky tests (`a_changed_file_starts_again_from_zero` and `external_sheets_embedded_sheets_and_inline_styles_cascade_in_order`) failed in one of two runs under load and pass alone.
- `tools/js/exec_diff.sh`: 79 runs, 0 differences.
- `tools/js/test262_check.sh`: tree, exit 0, no directory lost a test. With `BARE_JS_EXEC=byte`: only the 3 known `top-level-await` tests lose (40 to 37), and the result list of byte equals the one of tree otherwise (32,838 tests).
- `tools/js/cost_matrix.sh` against main `1e793d74`: 803 rows, 0 over +0.5% under both allocators, mean glibc +0.002%, jemalloc +0.009%. Two rows are over under glibc only: `form_load gates 1` +0.62% and `gates 10` +0.65% (jemalloc +0.01%). The switch is off in these rows, so I treat them as heap layout. `parse_load deep 1` and `deep 10` fail to run (stack overflow) on main too.
- `tools/js/typing/keycost.sh`: tree 295.7 M for each key on `#a1` and 301.0 M on `#f0`, load and mount 613.6 M, peak RSS 30.7 MiB at 50 keys (the values of the last merge: 295.7 M, 301.1 M, 613.8 M). With `BARE_JS_EXEC=byte`: 296.8 M, 302.2 M, 629.3 M.

### Not tested

- Wall time on an idle machine. Live pages. A deep recursion beyond depth 200 in a program that mixes the three kinds of frame (the unit test stops at 200, the ramp `nest_1022` runs a plain function). `Error.stack` text of inline frames against Node beyond the fixtures. The peak memory of a deep recursion (the register stack grows by `resize`). Journeys on e16. A page that reads `cssRules` or the DOM from a function with a closure in the lane beyond the 47 journeys.

### Noticed, not changed

- The GC still runs only at depth 0 of the lane (step 5 of the plan). `Auto` compiles at the second call of any function. A hotness count might remove the `webpack` loss (hypothesis, not built).

## Rule-set cache: idle sets bounded by bytes (2026-11-14)

Task: stage 1 of rule-set sharing (#515) raised the summed peak RSS of the 47 journeys by 2.3% (1,691 to 1,730 MiB), and the Wikipedia journeys by 4% to 14%. The cause was the last set of the document before, kept in the cache. Branch `t3/bound-rule-cache-bytes`, rebased on main `8d64702a`.

Owner decision (2026-11-14): bound the idle sets (sets that only the cache holds) by bytes. Keep small repeated lists, drop large one-off sets. Compare at least two eviction rules before choosing one. Target: journeys summed peak RSS within +0.5% of the build before #515 (1,691 MiB), Wikipedia journeys within +1%, most of the instruction gain on `docs-rs-home`, `duckduckgo-html-search`, `rust-lang-org-home`, and the suite at about 10.4 G.

### What I built

- `RuleSet::heap_bytes` (`cascade.rs`, `Selector::heap_bytes` in `selector.rs`): the live bytes of a set, counted from the sizes of its tables, also the lazily read blocks and the split lists.
- `rule_cache`: idle sets weigh at most `MAX_IDLE_BYTES` = 2,500,000. Over that, the set with the lowest priority goes. Priority = uses + the priority of the last set that went (GDSF with a cost in proportion to the size, so uses and age decide).
- `settle` (called by the document after it replaced its set): the step of a page (the set before its next one) goes at once. Before, it went one list too late, so each loading page held one set more than before #515.
- `Cache::diverged`: a document that asks for a list that the document before it did not ask for is on another site. The idle sets that it did not use go at that look. A page of the same site makes the same lists in the same order.
- `MAX_RULES` (65,536 rules) is removed. The real bound is now the bytes. The `max_rules` and `max_names` limits of a document stay.

### Measurement 1: the live size of a set (bytes, not rules)

A counting allocator in a temporary build (not committed: `/data/bare-tmp/rcb/experiment-all.patch`) measured the bytes that one build leaves alive, for the first build of each of the 45 journeys that build one. `heap_bytes` gives 0.90 to 1.00 of that (the difference is the allocator's own bookkeeping of the sheet of the browser, about 7 KB, so small sets are the 0.90). Sets with 400 or more rules are 0.95 to 1.00.

| Set | Rules | Live bytes | Bytes for each rule |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| suite fixture (60 KB sheet) | 2,272 | 1.31 MB | 577 |
| `docs-rs-home` | 1,333 | 0.94 MB | 704 |
| `duckduckgo-html-search` | 1,489 | 0.97 MB | 648 |
| `rust-lang-org-home` | 2,201 | 1.19 MB | 542 |
| `wikipedia-article`, last list | 1,782 to 2,533 | 1.31 to 2.06 MB | 734 to 813 |
| `python-org-docs-link`, the list that hits | 2,938 | 2.19 MB (2.26 MB after styles read blocks) | 745 |
| `github-docs-home` | 8,919 | 7.88 MB | 884 |
| `devto-home` | 17,456 | 12.4 MB | 711 |

The sets that a later document found in the cache (31 hits in 22 journeys) are 0.08 to 2.26 MB. The sets that were idle and never hit (18 cases) sum to 19 MB, 7.9 MB of that is `github-docs-home`. A hit set and a wasted set have the same sizes, so size alone cannot tell them apart. All hits are one document after the set was used.

### Measurement 2: the rules

Journeys: `journeys.sh compare --clock virtual`, corpus `virtual`, 47 journeys. Base is main before #515 (`f68e956a`). The same-binary spread of the sum is -0.30% to +0.16% for RSS and -0.4% to -0.1% for the Wikipedia rows (two runs of 5, the binary against itself). Peak heap is the peak of live bytes of the page thread (counting allocator, deterministic: two runs gave the same number).

| Config | RSS sum, median / min | Wikipedia RSS, median / min | Instructions | Peak heap sum (Wikipedia) |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| #515 as merged (15 runs) | +1.25% / +1.26% | +3.7% / +4.3% | -0.76% | 775.2 MiB (145.1) |
| drop every idle set at each look (9 runs) | -0.51% | +1.2% (noise) | -0.64%, gains of the 3 journeys gone (-2.0%, -1.7%, -1.7%) | 763.5 (143.7) |
| `settle` and 2.5 MB, no `diverged` (15 runs) | +0.66% / +0.41% | +2.0% / +2.4% | -0.74% | 765.4 (144.0) |
| `settle`, 2.5 MB and `diverged` (15 runs) | +0.26% / -0.20% | +0.2% / +0.1% | -0.74% | 764.1 (143.7) |

- Byte bound alone: 1.5 MB gave +2.2% on Wikipedia (5 runs, before `settle`), 1.0 MB lost the gain of `rust-lang-org-home`, 2.5 MB gave +2.0% to +2.4%. The idle set that remains is a set of the page before that the next page does not use, and it is the same size as a set that is used. So the byte bound caps the worst case (`github-docs-home` 7.9 MB, `devto-home` 12.4 MB, `substack-home` 6.8 MB never stay), and `diverged` removes the rest.
- `settle` alone changes the peak heap by 0.3 MiB over 47 journeys (774.9 against 775.2): the step costs less than it seemed. It stays because it is the same set one list too early.
- Eviction rules among the idle sets, at 2.5 MB with `settle`: largest first, oldest first, GDSF. On the 47 journeys the peak heap is 765.4 MiB for all three: at most one or two sets are idle, so they choose the same set. On the suite the same: one set. A synthetic stream (30 sites, sizes lognormal with a median of 0.8 MB and a long tail to 8 MB, Zipf visits, half of the visits repeat the last site, 20 streams of 4,000 visits, `/data/bare-tmp/rcb/sim.py`) at 2.5 MB: hit bytes 0.580 (largest first, mean idle 2.21 MB), 0.609 (oldest first, 1.54 MB), 0.657 (GDSF, 1.83 MB). At 5 MB: 0.628, 0.672, 0.723. GDSF is chosen: the most hits at each budget, and it keeps a set that is used often.
- The number 2.5 MB: the largest set that a journey found in the cache is 2.26 MB (`python-org-docs-link`); 2.5 MB leaves 0.24 MB of room over it. The suite's set is 1.37 MB. Below 2.3 MB the `python-org-*` gain (-3.2%) is lost.

### Final numbers (clean build, rebased on `8d64702a`, measured before the rebase for the journeys and the suite: the rebase only added `crates/js` changes)

Journeys, 9 runs, base = main before #515 (`f68e956a`):

| Measure | Before #515 | Branch |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| Instructions, sum of medians | 90,536 M | 89,729 M (-0.89%) |
| Peak RSS, sum of medians | 1,684.0 MiB | 1,681.6 MiB (-0.14%). Minimum of the runs: 1,659.6 / 1,658.0 (-0.09%) |
| Wikipedia journeys, peak RSS | | -0.1% (median), +0.5% (minimum) |
| `docs-rs-home`, `duckduckgo-html-search`, `rust-lang-org-home`, `python-org-docs-link`, instructions | | -25.5%, -17.9%, -14.3%, -3.2% |

Against main with #515 (`1e793d74`), 9 runs: instructions 89,713 M to 89,727 M (+0.02%), peak RSS 1,707.9 to 1,688.0 MiB (-1.2%), Wikipedia -3.3% to -9.8% for each journey (-4.9% summed). `github-docs-home` -7.7%, `python-org-docs-link` -4.4%. The three gains stay (+0.2% to +0.4% against #515 on those rows, 0.2 to 0.3 M).

Suite (40 tests, one worker, shared login, 3 runs): branch 10,053 M (10,042 to 10,067), main with #515 10,061 M (10,054 to 10,066), before #515 13,162 M. Peak RSS of the worker 27.1 (26.8 to 27.4) / 26.8 / 26.2 MiB. The first build of this change walked the set at each idle check and cost 10,118 M (+0.57%); the walk now runs once for each set. Against the frozen V0 (21,078 M) the suite is 2.10 times lower. It is 10.05 G, not 10.4 G: main moved since #515.
Suite of 800 tests (the 40 repeated 20 times, `/data/bare-tmp/rcb/suite800`), 1 run: 198,211 M, 28.0 MiB; main with #515 197,976 M, 27.9 MiB; before #515 259,671 M, 27.1 MiB.

### Checks

- `cargo test --release -p bare-css --lib rule_cache`: 10 tests, 4 new (`idle_sets_weigh_at_most_the_budget_and_the_one_with_fewer_uses_goes`, `a_set_over_the_budget_goes_when_nobody_holds_it`, `the_step_of_a_page_goes_when_the_page_has_its_next_set`, `a_page_on_other_lists_than_the_page_before_drops_its_idle_sets`). The old test of the 65,536-rule bound is replaced. `browser_rule_share_tests`: 11 of 11.
- `cargo test --release --workspace --no-fail-fast`, after the rebase: only the known failures: 7 openssl tests (`https_openssl` 2, `client_openssl` 4, `tls12_openssl` 1, `BadSignature`), `a_hidden_iframe_download_is_saved`, `downloads::run::tests::a_changed_file_starts_again_from_zero`. None is in code that I changed.
- `tools/js/cost_matrix.sh` against `8d64702a`: 803 rows, 0 over +0.5% under both allocators, 0 over under one. Mean change glibc +0.001%, jemalloc +0.000%. `parse_load deep 1` and `deep 10` do not run (stack overflow, as on main).
- `tools/js/typing/keycost.sh`: `#a1` 295.7 M, `#f0` 301.0 M for each key, load and mount 613.6 M, peak RSS 30.9 MiB at 50 keys (the last merge: 295.7, 301.0, 613.6).
- `test262_check.sh` and `exec_diff.sh` not run: no change in `crates/js`.

### Not tested

- Real network timing. `diverged` assumes that a page of the same site makes the same lists in the same order. With a real network the lists of the first look can differ, and then an idle set goes one document early (a lost gain, never a wrong style). The corpus replay uses a virtual clock.
- A page with many frames (each frame is a document of the thread: its look counts for `diverged` and `new_document`). A suite on more than one worker. The wall time of the suite and of the journeys (shared machine). The 800-test suite has 1 run. The 15-run RSS rows use the build with the experiment switches (same code path as the final build; the final build was measured with 9 runs).
- `heap_bytes` is read once for each set when it is first idle. The set grows by 3% after that (`python-org-docs-link`).
- The measurement counters, the switches and the synthetic stream are not in the repository: `/data/bare-tmp/rcb/` (`experiment-all.patch`, `an.py`, `peaks.py`, `sim.py`, the traces in `trace/`).

### Noticed, not changed

- RSS of one journey moves by 2% to 3% from run to run on the same binary; the sum by 0.3%. A change of 1% on the Wikipedia rows needs 9 or more runs to show.
- `Counts.rules` (rules in the cache) is removed with `MAX_RULES`; nothing used it.


## Modern color rendering, 2026-11-14

Issue #464. Candidate production source: 79164130. Modern absolute colors and two-operand mixes now reach the existing sRGB painter. Deferred currentColor expressions share the variable arena. Color stays four bytes, Value eight bytes and Side 72 bytes. Stored deferred entries grow from 32 to 56 bytes. The color crate uses its Rust libm backend to avoid an extra shared-library load on ordinary pages.

The final serial release run passes 1,913 tests with seven ignored. The selected three-row browser cost gate passes its unchanged 0.5 percent rule under both allocators. The final 390-pixel synthetic page and real Deck primary button pass computed-color and inspected-pixel checks. The tests use headless bare; no mirrored test is claimed. Full resource samples, failed intermediate checks and syntax limits are in [the results](rendering-colors-results.md).

No installation, merge or deployment is included. Wrapping remains separate in #467.

NEW and BASE: `base-build <sha> --release -p bare-drive`. The cost matrix and the stress runs use the `base-build` default trees (`--release --workspace --examples`) plus `--release -p bare-stress`.

### Criterion 1 and 2: the journeys

Inputs: corpus `virtual`, 47 journeys, 3 runs plus the PSS run for each journey and binary (94 journey-binaries, 4 runs each, runs interleaved). Command: `tools/bench/journeys.sh compare --clock virtual --runs 3 --pss /data/bare-tmp/fb/bin/bare-drive-base-vclock /data/bare-tmp/fb/bin/bare-drive-new`. Log: `/data/bare-tmp/fb/journeys.{log,tsv}`.

- All 47 journeys pass in all runs on both binaries. The same-binary spread of instructions is 0.3% or less on every journey (target of the clock task: under 2%). The replay has zero misses, except `mdn-reference` on NEW (47 misses in each of its 4 runs) and 1 miss in run 0 of `wikipedia-toc-languages` on BASE.
- **`mdn-reference` on NEW does not do the recorded work.** It asks for 47 JS chunk files at a wrong address (`GET https://developer.mozilla.org:443/en-US/7489.879b548e785958fd.js`, and 46 more like it; the recording has them under another path) and no reply is recorded for them. The journey still passes. Its instructions fall from 6,978 M to 1,862 M (-73.3%) and its peak RSS from 116.0 MiB to 29.6 MiB. That is not a gain. I ran the journey with `BARE_NET_REPLAY` on the merge commits in between: 0 misses at `226935a5` and `0727ffef` (#498), 47 misses from `e497ff5f` (#492) up to NEW. So PR #492 changed the address of these requests. Hypothesis: the page builds the chunk address from a script address or a script property (a webpack public path), and the lazy function parse of #492 changes that value. Not examined. On the live site this would be 47 failed chunk loads. This looks like a correctness regression; it needs an issue and a fix. I did not change code.
- Without `mdn-reference`, the 46 other journeys give: instructions 98,211 M to 87,857 M (ratio 0.895), CPU 11,220 ms to 10,389 ms (0.926), peak RSS 1,989.7 MiB to 1,712.0 MiB (0.860). I report 85.3% (all 47, as measured) and 89.5% (without it). Both miss the 80% target.
- Totals, sum of medians: instructions 105,189 M to 89,719 M (-14.7%, ratio 0.853). CPU (user+system) 12,090 ms to 10,579 ms (-12.5%). Wall 11,343 ms to 10,190 ms (-10.2%, loaded machine). Peak RSS 2,105.7 MiB to 1,741.6 MiB (-17.3%).
- PSS: the 20 ms sampler of run 0 misses many short journeys (17 of 47 give under 10 MiB, mostly 0.0, for at least one binary). Over the 30 journeys with a valid sample on both sides, PSS is 1,696 MiB to 1,339 MiB (-21%). This is not a criterion and the sample is partial.
- Median change of a journey: -13.7%. Geometric mean of the ratios: 0.729. 36 journeys are more than 5% lower, 9 are within 5%, 2 are more than 5% higher (`wiktionary-portal` +10.6%, `paulgraham-home` +10.3%).
- The total is held up by five journeys: `react-docs` (16,936 M), `rust-book-search` (16,315 M), `wikipedia-article` (7,701 M), `wikipedia-search` (7,244 M) and `nodejs-org-home` (5,864 M). They are 60.3% of the NEW total, and they moved by -0.8% (54,510 M to 54,060 M). The other 42 journeys went from 50,679 M to 35,659 M (70.4%). Hypothesis: these five spend their instructions in page JS execution, which the steps of the goal did not reduce much (the profile of 2026-11-13 gave JS execution 25.5% of the journeys and 57.7% of the ramps). Not measured per subsystem on NEW.

### Criterion 8: the limits

- Restyle charge. Method: a page that restyles 6,002 elements (the `rest_13` page with 3,000 loops, element count from the step 4 notes) runs until the 500 M step budget of a task ends the script (`LIVE_TASK_STEPS`, `crates/bare/src/page.rs`). Then instructions divided by the budget is the instruction cost of one charged step. `/data/bare-tmp/fb/pages/rest_3000_j.html` logs the loop counter every 25 loops.
  - BASE: the budget ends after 14 or fewer restyles (the ramps: `rest_13` passes, `rest_15` stops) at 11,636 M instructions: 23 instructions for each charged step.
  - NEW: the budget ends after 1,700 to 1,724 restyles at 102,842 M instructions (60.1 M for each restyle): 206 instructions for each charged step.
  - A step of a plain JS loop costs 198 instructions (`steps_5000000` to `steps_50000000`: 1,805 instructions for each iteration, about 9.1 steps for each iteration, from the benchmark round of 2026-11-13, section B: 55 M iterations fit in 500 M steps).
  - So the charge was about 9 times the cost on BASE (23 against about 200) and is 1.04 times the cost on NEW (206 against 198). Met. `STEPS_PER_RESTYLED_ELEMENT` is 32 (`crates/bare/src/browser_computed.rs:229`). One run each, deterministic.
- `cssom-objects` cap. `MAX_OBJECTS = 1 << 19` (524,288) at `crates/bare/src/browser_cssom.rs:20`, and `MAX_RULES = 1 << 21`. The old value was 65,536. The cap is not removed and is not computed from the rule count: it is a fixed constant chosen from the measured bytes of a read rule (585 B, about 290 MiB at the cap). Probes in criterion 5: the realistic 16 MiB sheet (187,852 rules) is read in full, and the dense one (844,366 rules) stops at the cap. A different limit, `style-objects` (65,536), binds first when a page reads `.style` of every rule. Not met as written ("removed or set by the rule count"). It is met in effect for the biggest sheet the loader accepts that has realistic rules. I report it as partly met.
- The `computed-work` cap is unchanged (nodes times rules). The step 4 section shows it refuses `comp_48000` and `compm_34000`, which cost 1 to 3 G with the index. I did not re-measure that.

### Other: `bare-stress` growth exponents on the style cases

`bare-stress scale css` (50 style cases, each at 1x, 10x and 100x of its base size, one process for each size), BASE and NEW `bare-stress`, 3 runs each, alternating. The exponent is `log(time at the last size / time at 1x) / log(size ratio)` from wall time inside the process (not instructions: this tool measures time). Tables per run: `/data/bare-tmp/fb/stress/{BASE,NEW}.{1,2,3}.md`; per-case summary: `/data/bare-tmp/fb/ssum.md`.

- No case has a time exponent over 1.5 on either tree, in any of the 6 runs. The largest median exponents: BASE `css-layers-statement` 1.19, `css-var-many` 1.18, `css-selector-list` 1.12. NEW `css-layers-statement` 1.20, `css-var-many` 1.18, `css-selector-list` 1.12, `css-var-chain` 1.12. The flagged list is the same in all 6 runs and on both trees: 3 memory limits at 2 GB (`css-rules` at 10,000,000, `css-selector-list` at 5,000,000, `css-unique-styles` at 2,000,000).
- Memory (peak MB of the counting allocator at the largest size that ran, median of 3 runs). 41 cases have a peak of 5 MB or more on one tree. 19 of them are within 5%. NEW is more than 5% higher on 20, and more than 5% lower on 2 (`css-layers-anon` 1,111 to 952 MB, `css-media-many` 1,111 to 1,025 MB). The largest rises: `css-bad-rules` 1,208 to 1,313 MB (+9%), `css-declarations` 1,007 to 1,107 MB (+10%), `css-important` 503 to 603 MB (+20%), `css-long-value` 0.1 to 100.1 MB, `css-escapes` 20 to 60 MB, `css-import-many` 151 to 189 MB (+25%); `css-rules` at 1,000,000 rules 433 to 450 MB (+4%). Hypothesis: three of the rises are +100 MB on a 100 MB input, one extra copy of the sheet text. The lazy rule bodies (#498) keep the block text. Not checked.
- Time at the largest size, median: NEW is faster on `css-rules` (722 to 410 ms), `css-bad-rules` (4,367 to 3,078 ms), `css-escapes` (236 to 147 ms) and `css-is-wide` (814 to 561 ms). It is slower on `css-var-uses` (213 to 250 ms) and `css-important` (1,548 to 1,691 ms). These are wall times of a shared machine, so they are weak.

## Fix: `import()` and `import.meta` in a lazy function belong to its module (2026-11-14)

Branch `t3/fix-lazy-js-chunk-path`, on `8f879534`. Fixes the regression that the final benchmark found in `mdn-reference` (PR #492, lazy function bodies).

### Cause

`mdn-reference` loads a bundler runtime, `/static/client/runtime.<hash>.js`, an ES module of 19,664 bytes. Its loader is `import("./" + o.u(chunk))`, in a function of the runtime. A browser resolves `./<chunk>.js` against the module's address, `/static/client/`. Since #492 the function is lazy: its first call parses it again and runs the tree in a script slot of its own (`lazy_load`). `mod_of_current` found the module by comparing the running script slot with the slot of each module. The slot of a lazy tree is no module's slot, so `import()` gave no referrer, the host resolved against the page (`/en-US/`), and `import.meta` in such a function threw "import.meta outside a module". Verified: the recorded runtime has `o.p="/static/client/"` and `import("./"+o.u(s))`, and the replay asked for `/en-US/7489.879b548e785958fd.js`; the chunks are recorded under `/static/client/`. Hypotheses in the benchmark (`document.currentScript`, stack file names, a regex) were not the cause.

### Change

- `Interp.lazy_owner` (`eval.rs`): the slot of each lazy tree, mapped to the slot of the script that holds its stub. Filled in `lazy_load` (`eval_scripts.rs`), after the tree is walked.
- `mod_of_current` (`eval_modules.rs`) follows `lazy_owner` up to the slot that a module owns (a lazy function inside a lazy tree takes more than one step). It runs only for `import()` and `import.meta`. Lazy parsing stays on for modules and pages.
- Other readers of the current script slot do not need it: `hscope_find` reads handler functions, which are small and never lazy. The stack frames key by slot and keep working.

### Tests (written first, failing on main)

- `eval_modules_tests::a_dropped_function_of_a_module_is_still_code_of_that_module`: a module of 20 KB with two lazy functions (one nested in a lazy function) that call `import()` and read `import.meta.url`. Failed with `Unsupported("import.meta outside a module")`, passes now.
- `browser_loader_tests::a_dynamic_import_in_a_lazy_function_is_relative_to_its_module`: a page loads `/static/rt.js` (long, lazy `load(n)` with `import('./' + n + '.js')`); the chunk must come from `/static/c1.js`. Fails on main (empty log), passes now.
- No `exec_diff` case: the byte lane refuses module syntax (`bc_gen_expr.rs`), so the fixtures hold no module code.

### `journeys.sh compare` checks replay misses

`compare` prints "Replay misses" at the end: per journey, the most misses of runs 1 to N for each binary. A journey fails when NEW has more than BASE; the script prints `FAILED` and exits 1. A miss that BASE also has (the `wikipedia-portal` beacon POST, 1 each) does not fail. Run 0 (PSS) is left out, because its timing gives misses that the other runs do not. `run` prints the most misses of a journey after its median line. Check: `compare` of `0727ffef` against `e497ff5f` on `mdn-reference` prints `base 0 new 47 FAILED` (exit 1); a unit check of the report on made-up rows (mdn 0 vs 47, wp 1 vs 1, run-0 only miss) fails only the first.

### Numbers (archMachine, corpus `virtual`, `BARE_CLOCK=virtual`, `bare-drive` built with `-p bare-drive`, instructions are the median of 3 runs)

`mdn-reference` replay: 47 misses on main (`8f879534`), 0 on this branch (1 run, then 3 runs of the full set below). Instructions: 2,102.3 M on main, 7,179.3 M on this branch (+241.5%), peak RSS 31.9 to 113.9 MiB. This rise is expected: the page code now runs. The merge before #492 (`0727ffef`) gave 6,978 M and 116.0 MiB in the benchmark. The branch is +2.9% above that. Hypothesis: later merges changed the cost of the page's code; not examined.

The 47 journeys, main against branch, 3 runs: all pass, same-binary spread 0.4% or less on the branch (2.3% on main for `wikipedia-toc-languages`, 1 run with 1 miss). Except `mdn-reference`, no journey moves by more than 0.1% in instructions. Total 90,359 M to 95,445 M (+5.6%, all from `mdn-reference`; 88,257 M to 88,266 M without it). Peak RSS sums: 1,694 to 1,775 MiB (`mdn-reference` +82 MiB; others within noise, `wikipedia-article` +2.5 MiB with equal instructions). Misses: `mdn-reference` 47 to 0, `wikipedia-toc-languages` 1 to 0. The total of the final benchmark (85.3%) changes with this fix: its `mdn-reference` row was 1,862 M instead of about 7,100 M.

### `wiktionary-portal` and `wikipedia-portal`: not the same cause

Instructions, M, median of 3 runs, 0 misses in all runs, spread 0.1% or less:

| Journey | `0727ffef` (before #492) | `e497ff5f` (#492) | main `8f879534` | this branch |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| `wiktionary-portal` | 1,213.4 | 1,582.5 | 1,559.9 | 1,560.0 |
| `wikipedia-portal` | 999.9 | 1,254.4 | 1,233.0 | 1,233.0 |

The fix gives no change on either. They have no module with `import()`; the cost step is still #492. Hypothesis (not measured): the second parse and the extra script slot of the lazy functions that these pages call. They have a standing exception in "Standing exception: PR #492" for another row only; these two rows need their own look (a source-size threshold for lazy bodies, or cheaper second parse).

### Checks

- `cargo test --release --workspace --no-fail-fast`: all pass except the 7 TLS tests that fail on main (`https_openssl` 2, `client_openssl` 4, `tls12_openssl` 1) and `a_hidden_iframe_download_is_saved` (flaky under load; passes alone).
- `tools/js/cost_matrix.sh` against main `8f879534`: 803 rows, 0 rows over under both allocators, 0 over under glibc, mean +0.000%; `parse_load deep 1` and `deep 10` do not run (known stack overflow).
- `TEST262=/data/claude-tmp/test262 tools/js/test262_check.sh`: exit 0, no directory below the baseline.

- `tools/js/typing/keycost.sh`: 295.6 M for each key (`#a1`), 301.0 M (`#f0`), load and mount 613.7 M, peak RSS 30.9 and 31.0 MiB. Not compared with main (no change on the typing path; the cost matrix has the rows).

### Not tested

A live run on developer.mozilla.org (the chunks load on the recorded corpus only). `import()` inside a lazy function of a classic script (no referrer there, as before). A realm shared across threads with `lazy_owner` (the map is per realm, as `lazy`). Windows and macOS.

## R2-D: why lazy JS functions cost more on the portal journeys (2026-11-14)

Task: measure and design, docs only. Design: `docs/design-js-reparse.md`. Main `28a8fbc2`. Counters and scripts: `/data/bare-tmp/r2/R2-D/` (`counters.patch`, `r2d.rs`, `sweep*.sh`, `s1` to `s4` raw rows). Machine archMachine, corpus `virtual`, 3 runs per journey and mode (counter files: 1 run).

### Result

- **The hypothesis holds, with a correction.** The first parse of a long function is a full parse that drops its nodes, not a preparse. A function that runs is parsed again, and so is every long function inside it. A function `d` lazy functions deep that runs is parsed `d + 2` times. Depth reaches 7.
- `wiktionary-portal`: 1,561 M lazy, 1,239 M with lazy functions off (same binary), 1,213 M before #492. Second parses 331.4 M (655 functions, 3.04 MB), load step 19.9 M, walk saved -39.1 M. `wikipedia-portal`: 1,234 M, 996 M, 1,000 M. Second parses 237.8 M (703, 2.11 MB), load 16.0 M, walk saved -25.6 M.
- 47 journeys: lazy 95,488 M, lazy off 91,998 M (+3,490 M, +3.8%), `nonest` (lazy only in the first tree) 93,804 M. Peak RSS sums 1,779.7 / 1,841.6 / 1,800.3 MiB. Split of the 3,490 M: second parses +3,115.5 M, load +357.6 M, walk saved -809.0 M, slot swaps +822.5 M.
- **A second cause: slot swaps.** Each lazy function is a script slot. A call across slots swaps 11 interpreter fields, about 190 instructions. `react-docs` has 1.40 M more swaps than eager code (272 M), `nodejs-org-home` 0.67 M (129 M), `github-docs-home` 0.44 M (83 M). This explains the rows that the second parses do not.
- Not the cause: the parse cache (0 hits on the portals), the regex compile (185 programs, 42 M, lazy is cheaper than the old walk-time compile), the garbage collector.
- Share of lazy functions that run: depth 0, 37% by count and 75% by bytes (3,470 of 9,471; 13.91 of 18.44 MB). The portals: 85% and 83%. 66% of the second-parse bytes are lazy bodies inside the function (17.34 of 26.37 MB).
- Raising `LAZY_MIN_BODY` from 128 to 8,192 gives -1.6% instructions and +5.3% RSS on 18 journeys. It is a weak lever.

### Recommendation

A: keep skip data (end position, strictness, inner table) for lazy functions inside a lazy function, as V8 skippable functions and the JSC `SourceProviderCache` do. Estimate: -1,989 M over the 47 journeys (range 1.6 to 2.4 G), `wiktionary-portal` about 1,317 M, `wikipedia-portal` about 1,072 M, RSS unchanged (0.3% for the table). Then S: make a slot swap one pointer swap (estimate -730 M). Criterion 2: 90.1% to about 88.2% (A) and 87.5% (A and S). Not B1 (no lazy functions: -3,490 M, but +61.9 MiB RSS), B2 (a higher body limit), B3 (a heuristic), or C (a record of which functions ran: no gain on a cold run). Fallback: D, measured -1,685 M, +20.6 MiB.

### Not tested

A prototype of A or S (their gain is arithmetic from counters and swap counts; the per-byte cost of inner bodies may differ by 20%). Swap counts on 39 of the 47 journeys. RSS of A. Live sites, other platforms, the byte lane. The cause of +25 M at lazy off against `0727ffef` on `wiktionary-portal` (23 merges in between).

### Noticed, not changed

- Data literals only exist in the lazy parse mode (`self.lazy`). A switch that turns lazy parsing off also turns them off. A first sweep of this task did that and gave a false -857 M on `python-docs-search`.
- `journeys.sh`-style runs under heavy load showed 1 to 4 replay misses on four `wikipedia-*` rows of the threshold sweep. The main sweeps had 0.
- The parse cache keeps one entry for the lazy kind and one for the eager kind of the same text (from #492).

## R2-B: where the Wikipedia journeys spend instructions (2026-11-14, docs only)

Design: `docs/design-wikipedia-journeys.md`. Task R2-B of the round 2 plan. No product code changed. Machine-local files: `/data/bare-tmp/r2/R2-B/` (counter patch, no-settle patch, profiles, TSV files).

Method: symbol build of main `28a8fbc2`; `perf record -e instructions:u -c 500000` with frame pointers, 3 runs per journey; counters in a patch (`BARE_FORCE_STATS`); the corpus `virtual`. Instruction spread of the journeys: 0.1% (`wikipedia-article`, 3 runs: 7,776 M), 0.0 to 3.1% (`wikipedia-search`, 7,338 M; run 0 had 2 timing misses).

Measured split (mean of 3 profile runs, spread 0.5 points or less):

| Subsystem | `wikipedia-article` | `wikipedia-search` |
|---|---:|---:|
| Style | 30.7% | 25.2% |
| JS execution | 22.5% | 22.3% |
| Window named-property list rebuilt (`browser_frames::build`) | 11.5% | 10.7% |
| Layout | 8.8% | 11.9% |
| JS parse | 8.4% | 10.6% |
| Other (DOM bindings 3.7%, selector API 2.7%, HTML 2.4%, CSS parse 2.3%, regexp 1.8%, rest) | 18.1% | 18.7% |

Findings:

- The round 1 hypothesis (the heavy journeys are bound by page JS) is wrong for Wikipedia. JS is 33% and 35%. Style, layout and the name list are 51% and 48%.
- The replay driver's `settle_pictures` loop is 74% of `wikipedia-article`, 56% of `wikipedia-search` and 52.8% of all 47 journeys (95,376 M with it, 45,037 M without; all journeys pass without it). The baseline pays it too: criterion 2 is 90.7% with it and 89.3% without it (2 runs each, `-p bare-drive` builds). `react-docs` is 99.3% loop (16,948 M to 127 M). Owner decision needed: keep or bound the loop (both sides, baseline measured again).
- Window names: 54 and 40 rebuilds of a list of every id of the page (15 k nodes, 17 M each) for 16 and 18 global names that do not exist. All stale by `name_revision`. 894 M and 785 M.
- Style: 8 full passes (782 M) for one load of the long article, caused by 4 appended sheets, 2 restyles that gave up and 2 frame requests. One hover restyled 90,232 elements (9 times the document, 865 M, 10.8% of the article): covered roots are styled again. The 10 "kept" layouts of each journey reused 0 fragments.
- Memory (`massif`, one run): heap peak 50.6 MB, of which JS objects 27.6%, JS trees 10.5%, DOM attributes 7%, layout fragments 8%. RSS without the loop: 33.0 MiB against 60.3 MiB.

Recommendation: W1 (window name by one walk, no list), H1 (skip a covered restyle root), S-A (one retained cascade and layout updated by damage marks). Estimate on the settled benchmark: article -38.5%, search -32.8%, the two -5.4 G (5.7% of the total): criterion 2 from 90.7% to about 85.5%. If the four other Wikipedia journeys gain 25 to 35% (hypothesis), 82 to 83%. The arithmetic is in section 7 of the design.

Not measured: the four other Wikipedia journeys; the roots of the 90 k restyle (cause is a hypothesis); why a reload of the same page pays the same rule-build cost; wall time; the live sites.

## Style round 2: measurements and design (R2-E, 2026-11-14)

Task R2-E of the round 2 plan. Design: [design-style-round2.md](design-style-round2.md). Docs only. Base: main `28a8fbc2`. Machine: archMachine. Each case ran 3 times. The spread of instruction counts was 0.

### Criterion 3: what is left in `compm_22000` and `rest_13`

Driver totals: `compm_22000` 1,835 M (target 1,166 M, -36.5%), `rest_13` 1,240 M (target 1,087 M, -12.3%).

| Stage (M instructions) | `compm_22000` | `rest_13` |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| HTML parse | 131 (7.1%) | 25 (2.0%) |
| Rule set build | 130 (7.1%) | 210 (16.9%) |
| First full compute | 581 (31.7%) | 103 (8.3%) |
| Restyles (2 and 13) | 825 (45.0%) | 456 (36.8%) |
| JS, layout, glue, exit | 169 (9.2%) | 450 (36.3%) |

- PR #494 and #502 facts: one build per ramp (confirmed). Build share 7.1% and 16.9% (confirmed, a little higher). The selector parse is 42% of the build on `compm_22000` (54.6 of 130 M), not 51%. The first selector parse is 3.0% of `compm_22000` and 7% of `rest_13`. It is not the lever.
- Cost of a restyle pass where every element hits the memo: 236 M on `compm_22000` (5.4 K per element) and 31.7 M on `rest_13` (5.3 K per element). About 3 K of it is string work on class names (hash, compare, split, attribute scan).
- Cost of a memo miss: 9.2 K. `compm_22000` has 77,769 misses in 3 passes (89% of the full compute). 82% of the misses end with a style that already exists. The full-style hash (1.5 K) and compare (2.0 K) are paid for nothing in those cases.
- Model: 132,006 element-passes x 5.4 K + 77,769 misses x 9.2 K = 1,429 M. Measured compute plus restyles: 1,406 M.
- Signature sharing (M3) gives 0% on both ramps: all 22,000 matched lists differ. Precise invalidation skips only about 9% of the elements (each div has 6 classes).

### Recommendation

Three parts, in this order, each measured on the whole browser: A class atoms (class and id index keyed by atom, per-element class atom slice), D selector arena with a direct parser, B cascade by winners (second memo keyed by winner values). Estimated saving on `compm_22000`: 506 M (low), 614 M (middle), 781 M (high) against 669 M needed. Only the high case reaches 10x. The middle case gives 9.6x. On `rest_13`: 221 M, 263 M, 340 M against 153 M needed: all cases reach 10x. All gains are estimates. A spike of part A must show 2.7 K or more saved per element before the rest is built. Option H (a lazy style for one element) would remove 77% of `compm_22000` but changes no journey and not `rest_13`. The owner decides.

### Criterion 8: the `cssom-objects` cap

- It protects memory, not an algorithm. `State::roots` in `browser_cssom.rs` gets every CSSOM object that the host makes and never loses one. `deleteRule`, `replaceSync` and a removed sheet leave the roots in place.
- Cost per object after PR #491: 17.8 K instructions and 750 to 960 B for a rule read; 31.4 K and 1,258 B with `.style`; 34.8 K and 839 B leaked for one `insertRule` plus `deleteRule`. A one-rule sheet edited in a loop hits the cap after about 506 K iterations at 494 MiB.
- Recommended design (D1): un-keep the objects that leave a list, prune the host tables when the heap says a handle is stale (`Heap::is_live`), and remove the cap. The JS heap limits (1 GiB, 16 M objects) stay. Tying the cap to the rule count (D2) was rejected: it fails the churn loop sooner.

### Not measured

The journeys. Wall-clock time. Whether a span of the text arena can be reused (needed for part A). Quirks-mode class matching. The Gecko lazy-resolve implementation. Layout inside `rest_13` beyond its call-tree share (about 18.5%).

Kept outside the repo: `/data/bare-tmp/r2/R2-E/` (staged example, counter patch, scripts, profiles).

## R2-C: memory of `python-docs-search-results` after PR #501 (2026-11-14)

Task R2-C of perf goal round 2. Docs only. Design: `docs/design-js-memory.md`.

Question: criterion 6 needs a peak RSS of 92.8 MiB or lower. PR #501 gave 90.3 MiB. Main gives 98.2 MiB. Where did the 8 MiB come from?

Method: 18 merge commits from #498 to `28a8fbc2`, built clean with `base-build`. Recorded corpus, virtual clock, 4 rows each (run 0 with PSS, runs 1 to 3). Machine: archMachine, shared. A second set of builds with a temporary patch (not in the repository) printed live counts. massif gave allocation sites on main. `heaptrack` is not installed. I installed no package.

Results (medians of 4 runs, MiB):

| Merge | Peak RSS | Live bytes in malloc | Cause |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| #494 | 114.1 | 104.3 to 104.9 | syntax tree of the data literal: 19.4 MiB |
| #501 | 90.3 | 79.2 to 79.6 | the literal is source text: 3.9 MiB |
| #504 | 90.2 | 78.6 to 79.5 | |
| #497 | 97.5 (+7.3) | 84.3 to 84.7 (+5.1 to +5.5) | strings over 32 units are no longer shared: 5.74 M units become 8.61 M units |
| #512 | 95.8 | 84.7 (+0.0) | object record +24 B (+2.3 MiB) against 88.7 K slot `Vec`s removed (about 2.8 MiB) |
| #515 | 97.8 | 85.2 (+0.5) | not examined |
| main | 98.2 | 84.7 | |

- PR #497 explains the growth. The page fetches equal documents several times (`whatsnew/3.14` four times). Each copy is now a new flat string. A forced collect frees 13.5 MiB of them. The collector ran once, because of the 1.75 factor and the 8 MiB minimum.
- PR #512 added no live bytes. Its slab capacity grew by 3.0 MiB and stayed untouched.
- The steps of 1 to 2 MiB after #497 have no change of live bytes behind them. Hypothesis: allocator layout. Not proven.
- Peak split on main (massif, 81.9 MiB live): DOM arena from `DOMParser` documents 22.1 (27%), JS strings 14.0 (17%), object records 12.8 (16%), atoms 8.1 (10%), array elements 7.1 (9%), dictionary properties 5.0 (6%), source copy 3.69, client bodies 3.75, other about 5.4.

Experiments on main (peak RSS, median of 5 runs; MiB):

| Setting | RSS | Instructions |
| --- | --- | --- |
| default | 97.5 | 2,487 M |
| shared equal text from `Response.text()` | 94.0 | 2,471 M |
| `M_MMAP_THRESHOLD` 256 KiB | 91.5 | 2,484 M |
| both | 85.9 | 2,469 M |
| collect when 8 MiB of flat strings arrived | 94.5 | 2,633 M |
| jemalloc by `LD_PRELOAD` | 121 to 123 | 2,468 M |

Recommendation: build Design 1 (share equal host text, and a fixed mmap threshold of 256 KiB). Expected: criterion 6 at about 86 MiB (-26% against 116). Design 2 (size-class element blocks, inline Latin-1 atoms) is the portable follow-up (about 88 MiB, arithmetic only). Design 3 (free `DOMParser` documents and strings at once) needs a cheaper collector first (one collect costs about 137 M instructions).

The threshold call is glibc only. The fixed threshold costs CPU through page faults: +0.4% to +5.7% on three journeys, +2.8% summed over 47 journeys (loaded machine). Peak RSS summed over 47 journeys: -3.9%.

Not measured: CPU on an idle machine; macOS, Windows and musl allocators; the sharing on the other 46 journeys; XHR `responseText` and `innerHTML` as duplicate sources; Designs 2 and 3 (arithmetic only); test262 and `exec_diff` (no product code changed).

Open questions for the owner are in section 11 of the design document.

## R2-A: where the heavy JS journeys spend instructions (2026-11-14, docs only)

Design: [design-heavy-js-journeys.md](design-heavy-js-journeys.md). Task R2-A of the round 2 plan. No product code changed. Machine-local files: `/data/bare-tmp/r2/a/` (counting profiler, `for-in` and regex prototypes, loop-off patch, profiles, perf data).

Method: main `28a8fbc2`, archMachine (shared), corpus `virtual`, virtual clock. Instruction totals: 3 runs each for `rust-book-search` and `nodejs-org-home` (spread 0.0%), 4 runs for `react-docs` without the loop. Subsystem split: one `perf record -e instructions:u` run per journey with frame pointers. JS-level counts: a counting profiler (patch, 3x overhead; counts and shares only).

Measured split of `rust-book-search` (16,322 M; the loop adds 0 to it):

| Subsystem | Share |
|---|---:|
| Evaluator (tree walker) | 32.3% |
| Regex engine | 25.8% |
| `for-in` key enumeration | 18.0% |
| JS builtins | 9.3% |
| Regex wrapper | 5.2% |
| GC / `JSON.parse` / parse / rest | 9.4% |

Findings:

- `rust-book-search`: 113,523 `for-in` loops examine 6,115,194 prototype keys for 340,317 own keys (all prototype keys are non-enumerable built-in names). 987,649 `RegExp.test` calls run 49,109 different (regex, input) pairs: 95.0% repeat an earlier run. 96.2% of the regex executions are `test()`. 91% of the journey is `makeTeaser` and its callees; the Porter stemmer function of `elasticlunr.js` is 52% (109,398 calls).
- `react-docs`: 16,951 M with the `settle_pictures` loop, 127 to 138 M without it. No lever outside the loop. A lazy image decode (-3.4%) was confounded by the loop and is dropped. One `compare` run gave 4,321 M with the loop off; not explained.
- `nodejs-org-home` (5,921 M, the same with and without the loop): evaluator 75%, parse 6.6%, GC 3.6%, regex compile 1.9%, `for-in` 1.6%. Flat. The register VM lane is not a lever (PR #518: -0.07%).

Prototypes on `rust-book-search` (upper bounds, no invalidation code): `for-in` without the prototype walk 16,322 M to 13,446 M (-17.6%); regex result memo 12,751 M (-21.9%); both 9,861 M (-39.6%, 1.68x against the 16,607 M baseline). Criterion 4 needs 12,774 M or less: the memo alone passes by 23 M only.

Recommendation: D1 (`for-in` stops at a prototype tail with no enumerable key; a count in the shape, or a realm epoch) and D2a (regex result table that charges the stored steps; plus a `test()` wrapper fast path). Estimate: `rust-book-search` about 9.5 to 9.9 G (1.68x to 1.74x), criterion 4 met. Criterion 2: 90.1% to about 84.0% from these two (94,796 M to 88,334 M of 105,189 M); about 79% if the R2-B estimate (-5.4 G) also holds. D2b (a lazy DFA for `test()`) is a later option, estimate only. Nothing for `react-docs` (fix the loop) or `nodejs-org-home`.

Not measured: property gets by kind, string allocations, array growth; live runs; the other 44 journeys; wall time and memory of the prototypes; `size_of::<Res<Value>>()`; the cause of the 4,321 M run; D2b (not prototyped).
Strict formatting fails on unchanged baseline files. Checking an unchanged example from the base reproduces its formatting failure. Strict clippy stops on existing type complexity in the HTML crate. A no-dependencies clippy run also reports existing diagnostics outside the changed logic. These gates are not green. The candidate bare MCP binary passes the local header-echo and protected-route check: status 200, site `same-origin`, mode `cors`, destination `empty`. The installed pre-fix browser sent none of these headers. Both checks used real page JavaScript and a local HTTP server. All owned processes and sessions stopped afterward. No load-test or performance claim is made.

## The replay driver settles pictures without running the page (2026-11-14)

Branch `t3/settle-replay-pictures`, on main `c4e32a85`. Owner decision 2026-11-14: fix the settle loop of the replay driver and measure the baseline again. Decision: `docs/decisions.md`. Machine: archMachine, `heavy` lock held. A first agent built the change and stopped on a network error. This agent applied its patch, reviewed it, and measured everything again. Files: `/data/claude-tmp/settle/` (first agent, counters), `/data/claude-tmp/settle2/` (this agent: `cmp.log`, `cmp.tsv`, `ws.log`).

### Why pictures stayed pending

The counts come from an instrumented build of main `1bb278e9` (first agent, `/data/claude-tmp/settle/all.log`, corpus `virtual`, 1 run, 48 journeys). Each call of `Session::settle_pictures` printed its ticks, its page time and the state of the picture queue at its first look. 347 calls. 273 end at once (0 ticks). 74 tick the page: 1,148 ticks and 1,539 ms of page time in all. No call reached the 5 s limit. The longest sum for one journey is 126 ms of page time (`wikipedia-article`, 9 calls, 107 ticks). Reasons at the first look of the 74 calls: 64 had a document that was not at `interactive` (the loop ticked the page until it got there), 5 had pictures queued or in flight, 5 had a document at `interactive` with nothing queued (the frame for CSS pictures, or the start of the pictures, was missing). Journeys with no ticking call are left out of the table (`nextjs-docs` too: it does not pass on replay).

| `blog-rust-lang-home` | 7 | 2 | 13 | 27 | 2 | 0 | 0 |
| `curl-se-home` | 9 | 2 | 11 | 27 | 2 | 0 | 0 |

So the hypothesis "pictures stay pending for 5 s" is wrong. The loop ends when the pictures are done. Its cost is what each tick runs: the loader, the scripts of the document, timers, idle callbacks, animation frames. In 64 of 74 calls the pictures were not even started: the loop ticked the page to the end of the load of the last document of a journey, and a live run does not do that. A picture with no reply on the tape fails at once (replay returns the error without a socket), so it never held the loop. A page that keeps asking for new pictures could: the test below does it, and the old loop ticks it about 5,000 times.

### What was built

- `Page::settle_images` (`crates/bare/src/images.rs`): look at the frame for CSS pictures, `images_step` (starts the queued pictures and gives the finished ones to their elements), and while pictures are queued or in flight move the page clock to the due time of the next reply (`vclock::next_task_due`; `nap`, with a short sleep when the clock is off). No timer, script, frame or document load runs. The `load` or `error` event of a picture waits for the next tick of the page. It ends when no picture can still arrive. The 5 s bound (`CAPTURE_WAIT`) stays as a stop for a hang. It is not a guard for a slow algorithm, and no journey reaches it.
- `Session::settle_pictures` (`crates/drive/src/run.rs`) calls it. Same call points (before each step and at the end), still only with a tape.
- Fix of a time leak: `Parsing::step` (`crates/bare/src/browser_session.rs`, the slice of the document parse) compared a deadline on the page clock with the real clock. The first agent saw `wikipedia-portal` at 160 M, 349 M, 384 M or 397 M in one binary, by machine load, before this fix. The old loop hid it because it ran every journey to the end of the load. With the page clock in the three places, `wikipedia-portal` gave 160.3 M with 0.2% spread in my run. I did not run the binary without this fix. When the clock is off, `vclock::instant()` is `Instant::now()`: nothing changes outside the benchmark.
- Test (`crates/drive/tests/replay.rs`): a page starts a timer every 1 ms, and each time asks for a new picture that has no reply on the tape. Steps: `open`, then two `expect`. Before the change (old `settle_pictures` put back, checked in this session): fails (the drive exits with 1; the page asked for pictures up to `/gone5254.png`, so its timer ran more than 5,000 times). After: passes in 0.02 s.

### Numbers

Corpus `virtual-settled`: a copy of `virtual` with the replies that the new end state asks for (5 journeys had 1 to 3 misses, mostly `POST` beacons to telemetry hosts; `journeys.sh fill --clock virtual`, 2 runs without a miss). The first agent made it. That fill sent those POSTs to the live hosts, as every earlier fill did. `virtual` is not changed. Pass `--corpus /data/bare-tmp/corpus/virtual-settled` to `journeys.sh`: the default of `--clock virtual` is still `virtual`.

Baseline: local branch `bench-base-vclock` in `/data/bare-tmp/bench-base-src`, HEAD `2ddee1da` (replay patch on `f6415364`) plus the staged virtual clock patch plus the same driver change (the three functions are identical to this branch; not committed, not pushed). New: main `c4e32a85` plus this change (the first measurement was on `5bc18d14`, before the rebase onto the textarea change of PR #500: 59,372 M and 51,595 M, the same within 0.01%). `journeys.sh compare --corpus .../virtual-settled --clock virtual --runs 3 --pss`, 47 journeys, runs interleaved; run 0 is the PSS run, runs 1 to 3 give the medians. Log: `/data/claude-tmp/settle2/cmp2.log` (`cmp.log`: the first measurement).

| Instructions, sum of medians | 59,370 M | 51,597 M | -13.1% (86.9% of the baseline) |
| CPU (user+system) | 7,489 ms | 6,698 ms | -10.6% |
| Peak RSS | 1,592 MiB | 1,418 MiB | -10.9% |

All 47 pass on both. 0 replay misses on both. The sum with the old loop was 105,217 M (baseline) and 96,345 M (main). The loop was 43.6% of the baseline and 46.4% of main. CPU and wall are from a loaded machine: CPU was 9,126 ms and 8,669 ms in my first measurement, so do not read them closely.

Determinism: the same-binary spread of the new binary (3 runs, 47 journeys) is 0.3% or less on 46 journeys. `devto-home` (67 M instructions) varies by 0.4 M: 0.2% in the first measurement, 0.6% in this one (67.4 to 67.8 M); the baseline binary varies the same way (0.4% and 0.7%). The limit of 0.5% is missed on that journey in one of two measurements. The cause is not examined (hypothesis: a worker thread that is still decoding or reading when the process ends). It is 0.0008% of the total. 0 new replay misses, 0 on both binaries.

- Test first: `cargo test --release -p bare-drive --test replay` fails on the old loop with the new test (old `settle_pictures` put back) and passes with the change (3 of 3).

- `cargo test --release --workspace --no-fail-fast` (tree on `5bc18d14`; the rebase brought a change in `browser_element*.rs` only): all pass except 7 openssl TLS tests (`bare-net --test https_openssl` 2, `bare-tls --test client_openssl` 4, `bare-tls --test tls12_openssl` 1; known on main), `a_changed_file_starts_again_from_zero` (flaky under load: passes alone), and `a_hidden_iframe_download_is_saved` (`bare-mcp --test server`; fails alone on this branch and on main `c4e32a85`, so it is not from this change).
- `tools/js/cost_matrix.sh` (main `c4e32a85` against this branch): 803 rows, mean change glibc +0.002%, jemalloc +0.000%, 0 rows over the limit under either allocator. 2 rows (`parse_load deep 1`, `deep 10`) fail to run on both trees (stack overflow, known).

## Fetch metadata request headers (2026-11-13)

Issue 475: a same-origin page fetch omitted all Fetch Metadata headers. A local echo server confirmed the installed browser sent none. The first wire-header regression failed on an empty `Sec-Fetch-Site`.

Page fetch and XHR now add browser-generated site, mode and destination metadata for trustworthy destinations. Site classification uses pinned static PSL data and preserves redirect history. Author headers cannot override it or cause an extra preflight. Loopback classification now parses numeric addresses, including the URL parser's normalized IPv6 address.

Five new tests pass. They cover wire headers, XHR, redirect history, public and private suffixes, request modes, and secure/local targets. The full bare library run reports 1417 passed, one failed and six ignored. The failure is `a_pending_meta_refresh_is_queued_work`, which requires a timer deadline within 10 ms. The original pre-fix test binary fails the same test on this host. No timer change was made.

Strict formatting fails on unchanged baseline files. Checking an unchanged example from the base reproduces its formatting failure. Strict clippy stops on existing type complexity in the HTML crate. A no-dependencies clippy run also reports existing diagnostics outside the changed logic. These gates are not green. The candidate bare MCP binary passes the local header-echo and protected-route check: status 200, site `same-origin`, mode `cors`, destination `empty`. The installed pre-fix browser sent none of these headers. Both checks used real page JavaScript and a local HTTP server. All owned processes and sessions stopped afterward. No load-test or performance claim is made.

## Criterion 8: CSSOM objects follow the collector, the `cssom-objects` cap is removed (2026-11-14)

Owner decision (2026-11-14): build design D1 of `design-style-round2.md` section 4 and remove the cap. A first agent stopped on a network error and left an unfinished patch (`/data/bare-tmp/r2/crit8/wip.patch`). I took it as a start. It had a debug stub (`if true { return; }`) in the trace function, so the trace did nothing. I removed the stub and kept the rest after tests.

### What I built

- `State::roots` (`crates/bare/src/browser_cssom.rs`) holds the prototypes and the constructors only. `keep` is not called for a rule, a list, a sheet, a declaration or a media list any more. `MAX_OBJECTS` and the `cssom-objects` error are gone. The `adoptedStyleSheets` length check stays an argument charge (`it.charge(len)`).
- `trace` (new, called from `Host::trace`) gives the collector the links of an object: a sheet reaches its list; a list its sheet, its rule and its rule objects; a rule its sheet, parent, nested list, declaration and media list; a declaration or a media list its rule.
- `roots` gives the collector the sheets that are alive by themselves: the adopted sheets, and the sheet of each element that is in a document or a shadow tree (`el.sheet === el.sheet`). The sheet of a removed `<style>` element is garbage unless a script holds it.
- `prune` (new, called from `Host::prune`) drops the host table entries (`rules`, `lists`, `sheets`, `style_rules`, `medias`, `by_node`) of an object that the collector freed. The tables never keep a stale handle.
- `insertRule` makes no rule object. The new rule is a span of its text, like a rule that no script has read. Its object is made when a script reads its index. So an insert and a delete in a loop make no object and no declaration. The text of the element is the text of the rule as written (`.new { top: 1px }`, not `.new { top: 1px; }`): the same as for every rule that no script has read. One assertion in `rule_objects_made_on_demand_keep_their_place_when_the_sheet_changes` changed for this.
- I changed no file in `crates/js`. The design said `Heap::is_live` plus a prune at the start of `roots`. The host already has `trace` and `prune` hooks (used by `browser_style`, `browser_nodelist` and others), so I used them. See `decisions.md`.

### Tests (written first; 6 fail on the old code, all pass now)

`crates/bare/src/browser_cssom_tests.rs`, 8 new tests. 5 of them fail on the old code: the loop on a `<style>` sheet, the loop on a constructed sheet (1,000,000 cycles, more than the old cap), rules read and deleted, a removed `<style>` element and a replaced constructed sheet. The changed assertion for the text of `insertRule` fails too (6 in all). The other 3 pass on both old and new code, as guards: identity and expandos of a live rule across two collections, a held deleted rule (`parentStyleSheet` is null, its `.style` and nested rules still work, a write through it does not touch the live rules), and create-collect-read with no stale entry.

### Numbers

Machine: archMachine, shared (the load varies). Instructions: `perf stat -e instructions:u`. 3 runs each. Spread is under 0.1% unless said. BASE `f6415364`. MAIN `c4e32a85` (newest main at merge time; the first set was on `5bc18d14` and gave the same numbers). NEW is this branch on top of MAIN. Pages: `/data/bare-tmp/r2/crit8/pages/` (`gen.py`), runs by `ramp.py`.

Edit loop on a constructed sheet: `sh.insertRule('.b{top:1px}', 0); sh.deleteRule(0)` 1,000,000 times.

| Page | BASE | MAIN | NEW |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `cc_1000000` (one task) | stops on `cssom-objects`, 699 MiB (at 100,000 cycles) | stops on `style-objects` at about 66,000 cycles, 79 MiB | passes, 15.0 MiB (15.0-15.4), 16.15 G (16.1 K per cycle) |
| `ccs_1000000` (a task per 1,000 cycles) | stops, 700 MiB | stops, 82.6 MiB | passes, 15.0 MiB (14.7-15.1), 17.2 G |
| `ccr_1000000` (also reads `cssRules[0].selectorText` each cycle) | not run | stops, 82 MiB | passes, 55.4 MiB (55.4-55.8), 26.85 G. It is flat: 100,000 cycles 55.6 MiB, 300,000 cycles 55.2 MiB. |

Before (design table): one insert and delete leaked 839 B and cost 34.8 K instructions. Now it leaks 0 B after a collection and costs 16.1 K.

Criterion 5, the 16 MiB sheet ramp with a `cssRules` read (`sheety_16383`, steps `run2.steps`): NEW 274.3 MiB (274.0-274.4), 5,406.1 M. MAIN 273.8 MiB, 5,406.1 M. BASE 947.6 MiB, stops. Met (300 MiB or lower), same as before the change. `sheety_8192`: NEW 145.0 MiB, 2,717.5 M. MAIN 144.9 MiB, 2,717.5 M. BASE 828 MiB, stops.

Probes (one task, so the collector cannot help; the objects are live):

| Page | MAIN | NEW |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `rd_y_sel` (selector text of all 187,852 rules) | 211.2 MiB, 7,167.6 M | 212.5 MiB, 7,204.1 M (+0.5%) |
| `rd_x_sel` (all 844,366 rules of the dense sheet) | stops on `cssom-objects`, 461 MiB | passes, 545.0 MiB, 14,039.7 M |
| `rd_y_sty`, `rd_x_sty` (`.style.length` of every rule) | stop on `style-objects` | stop on `style-objects` (same, 161 and 157 MiB) |

The +0.5% on `rd_y_sel` is the new `trace` work: the collector looks up each visited object in the CSSOM tables (about 190 instructions for each of 187,852 rules). A page with no CSSOM object pays one `OnceCell` test for each visited object.

Journeys (47 on the recorded corpus, `tools/bench/journeys.sh compare --clock virtual --runs 3 --pss`, runs interleaved, all pass, no replay miss):

| Comparison | Instructions (sum of medians) | Peak RSS (sum) | CPU ms | Largest change of one journey |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| NEW against MAIN `c4e32a85` | 95,442 M to 95,475.8 M (+0.0%) | 1,772.8 to 1,772.3 MiB (-0.0%) | 11,541 to 11,606 (+0.6%, load) | within 0.4% |
| NEW against BASE (`bench-base-vclock`) | 105,187 M to 95,470 M (-9.2%) | 2,052.6 to 1,781.5 MiB (-13.2%) | 15,087 to 14,474 (-4.1%) | not examined |

On the first set (main `5bc18d14`) `wikipedia-search` showed +3.0%. It is not the change: the runs with 2 replay misses give 7,117 M and the runs with 0 misses give 7,338 M, on both binaries, and the same-run values are equal (7,117.36 M and 7,117.34 M). The rebased run has no miss.

### Checks

- `cargo test --release -p bare --lib browser_cssom`: 16 pass.
- `cargo test --release --workspace --no-fail-fast`: all pass except the 7 openssl TLS tests that fail on main (`https_openssl` 2, `client_openssl` 4, `tls12_openssl` 1). `a_changed_file_starts_again_from_zero` failed once in the first run and passed in the second (flaky under load, as known).
- `tools/js/cost_matrix.sh` against MAIN `c4e32a85`: 803 rows, 0 rows over 0.5% under both allocators (mean +0.001% glibc). 2 rows fail to run: `parse_load deep 1` and `deep 10` (the known stack overflow, also on main).
- `keycost.sh` (`#a1`): 295.6 M per key, load and mount 613.7 M, peak RSS 31.2 and 30.8 MiB at 20 and 50 keys. MAIN gives the same 295.6 M and 613.7 M.
- `test262_check.sh` and `exec_diff.sh`: not run. No change in `crates/js`.

### Limits

`cssom-objects` is gone. `MAX_RULES` (2,097,152, the length of one list), `MAX_TEXT` (32 MiB), `style-objects` (65,536) and the JS heap limits stay. `style-objects` now counts the declaration objects that are alive, not the ones ever made, because the collector frees them. It still stops a page that reads `.style` of more than 65,536 live rules.

### What I noticed and did not change

- A `<style>` element edited in a loop stops on `dom-nodes` (the DOM arena never frees a node, and each edit writes a new text node): `el_1000000` stops after about 500,000 cycles on NEW. The sheet objects are not the cause. A constructed sheet has no text node and passes 1,000,000 cycles.
- Each `rule.style` that a script reads makes one detached element in the DOM arena for the declaration. The arena does not free it. A loop that reads `.style` each cycle (`ccst_1000000`, 1,000,000 cycles) passes, and its peak RSS grows by about 70 B for each read (66 MiB at 300,000 cycles, 116 MiB at 1,000,000). It is the same arena as above.
- `group_insert` (`insertRule` on a `@media` rule) still makes the object at once. The collector frees it, so it leaks nothing; the lazy path would save instructions only.

### Not tested

Windows and macOS. A real page that edits a sheet (only generated pages). Memory after a collection inside a long run of more than 1,000,000 cycles on a `<style>` element (the arena limit stops it first). A wall time (the machine was shared). Live logins.
## W1: a window name is answered by one walk, no list (2026-11-14)

Design: `docs/design-wikipedia-journeys.md` section 6.1, W1. The owner decided on 2026-11-14 to build W1. This is a retry: an earlier agent stopped on a network error. I applied its patch (`/data/bare-tmp/r2/w1/wip.patch`), reviewed it, and finished it.

What changed:
- `crates/bare/src/browser_frames.rs`: a miss on a window or document name runs `walk`: one walk in tree order that stops at the first answer (an iframe wins over an element that came first, as `build` does). It keeps the last answer for the name revision, so the same name asked twice walks once. The step charge is the nodes walked, not `doc.len()`. `build` stays for an index (`window[0]`), key enumeration, and the 16th different name at one name revision (`WALKS`).
- `crates/html/src/dom.rs`: `Document::may_have_name`, a hash set of every `id` and `name` value ever written (it only grows). A value that is not in it is a miss with no walk. Beyond W1 in the design; see `docs/decisions.md`. I added `Atom::NAME` (atom 2, in the table from the start) so that the check for a `name` attribute is one number compare. With a string compare per attribute, 5 rows of the cost matrix were over +0.5% under both allocators (`nodelist_load scan`, `resources_load dups`, `form_load gc`). With it, 0.
- Review: I checked every place that writes an attribute (`insert_element`, `insert_element_ns`, `import_node`, `set_attr_atom`; `clone_element` copies from the same document). All record the value. I hashed the bytes of the value in one call, and fixed the indent of one test in `dom.rs`.

Tests (written first by the earlier agent; they fail on main because `Frames::counts` does not exist, and the counter asserts no list is built): `a_missing_name_builds_no_list` (the counter: 0 builds and 0 nodes visited for a miss after each change), `a_walk_picks_the_same_node_as_the_list`, `a_name_asked_often_at_one_revision_builds_the_list_once`, `enumeration_and_an_index_still_see_the_names` (`in`, `for in`, `getOwnPropertyNames`, `frames[i]`), and `may_have_name_never_misses_a_name_that_was_set`. `bare` lib: 1462 pass; `bare-html`: 179 pass.

## R2-C build: equal response texts share one string buffer (2026-11-14)

Design: [design-js-memory.md](design-js-memory.md), section 6.1 (Design 1, first half). Owner decision (2026-11-14): build the sharing of `Response.text()` alone first and measure. The `mallopt(M_MMAP_THRESHOLD)` call is **not merged**. The owner decides on it after these numbers. A first agent stopped on a network error; its patch was reviewed, tested and finished here.

What was built:

- `Heap::shared_text(&str)` (`crates/js/src/heap.rs`): a text of more than 256 bytes is looked up in a weak table `HashMap<(hash, utf8 length), StrId>`. A hit is valid only when the slot still holds the string (`strings.get(index, gn)`) and its units equal the bytes (so a hash collision gives a new string). `collect` drops the dead entries. A shorter text is an atom as before.
- `Dom::js_text` (`crates/bare/src/browser.rs`) is `js_str` with that lookup. `consume` in `browser_fetch.rs` uses it for `text()` and for `json()`. Nothing else changed: `responseText`, `innerHTML` and `textContent` are not shared.
- A string is an immutable value, so no script can tell the difference. The table holds no root.

Tests (failing first): `equal_response_texts_share_one_string_buffer` (`browser_fetch_tests.rs`) failed with `js_str` (two more reads added 160,922 bytes, one copy is 80,002) and passes (under 8,000 bytes). Heap tests `equal_host_texts_share_one_string_and_one_buffer` and `a_shared_text_that_died_is_never_given_again`: same length and other content is another string; a dead entry is never given again; the table is empty after a collect.

Numbers (archMachine, shared and loaded; corpus `virtual`, virtual clock; `journeys.sh compare --pss`; 5 runs + 1 warm-up line each; instructions spread 0.0%):

| `python-docs-search-results` | Minstr | peak RSS MiB (median, range) | PSS MiB |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| main `5bc18d14` | 2,487.3 | 97.9 (97.5 to 98.2) | 94.6 |
| sharing only (this PR) | 2,455.3 | 93.9 (93.2 to 95.6) | 91.4 |
| sharing + `M_MMAP_THRESHOLD` 256 KiB (local patch, not merged) | 2,452.8 | 85.9 | |

- The threshold adds -8.0 MiB on top (93.9 to 85.9): criterion 6 is met with it, with 6.9 MiB margin. Local patch kept in `/data/bare-tmp/r2/text/out/mmap-local.patch` (one line in `limit_malloc_arenas`).

Instructions are equal (-0.1% to -0.4%), so the cost is page faults of fresh `mmap` blocks (hypothesis). Peak RSS: github-docs-home 94.6 to 86.9, wikipedia-article 59.5 to 54.6. ## R2-A build 1: `for-in` stops at a prototype tail with no enumerable key (2026-11-14)

Owner decision (2026-11-14): build D1, then D2a of [design-heavy-js-journeys.md](design-heavy-js-journeys.md) as two PRs, in that order. This section is PR 1 (D1). D2a follows in its own section.

What I built:

- `Heap::enum_tail_clean(p)` and `Heap::enum_tail_certify(q)` (`heap_shape.rs`). A table of 16 entries (`Heap::enum_tail`, 256 bytes, direct-mapped by the slot of the first object) holds tails that a `for-in` found to hold no enumerable string key, each with the `proto_epoch` of that moment.
- `Interp::for_in_keys` (`eval.rs`) tracks the run of objects after the receiver that have no enumerable key. The walk peeks the enumerability of shadowed keys too, so a hidden enumerable key keeps the run dirty. When the walk reaches the end of the chain, or an already certified tail, it certifies the run. A later walk stops before a certified tail. The receiver's own keys are always walked.
- Invalidation: the design said "a shape count or a realm epoch". I reused the inline cache epoch (`proto_epoch`), not a new one. `certify` flags each tail object `ic_chain`. A change of a key, an attribute (the enumerable bit too) or a prototype of a flagged object bumps the epoch (`chain_changed`: `ordinary_define`, `delete`, `set_prototype_of`, `set_integrity`, `add_lazy_prototype`). That covers `defineProperty`, `defineProperties`, `Object.assign`, assignment, `delete`, `Object.setPrototypeOf` and `__proto__`. The inline caches already need these events, so no new write path is hooked. After a bump the next loop walks the tail again (about 52 peeks) and certifies it again.
- Not covered by the epoch, so checked at each use (`tail_plain`, about 8 loads per tail object): no tail object is exotic (proxy, typed array, String wrapper, host object with named properties), none has `LAZY_ONS` or `LAZY_CHAIN` (host `on*` accessors), and none has an element or an index key. The epoch does not see element writes (`splice_dense` and the other dense paths write `elems` directly).
- Spec order and shadowing are kept: a tail is skipped only when no object of it has an enumerable string key, so nothing can be yielded from it, and its keys cannot hide a key of a closer object (those are walked first). The proxy rule (`px_for_in_has`) is unchanged.
- Steps: a skipped key does not charge a `tick`. The step charge of a `for-in` now follows the work done (own keys), not the length of the chain. No limit is removed.
- Memory: 256 bytes per heap. A certified object has `ic_chain` set; `add_data_fast` takes the general path for it, as for any prototype that an inline cache walked.

Tests (`eval_forin_tests.rs`; written first, they passed on the old code except the counter test):

- 33 programs against Node 22 (one fresh context for each): an enumerable key added to `Array.prototype` or `Object.prototype` before, between and during the loop; `defineProperty` with `enumerable` flips; `Object.assign`; `defineProperties`; an accessor; an index key on a prototype; a non-enumerable own key that hides an enumerable key; `setPrototypeOf` and `__proto__` on the receiver, a class prototype and `Array.prototype`; an immutable `Object.prototype`; a proxy as receiver and as prototype; a typed array as receiver and as prototype; a String wrapper; a key deleted and a key added during the loop; class and function prototypes; a setter that adds the key; a frozen prototype; symbol keys.
- The counter test: `Heap` stat `enum_tail_skips` counts one skip for each loop, and a loop over a dirty tail takes more than 60 more steps.
- Mutation check: with the `ic_chain` flag line removed, 8 of the programs and the counter test fail.

Numbers (archMachine, shared; corpus `virtual`, virtual clock, 3 runs, spread 0.0% on every row):

| `rust-book-search` | Instructions | Change |
|---|---:|---:|
