## R2-D build, PR 1 (design A): a lazy function inside a lazy function is skipped in the second parse (2026-11-14)

Branch `t3/retain-nested-lazy-skip-data`. Design: `docs/design-js-reparse.md` section 4, option A (PR #524). This is a retry: an earlier agent stopped on a network error; its patch (`/data/bare-tmp/r2/r2d/wip.patch`) was applied, reviewed and finished.

**Owner decision (2026-11-14):** build design A, then design S, as two PRs in order. PR 1 is design A (this section). PR 2 is design S (one pointer swap for a call across lazy script slots); it is rebased on PR 1 after PR 1 merges.

### What changed

- `LazyFn` (`ast.rs`) keeps three more fields: `end` (the byte after the `}` of the body), `strict_out` (the strict state after the body) and `inner: Option<Rc<[LazyFn]>>` (the lazy functions that the first parse found inside the body, sorted by `start`).
- `function_inner` (`parse.rs`): when it drops a body, it moves the stubs of that body (`lazies[mark.lazies..]`) into `inner` of the dropped function, instead of truncating them away. The second parse (`parse_lazy_function`) gets the table of its function in `Parser.skip`. At a lazy-eligible function that has an entry for its `start`, the parser jumps the lexer to `end` (`Lexer::seek`, as the data literals do), sets the strict state and pushes the entry as `Body::Lazy`. It does not parse the body.
- Review of the earlier patch found one fault. A function inside the parameters of a later sibling (`function g(q = function p() {...}) {...}`) is made before `g` but starts after it, so the list was out of order and the binary search could miss it (the lookup then parses the function in full: correct, slower). `inner` is now sorted when it is not (`sort_unstable_by_key`, only for an unsorted list).
- Nothing else changes: the first parse, the load step, the walk, `lazy_owner` and the limits are as before. A function that was not lazy in the first parse (a call form, `super`, `new.target`, a class body) has no entry and parses in full.

### Tests (written first)

- `parse_lazy_tests::the_second_parse_skips_the_lazy_functions_inside_the_function` failed on main (`left == right` on the node count of the second parse of `f`, which grew with the length of `g`'s body) and passes now. Checked by running the new tests with `parse.rs` and `ast.rs` reverted.
- `a_function_in_the_parameters_of_a_sibling_is_skipped_too`: fails when the sort is removed, passes with it.
- Correctness guards (they also pass on main, they must still pass): `a_skipped_function_leaves_the_parser_where_the_full_parse_leaves_it` (10 texts: a declaration then a regex, a division after a function expression, no semicolon, getters and setters, a directive in the inner body, `010` and `with` after a strict inner function, a function in a block, a label, three levels, `super`; each lazy tree is compared with the eager parse: spans, strictness, kind, name, statements), `a_skipped_function_in_a_module_and_a_getter_load_with_their_own_tables`, `a_function_three_levels_deep_runs_as_it_would_with_its_body_kept` (scopes, `arguments`, `with`, a default parameter, strictness, `Function.prototype.toString`), `error_stack_positions_in_a_function_below_a_skipped_body_are_the_source_positions`, `eval_and_super_below_a_skipped_body_give_what_the_eager_parse_gives` (eval and `super` in a class below lazy functions, each compared with the same text without padding).
- `import()` and `import.meta` (PR #521): `eval_modules_tests::a_dropped_function_of_a_module_is_still_code_of_that_module` has a lazy function nested in a lazy function and passes; so does `browser_loader_tests::a_dynamic_import_in_a_lazy_function_is_relative_to_its_module`. `lazy_owner` is unchanged: the second-parse tree still gets its own slot.
- Direct `eval` is not supported by the engine (an `eval` call is indirect), so the eval test compares lazy and eager answers and does not assert a value.

### Numbers

Machine archMachine, corpus `virtual`, `BARE_CLOCK=virtual`, `journeys.sh compare --clock virtual --runs 3 --pss` (runs interleaved), 47 journeys (`nextjs-docs` is not in the corpus), instructions are the median of 3 runs. Baseline: `f6415364` plus the replay patch plus the virtual clock (branch `bench-base-vclock`; its `wiktionary-portal` run gives 1,408.3 M, as in the earlier record). Main: `5bc18d14` (`/data/bare-tmp/base/5bc18d14f5`). Branch: this change on `5bc18d14`. The plain `f6415364` build cannot replay the corpus (it has no replay support), so it is not used.

| | baseline | main | branch | branch against main |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| Instructions, sum of medians, 47 journeys | 105,187 M | 95,232 M | 93,152 M | -2,080 M (-2.2%) |
| against the baseline (criterion 2) | 100% | 90.5% | 88.6% | |
| Peak RSS, sum of medians | 2,056 MiB | 1,780.5 MiB | 1,778.8 MiB | -0.1% |
| `wiktionary-portal` | 1,408.3 M | 1,559.9 M | 1,310.4 M | -16.0% |

I ran it a second time with `LAZY_MIN_SOURCE = 0` and `LAZY_MIN_BODY = 1` (every function body is lazy, so every test runs the skip code; temporary change, not committed): `results.txt` of both runs is identical (32,838 lines, no difference). `test262_run` runs each test through `run_script`, which uses the lazy parse.

### Limits

No limit is removed. A makes two limits weaker (design section 5): `LAZY_MIN_SOURCE` (16 KiB) protects the second parse, which is now cheap, and the `lazy_work` count in `lazy_load` counts less work. I did not try lower values.

On `5bc18d14` the `wiktionary-portal` replay costs 1,560 M and loads the logo and more scripts; on `c59e1bcf` and on `b9c89248` it costs 95.9 M and 95.4 M, 0 replay misses, `ok: true`, and the network list is shorter (the logo `Wiktionary-logo-tiles_1x.png` is not requested; the run lasts 27 ms, not 408 ms). The full compare on `c59e1bcf` gave 51,593 M for main and 50,768 M for the branch (they agree, and both are about half of the real work). I did not find the cause. Any benchmark of the journeys on a main at or after #479 is not valid until this is fixed; for that reason the journey numbers above are from `5bc18d14`.

The bytecode lane with lazy functions (it does not run lazy functions).

## H1: a restyle styles each element once (2026-11-14)

Design: [design-wikipedia-journeys.md](design-wikipedia-journeys.md) section 6.2, option H1. Owner decision (2026-11-14): build H1. This is a retry of an earlier agent that stopped on a network error; its patch was the start (`/data/bare-tmp/r2/h1/wip.patch`). It put the cover set inside the hot walk and made the `rest_*` ramps slower (below), so I moved the check out of the walk.

Cause, measured (the R2-B cause was a hypothesis): on `wikipedia-article` the one hover restyle has 292 roots, all subtree roots (`:hover`, `:active` and focus are all read with a sibling combinator somewhere in the sheets, so `Scopes` gives `Siblings`: the changed element, each ancestor that differs, and each of their later siblings, with their subtrees). The root of an ancestor contains the roots below it, nested. `RuleSet::restyle` styled 90,137 elements for one element whose style changed (9,295 after the change).

Change (`crates/css/src/cascade.rs`, `restyle_with`): before the walk, sort the roots by depth, a subtree root before a root of the same element, and drop a root that has a subtree root as an ancestor on the flat-tree path. A hash set of the kept subtree roots holds them (each root costs one walk up its ancestors, only when the set is not empty). The alternative is a visited mark in the walk: it puts a lookup in the hot per-element loop. A non-subtree root covers nothing here, because it styles its subtree only when its own style changes (the walk still decides that). A root inside `display: none` is still skipped by the walk (its ancestor has no style). Not needed: the `USES_*` bits. They only say that some rule reads the state, and the sheets here read all three, so the hover cannot skip the restyle. A finer answer (which elements a `:hover` selector reaches, like the Stylo invalidation map) is a new design: after H1 the hover still styles 9,295 elements for 1 change.

Tests (first one fails without the change: 358 elements styled against 49):

- `nested_restyle_roots_style_each_element_once`: element count of a hover restyle with an ancestor chain as roots, and style equality with a full cascade.
- `covered_roots_do_not_hide_a_root_that_a_walk_did_not_reach`: five root lists that cover each other, with and without the subtree flag.
- `a_restyle_with_nested_and_repeated_roots_equals_a_full_cascade`: 30 random trees x 20 steps, random class changes, nested and repeated roots with random flags; every restyle that does not give up equals a full cascade (more than 500 of them).

Measurements. Machine archMachine, instructions of `perf stat -e instructions:u`, virtual clock, corpus `virtual`, 3 runs, `tools/bench/journeys.sh compare --clock virtual --runs 3 --pss`. MAIN is `476c04f995` (it has the settle-loop fix, commit `bdd3d4bc`). BRANCH is this change rebased on it. All 47 journeys pass on both; no replay misses.

| Journey (M instructions, spread 0.0 to 0.3%) | MAIN | BRANCH | Change |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| `wikipedia-article` | 2,741.4 | 2,175.4 | -20.6% |
| `python-docs-tutorial` | 333.2 | 249.3 | -25.2% |
| `wikipedia-main-random` | 1,402.8 | 1,270.6 | -9.4% |
| `w3c-home-links` | 88.1 | 82.6 | -6.2% |
| `python-org-docs-link` | 1,209.5 | 1,184.7 | -2.1% |
| `rust-book-chapters` | 525.5 | 520.5 | -1.0% |
| `github-docs-home` | 4,904.1 | 4,868.5 | -0.7% |
| All 47 (sum of medians) | 51,601.1 | 50,738.5 | -1.7% |

The other 36 journeys moved by 0.0% or +0.1% (noise). Peak PSS (sum of medians) 948.8 to 925.8 MiB (-2.4%); per-journey peak RSS moved by -3% to +4% (sampled every 20 ms, so it is noisy).

Before the settle-loop fix (MAIN `c4e32a85a1`, same method, run twice on two versions of this change): `wikipedia-article` 7,788.8 to 7,037.4 M (-9.6%, the design estimate was -9.9%), `python-docs-tutorial` -23.6%, total 95,181 to 94,101 M (-1.1%). The saving is the same 0.57 G in both; it is a larger share now that the loop is gone.

Baseline `f6415364`: `wikipedia-article` 2,258.4 to 2,175.5 M (-3.7%). The other journeys are not comparable with that driver (the old driver and corpus replay differ in work; spreads up to 290%, for example `github-docs-home` 1,853.9 M against 4,868.9 M), so the per-journey table above is against MAIN only.

`rest_*` ramps (`rest_N`: N restyles of about 6,000 elements, one root each; `/data/bare-tmp/bm/b/pages`), 3 runs, MAIN against BRANCH, M instructions, spread under 0.001:

The first version (set lookups inside the walk) was slower on every ramp, about 45 instructions for each styled element, though only the root does a lookup: the walk's code changed. The pre-pass leaves the walk as it was, and the ramps are within +0.007%.

Checks: `cargo test --release --workspace --no-fail-fast`: 3,958 passed, 8 failed, all known on main: the 7 openssl TLS tests and `a_changed_file_starts_again_from_zero` (flaky under load). `a_hidden_iframe_download_is_saved` failed in a first run and passed in the second. Cost matrix against `476c04f995`: 803 rows, 0 over under both allocators (mean +0.001% glibc, +0.000% jemalloc); the only failures are `parse_load deep 1` and `deep 10` (stack overflow, also on main). `keycost` (page `typing-page-lazy-arrow`): `#a1` 295.6 M and `#f0` 301.0 M for each key, equal to main; peak RSS 31.3 MiB at 50 keys.

Limits made unneeded: none. The restyle charge (`STEPS_PER_RESTYLED_ELEMENT`) counts styled elements, so a page with nested roots pays less steps.

Not tested: shadow trees with a real hover (a page with shadow rules gives up the partial restyle before this code); `:has()` (the engine drops rules with it); sibling combinators in the random test (its roots are chosen by the test, not by `Scopes`, so a sibling rule would need sibling roots; the cover logic does not touch them); the live sites; wall time; `crates/js` gates (no change there).

Noticed, not changed: after H1 one hover on `wikipedia-article` still styles 9,295 elements for 1 changed style, because `Scopes` keeps one scope for all selectors that read `:hover`. A per-selector invalidation map would remove that. The two `*-vs-branch` journey runs with a stale `bare-drive` (built with `--examples`, which skips the binary) gave wrong numbers; the table above is from a fresh build.

## R2-A build 2: `RegExp.prototype.test` answers a repeated pair from a table (2026-11-14)

Owner decision (2026-11-14): build D1 (PR #534, merged), then D2a of [design-heavy-js-journeys.md](design-heavy-js-journeys.md). This section is PR 2 (D2a).

What I built (`eval_builtins.rs`, `regexp.rs`):

- A result table for `test()` only (`Ext::re_tab`, `ReTable`). Direct-mapped. An entry (32 bytes) holds the compiled pattern id, the start index (`from`), the string handle (index and generation), the end of the match (or no match) and the steps the engine charged.
- Key: the pattern is named by `Regex::id()`, a process-unique counter (never 0), not by its address: the address of a freed pattern can return. The string is named by its handle. A string is immutable, and a freed handle gets a new generation (`Slab::sweep` adds 1; no reuse of a generation before 2^31 frees of a slot), so one key names one answer for good. A short string is an atom (handle equal when the content is equal); a long string is a hit only when the same string object is tested again. The table holds no string: its handles are not roots.
- `Interp::re_test_raw` is `re_exec_raw` for `test`. Both now start with `re_start` (the `lastIndex` read, its coercion that can run script, and the past-the-end case), so the `lastIndex` reads and writes run on every call, hit or miss. Only the engine call is replaced: `run_test` probes the table, and on a miss runs `run_engine` and stores the answer.
- Step charge: a hit adds the stored steps to `Interp::steps`, as the engine did. A stored answer is used only when its steps fit the budget that the engine would have had (`min(regexp_steps, step limit left)`, and the budget left is not 0). Otherwise the engine runs and ends the run as before. Only an answer that the engine gave is stored, never an error. So the budget, the limit kind and the point where a loop of `test()` ends are the same as without the table.
- `exec`, `match`, `replace`, `split` and `search` do not use the table (only 3.8% of the executions on this journey are `exec`; the table has no room for capture spans). A user-defined `exec` (an own property or one on `RegExp.prototype`) is found by `user_exec` before the table, as the spec calls it from `test`. Bare has no legacy statics (`RegExp.$1`, `lastMatch`), so there is no state to keep. A global or sticky pattern: `from` is in the key, and `lastIndex` is written from the stored end.
- Memory: 0 bytes until the first `test()`. It then has 256 entries (8 KiB), and doubles when it has replaced as many entries as it holds, up to 32,768 entries (1 MiB). A new `set_builtin_limits` empties it (a stored answer holds for the limits it ran under). The size of the maximum was chosen by measurement (below).

Tests (`eval_retable_tests.rs`, written first; the Node comparison passed on the old code, the counter tests failed):

- 19 programs against Node 22: repeats, global progress, `lastIndex` set by hand and past the end, sticky, equal content in another string object, concatenated strings, an own `exec` and a prototype `exec` added and removed after hits, flags that differ, `new RegExp` with the same source, a `lastIndex` with a `valueOf` side effect, captures and `exec` after `test`, empty global matches, unicode and case folding, `replace`/`match`/`split`/`search` beside `test`, a look-behind with a back-reference, coerced inputs, 9,000 distinct pairs through table growth and replacement, and strings that die between tests.
- Counter and budget tests: the second call of a pair is a hit and charges the same steps as the miss; `exec`, `match` and `replace` make no hit; a hit that does not fit the step budget is not used and the run ends with `Limit(Steps)`; a loop of `test()` still ends at the step limit; a call that hits the regexp budget is not stored and fails each time; new limits empty the table; 200,000 distinct pairs keep the table at or below 1 MiB.

Numbers (archMachine, shared; corpus `virtual`, virtual clock, 3 runs, spread 0.0%):

| `rust-book-search` | Instructions |
|---|---:|
| baseline `f6415364` (+ replay patch + clock) | 16,606.0 M |
| main with D1 (`5be6a2ec`) | 13,442.2 M |
| D2a | 10,189.6 M (-24.2% against main, -38.6% against the baseline) |

- Criterion 4 (12,774 M or less, 1.3x): **met**, 1.63x against the baseline. D1 and D2a together: 16,606 M to 10,190 M; the design prototype of both gave 9,861 M (its table was an unbounded map).
- Table size (3 runs each, same inputs, built on D1 main): 16,384 entries 10,577 M; 32,768 entries 10,205 M; 65,536 entries 10,005 M. I took 32,768 (1 MiB): 65,536 gains 2% more for 2 MiB. Hypothesis: a reuse distance longer than the table is the cause of the missing hits; not measured. The hit count on this journey was not recorded.
- Peak RSS of the journey: 126.6 MiB (main) to 128.2 MiB (D2a), +1.3%: the table at 1 MiB. PSS sum over the 47 journeys: 1,162.7 MiB to 1,128.9 MiB (-2.9%; one run each is a sample, the spread of PSS is not measured here).
- Wall time (weak, loaded): 1,218, 1,251 and 1,283 ms for D2a against about 1,390 ms for D1 (earlier runs); the baseline 1,650 ms.
- 47 journeys against main `5be6a2ec`, `journeys.sh compare --clock virtual --runs 3 --pss`: 46,687 M to 43,428 M (-7.0%); the largest increase of any other journey is 0.1% (`react-docs`, `curl-se-home`), the largest decrease besides `rust-book-search` is `devto-home` -0.6%. - Typing (`keycost.sh`): `#a1` 285.5 M for each key, `#f0` 290.8 M, load and mount 601.6 M (D1: 285.7, 291.1, 603.2); peak RSS 31.0 MiB at 50 keys.

Gates:

- Cost matrix against main `c9ead755`: 803 rows, 0 over under both allocators, mean -0.001% (glibc). 2 rows fail to run: `parse_load deep 1` and `deep 10` (known on main).
- test262 gate ok; the per-test results file is identical to the D1 run. `exec_diff`: 79 runs, 0 differences.
- `cargo test --release --workspace --no-fail-fast` (after the rebase on `c9ead755`): `bare-js` all pass. Failures that are not mine: the 7 openssl TLS tests, `a_changed_file_starts_again_from_zero` (passes alone) and `a_hidden_iframe_download_is_saved` (a timing test: run alone 10 times it passed 1 of 10 on main and 3 of 10 on the branch).

Limits made unneeded: none. The regexp step budget (`regexp_steps`) still guards a pattern that runs for the first time. The table makes repeats cheap; it does not remove the O(n x alternatives) work of a first run (design section 5.1; D2b, a lazy DFA, is the design that would).

Not tested: a live site; a page whose `test()` inputs never repeat (it pays a probe and a store: about 30 instructions a call; the cost matrix rows with `test` show no row over the limit); long strings built again for each call (no hit: different handles); a `RegExp` subclass with its own `exec` and a table hit in the same run (the `user_exec` check runs before the table, as in the programs above); more than 4 billion compiled patterns (the id counter is 64 bits).

Noticed, not changed: `test()` still reads `regexps[&r]` and clones the `Rc` of the pattern on each call, and `user_exec` reads the `exec` property each call; that is part of the 5.2% wrapper cost of design section 2 and is not changed here. The 7 TLS tests and the 2 download tests above are not caused by this change.
## R2-C2: the peak of `python-docs-search-results` without an allocator setting (2026-11-14, docs only)

Design: [design-peak-memory.md](design-peak-memory.md). Task R2-C2 of round 2. No product code changed. Machine-local files: `/data/bare-tmp/r2/c2/` (counter patch `r2c2-counters.patch`, scripts, `out/` with every TSV, timeline and the massif output).

Owner decision (2026-11-14): do not use the glibc mmap threshold (`mallopt(M_MMAP_THRESHOLD)`). Design the peak itself. This section and the design follow it. I read it as also excluding `malloc_trim` and other `mallopt` settings, and I measured none of them.

Target: criterion 6 needs 90.7 MiB or lower (20% under 113.4 MiB, settled corpus). Main `b9c89248` gives 94.5 MiB (clean build, 5 runs: 93.6, 94.4, 94.5, 94.8, 94.9) and 2,454.0 M instructions (spread 0.01%). Corpus `virtual-settled`, virtual clock, 0 replay misses.

Findings (counting build of main with a temporary patch; the patch changes nothing when its variables are unset: 94.2 MiB, 2,454.1 M, 3 runs):

- The collector runs once. `gc_due` counts JS heap bytes only. The first collect runs at 34.45 MiB used (live after: 27.11 MiB). The next limit is 47.4 MiB. The JS heap reaches 35.86 MiB, so no second collect runs. RSS grows by 27.5 MiB after the first collect, and the JS heap by 8.7 MiB.
- One collect costs about 145 M instructions (162 M at the first one). The walk of `Interp::collect` is 72% (116.8 M of 162.3 M). The mark and sweep of `Heap::collect` is 28% (44.9 M).
- Collect more often by JS bytes (T2), 3 runs each, base 94.2 MiB and 2,454 M: every 8 MiB 94.6 MiB (+6.2%); 4 MiB 93.3 (+11.8%); 2 MiB 92.6 (+23.0%); 1 MiB 92.4 (+51.6%). Best case -1.8 MiB for +1.27 G instructions. Rejected.
- The page parses 19 `DOMParser` documents (12 different texts, 5.15 MiB of HTML, 195,344 nodes, 60 B for each node with attributes and text). Every one is dead when its handler ends: at 7 collects, 1 tree had a live wrapper (the page, 608 to 844 of up to 195,966 nodes). The arena never frees: nodes 36 B, attributes 12 B, text in one `String`.
- A suffix cut of the arena (`r2_truncate`) cut 0 nodes (the page appends nodes between the documents): 92.9 MiB. A free list for node slots with a rebuild of the text and attribute buffers (`r2_reclaim`), plus a trigger that counts native bytes of parsed documents, gives the rows below.

| Prototype (3 runs, 5 where noted) | RSS median MiB (range) | Instructions M | Change |
| --- | --- | ---: | ---: |
| main, clean build (5 runs) | 94.5 (93.6 to 94.9) | 2,454.0 | |
| reclaim + native limit 8 MiB | 89.9 (89.7 to 90.0) | 2,696.3 | +9.9% |
| reclaim + native limit 4 MiB | 82.0 (82.0 to 82.1) | 2,869.8 | +16.9% |
| reclaim + native limit 2 MiB | 79.7 (79.5 to 79.9) | 3,189.5 | +30.0% |
| reclaim + native limit 4 MiB + cheaper walk (5 runs) | **82.4 (82.2 to 82.8)** | **2,651.5** | **+8.0%** |
| reclaim + native limit 6 MiB + cheaper walk | 87.4 (87.3 to 87.8) | 2,554.2 | +4.1% |
| native limit 2 MiB, no reclaim | 92.9 (92.2 to 93.8) | 3,133.6 | +27.7% |
| native limit 4 MiB + cheaper walk, no reclaim | 93.6 (93.2 to 93.6) | 2,599.6 | +5.9% |

- The cheaper walk skips the 12 side-table probes for plain arrays. First collect: walk 116.8 M to 63.2 M. Two extra collects: -150.8 M. On 47 journeys (1 run each) only `python-docs-search` (-4.46%), `python-docs-search-results` (-2.29%) and `go-dev-home` (-0.38%) change. The sum moves by +0.03% because the prototype reads an environment variable for each object.
- Only `python-docs-search-results` calls `DOMParser` among the 48 journeys (census, 1 run each): a native-bytes trigger costs nothing elsewhere. The 48 journeys run 14 natural collects in all.
- Other items over 5% of the massif peak (78.1 MiB): the object slab 14.5 MiB, the DOM node vector 13.0 MiB (6.7 used), atoms 7.4 MiB, flat strings 7.7 MiB, array elements 7.1 MiB, the HTTP cache body of `searchindex.js` 3.75 MiB plus the `Rc<str>` copy of the same source 3.69 MiB, and 14.3 MiB of file-backed RSS (9.7 MiB of it code). Dropping the code pages gave -0.6 MiB (one drop) and -2.3 MiB (three drops) for +26 M and +71 M instructions: rejected.
- Not valid: storing no HTTP cache body fails the journey (0 of 3 pass). A collect every 256 KiB with the reclaim prototype panics (stale `NodeId`; the prototype checks wrapper liveness only).

Recommendation: R1 (free dead trees in the page arena, with a free list and a rebuild of the text and attribute buffers) with T1 (a trigger that counts native bytes, 4 MiB), plus C1 (the walk skips plain arrays). Expected 82.4 MiB (-27.3% against 113.4 MiB, 8.3 MiB under the target) and +8.0% instructions on this journey, 0 elsewhere. S1 (one buffer for the cached body and the script source) is -3.7 MiB by arithmetic. The owner reviews the design before anything is built. Open questions are in section 11 of the design.

Not tested: the native holders of a `NodeId` (parser stack, ranges, selection, observers, style and layout tables, sheet scans); CPU on an idle machine; allocators other than glibc; the 25% rule of the trigger; S1 (arithmetic); the cheaper walk with arrays as weak keys; R1 or T1 on the other 46 journeys; Gecko, Servo and Ladybird node sizes; massif ran once; workspace tests, cost matrix, test262 and `exec_diff` (no product code changed).
## R2-D build, PR 2 (design S): a call across lazy script slots swaps a few words (2026-11-14)

Branch `t3/slot-swap-one-pointer`, on `c9ead755` (PR 1 is merged, PR #535). Design: `docs/design-js-reparse.md`, option S. Owner decision of 2026-11-14 is in the PR 1 section above: A first, then S.

### What changed

- `Interp::select` (`eval_scripts.rs`) used to swap `prog` and ten per-script tables (11 fields, about 190 instructions for each call that crosses scripts). The ten tables now sit in one `Caches` struct. `Code` holds `prog` and `cc: Caches`, and `select` swaps those two, then `scripts.swap(cur, id)`.
- Design S puts all ten tables behind one pointer. I built that first (attempt 1) and it failed the cost matrix: every access to `expr_name`, `scopes` or `slots` costs one more load, and those three are read for each expression. Attempt 2 (this PR) keeps the three hot tables inline in `Caches` and puts the seven cold ones in `Caches.cold: Box<Cold>`: `pat_name`, `stmt_label`, `func_name`, `site_strs`, `prop_str`, `fflags`, `cflags`. A swap moves the inline part (3 `Vec`s and a `Box` and the `Rc`, 10 words or less) and does not touch the cold tables.
- `ClassState` no longer has `fflags` and `cflags` (they were copies of two tables that now live in `cc.cold`).
- All uses are renamed (`self.it.cc.…`). No change of behavior.

### Test (written first)

`eval_scripts_tests::a_call_across_scripts_swaps_a_few_words_not_the_tables`: `size_of::<Code>() <= 10 * size_of::<usize>()`. It failed before the change (the struct had the 10 tables inline) and passes now. The behavior tests (lazy functions across slots, `import()` and `import.meta` of a lazy function, `Error.stack`, `toString`, `eval`, `with`, `arguments`, default parameters, `super`) all pass unchanged.

### Numbers

Machine archMachine. Journeys: corpus `virtual`, `BARE_CLOCK=virtual`, `journeys.sh compare --clock virtual --runs 3 --pss`, 47 journeys, sum of medians. The base is the PR 1 head on `5bc18d14` (the journeys are broken on main since #479; see the PR 1 section), the branch is this change on the same base (`/data/bare-tmp/wt-s-vbase`).

| | PR 1 | PR 2, attempt 2 (this PR) | PR 2, attempt 1 (all ten behind a pointer) |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| Instructions, 47 journeys | 93,295 M | 92,697 M (-598 M, -0.6%) | about -535 M |
| Matrix rows over +0.5% under both allocators | | 0 | 80 |

- The design estimate was -730 M. The hybrid gets 82% of it. The rest is the cost of the three inline tables.
- Cost matrix against `c9ead755` (803 rows, limit +0.5% under both allocators): 0 over under both, mean -0.215% glibc and +0.046% jemalloc (2 rows measured by the jemalloc pass). Two rows are over under glibc only: `resources_load small 1` (+1.5% glibc, +0.2% jemalloc) and `resources_load small 10` (+1.9% glibc, -0.1% jemalloc). They pass the gate. Hypothesis: allocator layout noise, because the jemalloc counts are equal and the code on that path is the same. I did not confirm it.
- Attempt 1 (all ten behind one pointer): 80 rows over under both allocators (for example `wrapper_load strindex` +0.9%, `select_load react 1000` +0.5%), mean +0.65% jemalloc. I dropped it and built attempt 2. This is one failed attempt, not two on the same problem.
- Peak RSS and PSS (`--pss`, sum of medians): 1,577.6 against 1,581.3 MiB (+0.2%), within the noise of a single sample. Three sites, 3 runs of the drive: `wikipedia-article` 59.6 to 60.9 MiB against 59.6 to 62.8 MiB (PR 1), `go-dev-home` 58.4 to 62.4 against 58.8 to 63.8, `crates-io-home` about 20 MiB on both. No difference beyond the spread. The change does not allocate more: one `Box` for each script.
- `keycost` (`typing-page`): `#a1` 278.5 M and `#f0` 283.9 M for each key, peak RSS 31.0 MiB at 50 keys. The H1 section records 295.6 M and 301.0 M on an older main; I did not run `keycost` on `c9ead755` alone, so I do not know how much of the drop is PR 1 and how much is PR 2.

### Checks

- `cargo test --release -p bare-js`: 964 passed.
- `cargo test --release --workspace --no-fail-fast`: only the known failures (the 7 openssl TLS tests in `bare-net` and `bare-tls`).
- `TEST262=/data/claude-tmp/test262 tools/js/test262_check.sh`: exit 0, and `results.txt` is identical to the PR 1 run.
- `tools/js/exec_diff.sh`: 79 runs, modes tree, auto and byte, 0 differences.
- Journeys: all 47 pass. `wikipedia-search` shows "more replay misses than base" (0 against 2) in one compare; reruns show the same on both binaries, so it is timing noise.

### Not tested

The journeys on a main at or after #479 (broken). Live sites. Windows and macOS. Wall time (the machine was not idle). The bytecode lane across scripts (it does not run lazy functions). A page with hundreds of scripts that call each other (no corpus page has one): the swap is cheaper there, but I did not measure it.

### Noticed, not changed

- The journey benchmark is broken on main since #479 (PR 1 section).
- The design estimate of -730 M assumed no extra load on the hot tables. Moving `expr_name`, `scopes` and `slots` to the cold side would save 130 M more but costs on the pure-eval rows. A different split needs a profile of the loads, which I did not do.

## Where a journey ends: bisect of the 1,560 M drop and the load state of the settled driver (2026-11-14, docs only)

Task: research, docs only. Design: `docs/design-journey-end.md`. Main `d6837f6d`. Machine archMachine, `heavy` lock held. Scripts, patches and raw logs: `/data/bare-tmp/r2/journey-end/` (`trace.patch`: temporary counters and end-point switches on main; `trace-old.patch`: the same counters on `c4e32a85`; `jrun.py`, `parse.py`, `summ.py`, `tot.py`; `runs/`). Nothing of it is in the repository.

### Correction: the journey benchmark is not broken by PR #479

The R2-D build sections say the journey benchmark is broken on main since PR #479 (`c59e1bcf`): `wiktionary-portal` costs 1,560 M on `5bc18d14` and 95.9 M on `c59e1bcf`. The drop is real. The cause is not #479. It is PR #529 (`2612b710`, the settled driver). A bisect of the merge commits between the two, `bare-drive` release builds, `journeys.sh run --clock virtual --runs 3`, both corpora, instructions as the median of 3 runs (spread 0.2% or less), all runs pass:

| Commit | `wiktionary-portal` `virtual` / `virtual-settled`, M | `curl-se-home`, M | `go-dev-home`, M (misses on `virtual`) |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| `5bc18d14` | 1,560.1 / 1,560.0 | 146.5 / 146.5 | 3,165.5 / 3,165.5 (0) |
| `c4e32a85` (#500) | 1,560.1 / 1,560.0 | 146.4 / 146.6 | 3,165.7 / 3,165.7 (0) |
| `2612b710` (#529, settle fix) | **96.0** / 96.0 | **122.9** / 122.8 | **1,078.1** / 1,078.2 (6) |
| `df1b9001` (#530, default corpus) | 96.0 / 96.0 | 122.8 / 122.8 | 1,078.1 / 1,078.1 (6) |
| `c59e1bcf` (#479, fetch metadata) | 95.9 / 96.0 | 122.8 / 122.8 | 1,078.1 / 1,078.2 (6) |

- The step is at #529 on all three journeys. #479 changes nothing (95.9 against 96.0 M).
- The corpus does not change the instructions of a commit. It changes the misses: the new driver on `virtual` has 6 misses on `go-dev-home`, 0 on `virtual-settled`. The old driver (before #529) has 0 misses on both corpora.
- #530 only changes the default corpus in `tools/bench/journeys.py` (one line).
- The journeys did not break. They measure a different end state since #529: the page of the last step is not run to its load. R2-D compared `5bc18d14` (old driver) with `c59e1bcf` (new driver), so the 1,560 M against 95.9 M is the driver. Its other claims (the logo is not requested, 408 ms against 27 ms, fewer scripts) are the same effect: the document of the click is not loaded (below). R2-D's PR 1 and PR 2 journey numbers (93,295 M, 92,697 M) are valid on the old driver and `5bc18d14`; they are not comparable with the settled-driver totals (42,319 M now).
- The "journeys on a main at or after #479" are valid measurements with `virtual-settled`: 0 misses, 47 of 47 pass.

### Claim 2: the old loop did too much work, the new driver too little

Counters: `Page::je_state` (document generation, `ready_level`, `DOMContentLoaded` flag, `load`, `Page::pending`, script elements of the tree that did not run) is printed before and after the settle call of each step and at the end (`BARE_JE_TRACE`). One run per binary (the counts of a document do not vary). The last record of each document says how far it got when it was left.

Old driver: `c4e32a85` plus the counters, corpus `virtual`, 0 misses. A cross-check with main plus the old loop (`BARE_OLD_SETTLE`) gives the same counts, with 7 journeys that have misses on `virtual` and on `virtual-settled` (hypothesis: requests of the page code that changed after `c4e32a85`; not examined). New driver: main plus the counters, corpus `virtual-settled`, 0 misses. 47 journeys (`nextjs-docs` does not pass on replay under any driver).

| | New driver (main) | Old driver |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| Documents (navigations) | 96 | 96 |
| Left without `DOMContentLoaded` | 26 | 3 |
| Left without `load` | 37 | 6 |
| Last document not at `DOMContentLoaded` / not at `load` | 20 / 25 | 3 / 5 |
| Requests pending at the end (journeys with at least 1) | 113 (26) | 31 (10) |
| Scripts of the last documents that did not run | 217 of 381 | 29 of 382 |
| Scripts of all documents that did not run | 265 of 658 | 41 of 648 |
| Page time in the settle calls (calls with more than 0.5 ms) | 1,033 ms (39 of 346) | 1,569 ms (74 of 346) |

- The old loop never came near its 5 s limit: 1,569 ms of page time in 346 calls, 127 ms at most in one journey (`wikipedia-main-random`, `wikipedia-article`). It ran each document up to the end of its load, so its extra cost is the load of the document. That is work that a user pays. The R2 hypothesis "the old loop ran page timers for up to 5 s" is wrong.
- The new driver ends 25 of 47 journeys in an unloaded last document, for example `wiktionary-portal`: after the click the English edition has 4 requests pending (3 style sheets and `load.php`) and 0 of its 4 scripts ran (the old driver: loaded, `idle`).
- Most scripts that do not run are relative `src` (153 of the 217 sorted by host), then 31 inline scripts, then `assets.dev.to` (12), `en.wikipedia.org` (6), `analytics.python.org` (5).
- The old driver is not a fair end either: it waited for the pictures, not for `load`. 5 last documents did not reach `load` with it (`archlinux-org-home`, `craigslist-home`, `crates-io-home`, `nodejs-org-home`, `substack-home`). The 6 documents left without `load` there are these 5 and one earlier document of `nodejs-org-home`.

Switches in the temporary patch: `BARE_JE_END=load|idle` (tick the page until `load`, or until `Page::idle()`, before the final settle) and `BARE_JE_STEP=load` (the same before each step), bound `BARE_JE_BOUND_MS` (5,000 ms of page time). B adds `python-docs-search` 34, `python-docs-search-results` 15, `mdn-reference` 3, `github-docs-home` 2. A miss ends a request at once, so these journeys cost less than the real work: the sums are lower bounds for them.

## The last document of a journey runs to `load` (2026-11-14)

Branch `t3/journey-end-at-load`, on main `95bd7864`. Owner decision 2026-11-14: option A of `docs/design-journey-end.md` (decision: `docs/decisions.md`). Machine: archMachine, `heavy` lock held. Files: `/data/bare-tmp/virtual-load/` (`fill.log`, `new-requests.txt`, `cmp1.log`, `cmp1.tsv`, `summ.py`, the two `bare-drive` binaries).

### What was built

- `Session::finish` (`crates/drive/src/run.rs`) calls `Page::wait_load(END_LOAD_WAIT)` before `settle_pictures`. `wait_load` is the existing loop (tick the page until the document is in and `load` ran, or nothing is scheduled, or the limit passes). `END_LOAD_WAIT` is 5 s of page time (virtual on the benchmark clock, as the 5 s of `CAPTURE_WAIT`). It is a stop for a hang. No step changes: a step ends at its own condition. No network-idle wait.
- It is in replay and in live mode alike, because the design puts it in `finish` and the old picture wait had the tape test but this one has none. In a live run (`bare-drive` without a tape, and `bare-mcp` `close`) a page that is not loaded now runs its ticks until `load` (or until nothing is scheduled, or 5 s). A page that is loaded costs one look. I did not measure a live run.
- Test first (`crates/drive/tests/replay.rs`, `a_replay_ends_the_last_document_of_a_journey_at_its_load_event`): the last page has an `async` script that runs after `DOMContentLoaded` and before `load`, and sends a request with no reply on the tape. The step (`expect js ...`) holds at the first look. The journey must end with the script run: stderr must show `no recorded reply for GET .../beacon`. Without the change the test fails (the script is fetched and not run); with it, it passes (4 of 4 tests in the file). The log of the page and its network list are not in the report after the last step, so a replay miss is the signal.

### The corpus `virtual-load`

A copy of `virtual-settled`, then `tools/bench/journeys.sh fill --corpus /data/bare-tmp/corpus/virtual-load --clock virtual` with the new binary (the same method as `virtual-settled`: replay with `BARE_NET_FILL` until two runs in a row have no miss). 6 of 47 journeys had misses in round 1: `substack-home` 11, `crates-io-home` 14, `react-docs` 9, `craigslist-home` 2, `go-dev-home` 1, `nodejs-org-home` 1. Every journey ended with 2 runs and 0 misses. The fill made 38 live requests (one for each new file; 33 GET and 5 POST). The POST requests went to `www.google.com` (go.dev analytics collect), `nodejs.org` (`/_vercel/insights/view`), `substack.com` (`experiment_exposure`, `firehose/batch`) and `o350427.ingest.sentry.io` (an error report envelope). Hosts of the 38: `crates.io` 13, `react.dev` 9, `substack.com` 5, `substackcdn.com` 4, `www.craigslist.org` 2, and one each for `nodejs.org`, `o350427.ingest.sentry.io`, `play.rust-lang.org`, `www.google.com`, `www.googletagmanager.com`. The list with URLs is `/data/bare-tmp/virtual-load/new-requests.txt`. No file was removed. `virtual` and `virtual-settled` are not changed. `nextjs-docs` still fails to pass (not in the 47).

`tools/bench/journeys.py` now uses `virtual-load` by default for `--clock virtual`.

### The frozen baseline

The local branch `bench-base-vclock` in `/data/bare-tmp/bench-base-src` got a commit, `300b8c53` (parent `2ddee1da` = `f6415364` plus the replay patch): the virtual clock patch and the settle driver change of PR #529 (both were staged and not committed before) and the same `finish` change as here. It is local, not pushed. Built with `cargo build --release -p bare-drive`.

## 2026-11-14: criterion 3, step 1 spike: class atoms (gate failed)

Owner decision (2026-11-14): build the class-atoms spike first. Build the selector arena (step 2) and the value-keyed memo (step 3) only if the spike saves at least 2.7 K instructions for each element in the restyle pass of `compm_22000`. The spike does not. This section ends at the spike. Steps 2 and 3 are not built.

Gate: **failed**. The restyle pass of `compm_22000` saves 2.40 K instructions for each element. The gate is 2.70 K. Earlier versions: 1.97 K (class names as atoms only), 2.51 K (atoms in the generic name table, before the packed class table).

What was built (`docs/design-style-round2.md`, part A):
- `ClassId`, a number for a class name, from a packed thread-local class table (`bare_html::dom::ClassTable`: one text buffer, spans, an open-address slot array).
- An element has a sorted list of `ClassId`, made from its `class` attribute on first use and kept in a per-document cache (`ClassCache`) until `class` is written. An element with no class has no slot.
- `Simple::Class`, the class buckets of the index, the class filter hash and `Reach` use the number. `has_class(&str)` stays for JS.
- Split lists (`Big`) find a key group by a hash probe, not a binary search. It saves the 10 to 15 compares of each probe.
- Quirks mode: the matcher (`matching.rs`, `selector.rs`, `dom.rs`) has no quirks-mode case folding, before or after this change. `has_class_id` compares exact names, like `has_class` did. The test `a_class_is_an_exact_name` covers the case, the repeat and the prefix. To verify: whether another crate folds the case of a class in quirks mode.

Measurements. Machine archMachine, `perf stat -e instructions:u`, 3 runs each, spread under 0.01%, ramp pages over http, `bare-drive` built with `-p bare-drive`. MAIN is `c9ead755aa`. Baseline `f6415364`: `compm_22000` 11,664 M, `rest_13` 10,873 M.

| Ramp (M instructions) | Baseline `f6415364` | MAIN | BRANCH | BRANCH against baseline |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| `compm_22000` | 11,664 | 1,828.0 | 1,543.9 | 7.56x lower (goal 10x) |
| `rest_13` | 10,873 | 1,239.4 | 1,020.3 | 10.66x lower (goal met) |

The other ramps (earlier version of the branch; the last change touched only the empty-attribute path): `compm_*` -3% to -22% against MAIN (`compm_20000` 1,662 to 1,409 M), `rest_*` -10% to -23% (`rest_200` 12,489 to 9,581 M).

The 47 journeys, virtual clock, corpus `virtual-settled`, 3 runs (earlier version): sum of medians 45,823.8 to 45,155.3 M (-1.5%), cpu_ms -1.4%, PSS sum -1.8%. Worst: `python-docs-search-results` +2.2% (2,453.8 to 2,507.8 M; it interns many distinct class names).

Memory, `bare-stress scale css`, 2 runs each, cases of 5 MB or more (78 cases): 6 cases grow by more than 2%, all with many distinct class names: `css-escapes` 10,000,000 +11.3% (60.1 to 66.9 MB), `css-is-wide` 20000 +9.7%, 200000 +8.3%, 2000000 +5.9%, `css-class-index` 20000 +3.1%, 200000 +2.9%. Three cases shrink: `css-selector-list` 500000 -15.2%, `css-many-classes` 500000 -11.1%, `css-class-index` 2000000 -3.8%. The criterion "memory must not grow" is **not met**. Cause (hypothesis): the class table keeps one copy of each name, and the per-element list and the cache slot are new memory; a name used once costs more than before.

Cost matrix (803 rows, MAIN `c9ead755aa` against BRANCH, both allocators): **5 rows over 0.5% under both allocators**: `flex-freeze-many` 2000 and 20000 (+0.64%, +0.66%), `grid-explicit-rows` 50000 (+0.53%), `fragment_load replace 10` (+0.79%), `sheets_load dynamic 10` (+0.69%). Mean glibc -0.02%, jemalloc +0.59% on the 7 rows that moved. Callgrind of `bare-stress run block-wide 20000` (element with no class): +1.5 M of 112 M; `element_hashes` +2.4 M, the ancestor-filter add and remove closures +0.7 M. The cost is the call and the closure of `with_classes` on an element that has an attribute but no `class`. Four versions of `with_classes` were tried:

| Version | Rows over under both allocators |
| --- | ---: |
| First (cache first, then attribute scan) | 63 |
| Return at once when the element has no attribute (kept) | 5 |
| Same, plus a document flag "no list made yet" | 12 |
| Same, plus an `#[inline(never)]` miss function | more than 12 |
| Kept version, plus a `class` test in `element_hashes` | 49 |

Per the 2-attempt rule I stopped here.

Checks: `cargo test --release --workspace --no-fail-fast`: only known failures (7 openssl TLS tests; `a_changed_file_starts_again_from_zero` and `a_hidden_iframe_download_is_saved`, flaky under load). The new tests (`class_atoms_follow_the_class_attribute`, `has_class_id_equals_has_class`, `the_class_table_gives_one_number_to_a_name`, `a_class_is_an_exact_name`, `a_big_list_finds_its_groups_by_key`) pass. `keycost` (page `typing`): `#a1` 285.5 M for each key, `#f0` 290.9 M; the load of 50 keys is 14,878.6 M against 14,878.8 M on MAIN; peak RSS 30.7 MiB at 50 keys.

Where the 2.7 K did not come from: the restyle pass with all memo hits costs 5.4 K for each element on MAIN. The class work was about 3 K of it by the R2-E estimate. The spike removes 2.40 K. The rest is the memo key, the style compare and the walk, which the selector arena and the value-keyed memo (steps 2 and 3) would change.

Not tested: steps 2 and 3; wall time; the live sites; test262 and exec_diff (no change in `crates/js`); quirks-mode class matching (the engine has none in these files); the memory cases with 3 or more runs.

Noticed, not changed: a `while pgrep -f` wait loop in a background command matches its own command line and never ends.

## 2026-11-14: criterion 3, step 1: class atoms, cost fixed (PR #541)

Owner decision (2026-11-14): fix the cost of the class-atoms spike, merge it, then build step 2 (selector arena with a direct parser, R2-E option D) and step 3 (second memo keyed by the winning declaration values, option B). One PR each, in this order. This section covers step 1.

What changed since the spike:
- Only a class name that a selector uses enters the class table (`Document::class_id`, called by the selector parser). A page token that no selector uses is looked up with `class_lookup` and never inserted. A page with no class selector reads no class list.
- The table is compact: a hash byte for each slot (`tags`), a name that is 1024 bytes or more is owned in `big`, and the name ends are implied by the next start. A lookup compares the hash byte first and the name in place.
- A class lookup after a change of the class attribute is one hash probe for each token. `CLASS_COUNT` is an epoch: a document resets its list cache lazily when a later selector adds a name.
- The selector parser keeps its simple selectors in one scratch stack and gives each compound a `Vec` of its exact size. Before, each compound `Vec` had room for 4. This is where most of the memory came back.
- `has_class_id` is `#[inline(never)]`, reads a list only when one exists, and makes none. A script that asks once does not pay for a list that no style pass reads again.

Measurements. Machine archMachine, `perf stat -e instructions:u`, 3 runs each, spread under 0.02% on the ramps. `bare-drive` built with `-p bare-drive`, ramp pages over http. MAIN is `49d6475d05` for the matrix, the stress memory, the journeys and `lookup`; `95bd786440` for the ramps. Baseline `f6415364`.

| `rest_13` | 10,873 | 1,239.3 | 1,040.4 | 10.45x lower (goal met) |

The spike had 1,543.9 M and 1,020.3 M. The branch gives back 11 M and 20 M of that for the memory and the cost rows. Other ramps against MAIN (version before the last change): `compm_*` -0.4% to -13%, `rest_*` -10% to -23% (`rest_200` 12,489 to 9,757 M).

The last change (`has_class_id` makes a list only after its attribute reads number more than the nodes of the document) came from the matrix. The first version of `has_class_id` made no list at all. It cut `python-docs-search-results` from +1.3% to +0.3%, but the row `browser_load lookup 1` and `lookup 10` grew +12% and +13%, because a loop of `querySelectorAll` read the attribute of each element again and again. With the count, `lookup 1` is 92.70 M against 101.45 M on MAIN (-8.6%, 3 runs, spread under 0.001%).

## Profile of `craigslist-home`: why the last page costs 47 G (2026-11-14, docs only)

Task: research, docs only. Design: `docs/design-craigslist.md`. Main `49d6475d` (PR #542). Machine archMachine, `heavy` lock held. Scripts, patches, raw logs: `/data/bare-tmp/r2/craigslist/` (`README.txt` lists them). Nothing of it is in the repository. Symbol build: `CARGO_PROFILE_RELEASE_DEBUG=line-tables-only`, own target dirs.

Owner decision 2026-11-14: profile `craigslist-home` and write a design document before any code. This section and the design are that profile. No product code is changed.

### What I found

- The 47,008 M are not a loop, a poll or a timer. One run is 5 ticks, 8 scripts, 8 timer tasks. 45,474 M (96.7%) run inside one listener: the `load` event of the last injected `<script>`. The listener calls `cl.onStagingComplete.unlock`, which runs every staged AMD factory. The 8 scripts (parse and top-level run) are 470 M (1.0%); the timers 7 M.
- The page serves its ES5 path because `cl.oldBrowser = !window.SharedWorker || …`, and bare has no `SharedWorker`. Checked in the page: `OB=true SW=undefined`. Chrome 155 on the same page: `oldBrowser` false, `SharedWorker` is a function, 10 requests, no polyfill.
- On the ES5 path the page loads formatjs polyfills (762 KB + 129 KB), core-js (289 KB) and an ES5 `browsePostings` (1.35 MB). In the formatjs `NumberFormat` and `DateTimeFormat` modules, `shouldPolyfill("en")` answers "polyfill" in bare, so each module runs the best-fit locale matcher: 561 available locales, about 1,125 rules, 1,122 calls of the distance function in all, 38 M instructions each. Probes that fail in bare: `unit:"bit"` long gives `"1E4 bit"` (a browser: `"1E4 bits"`), `DateTimeFormat.prototype.formatRange` is absent; hypothesis (not run or not read in the code): `roundingPriority` is ignored and `supportedLocalesOf(["es"])` is empty.
- Memory: the JS heap grows 7.3 MiB per 1 G instructions, 3.15 M objects at 432 MiB, RSS 702 MiB there (about 234 B of RSS for each object). One collection runs, at the end of the task: 3.19 M objects, 433 MiB freed; 12 MiB live. `gc_due()` needs call depth 0, and `Interp::collect` refuses a call, so nothing is freed inside a 45 G call chain.

### Numbers

All with `BARE_SEED=1 BARE_CLOCK=virtual`, corpus `virtual-load` (and a copy with the modern bundle, filled live: 1 new file, 360 KB gz). `tools/bench/journeys.sh run --runs 3 --pss` (run 0 plus 3 runs; medians of runs 1 to 3), and `perf stat -e instructions:u`.

| Case | Instructions | Peak RSS | Runs, spread |
| --- | ---: | ---: | --- |
| main, `SharedWorker` absent | 47,007.9 M | 749 MiB (PSS 748 MiB, run 0) | 4 runs, 0.002% (3 more `perf stat`: 47,007.7, 47,007.5, 47,006.6 M) |
| `DateTimeFormat.prototype.formatRange` defined (temporary patch) | 23,949.7 M | 436 MiB | 2 runs |
| and the 3 `NumberFormat` probes true | 4,148.6 M | 115 MiB | 2 runs |
| `SharedWorker` defined (a stub function; page serves the modern bundle) | 2,681.9 M | 84 MiB | 4 runs, 0.0% |

Split by subsystem (`perf record -e instructions:u`, 46,997 samples on main, 13,119 on the modern path; symbol names grouped by crate and module; libc and unresolved addresses are "other"):

| Subsystem | main | modern path |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| JS interpreter | 66.6% | 49.5% |
| JS heap and object model | 19.1% | 18.0% |
| other (libc, unresolved) | 4.6% | 7.7% |
| JS builtins | 4.0% | 1.7% |
| Allocator | 3.4% | 3.3% |
| JS parse | 1.4% | 8.2% |
| JS regexp | 0.4% | 2.0% |
| Layout, style, DOM bindings, network, HTML, CSS parse, JS GC, paint | 0.6% together | 9.8% together |

Chrome 155 headless, CDP, live site, 3 runs each (`Performance.getMetrics`): the page as shipped: script 100, 103, 120 ms, task 199, 202, 323 ms, JS heap 9.2 MB, 10 requests, 502 KB. With `SharedWorker` removed before the page runs (ES5 path): script 210, 210, 213 ms, task 310 to 316 ms, 13 requests, 889 KB. Chrome needs 2.0 times the script time on the ES5 path because its native `Intl` passes the probes, so the matcher never runs. bare needs 17.5 times the instructions.

DOM: 1,278 elements at `DOMContentLoaded`, 955 at `complete` (952 on the modern path); 233 links on both; 9 script elements (6 on the modern path). Chrome: 443 elements, 152 links (hypothesis: viewport; not checked).

### Recommendation (details and the other options in the design)

1. Build `SharedWorker` as a worker that fails to start, like `Worker` (same host record, lazy accessor, `error` event). Expected: `craigslist-home` 47,008 → 2,682 M (-94.3%), peak RSS 749 → 84 MiB. Criterion 2: (119,049 − 47,008 + 2,682) / 138,272 = 54.0%. Sum of peak RSS 2,496 → about 1,831 MiB. Needs a `fill` of `virtual-load` with the modern bundle.
2. Option 2, an `Intl` that passes the formatjs probes, gives 4,149 M (55.1%) in the faked test, with the cost of locale data, plural rules and a range formatter: a separate topic.
3. GC inside a call would lower the peak of any page with one long call, not the instruction count. For the GC owner. A trigger that is checked at depth 0 cannot fire in this journey.

The gain of 1 is a change of the page that we load, not a faster engine. Without `craigslist-home` criterion 2 stays 80.0%; `react-docs` (12.6 G) and `substack-home` (11.6 G) have not moved.

### Checks

- Clean binary for all timing numbers (the `SharedWorker` hunk only; it reads one environment variable at start). The counter builds are separate and their numbers are used for shares only. The first counter build added a per-call format and read 58 G for a 47 G run; I replaced it with a counter that runs only at the factory level (14% overhead, stated in the design).
- A first fake of the `NumberFormat` probes set `format` by assignment, which a getter ignores: it changed nothing. The 23.9 G then came from `formatRange` alone. I redid it with `Object.defineProperty` (4.15 G).
- `git status` of the worktree: only the two docs files. No test run: docs only.

### Not tested

Wall time on an idle machine. The other 46 journeys with `SharedWorker` defined (and `substack-home`, which names it). A live run in bare. Windows and macOS. The 443 against 952 elements. The 749 MiB by structure (malloc and mmap totals only). `nodejs-org-home` (5.8 G) loads formatjs: not profiled.

### Noticed, not changed

- `docs/perf-goal.md` and the #542 table say 47 journeys pass; this is unchanged.
- Another site that loads formatjs will pay for the matcher while bare's `Intl` fails the probes.
## R2-C2 build: dead trees of the page arena are freed, and native bytes start a collect (2026-11-14)

Owner decision 2026-11-14: build R1, T1 and C1 of `docs/design-peak-memory.md`. S1 is not part of this task. The `dom-nodes`, `dom-text` and `dom-attrs` caps count live nodes, text and attributes. This section records that decision.

### What was built

- R1, in `crates/html/src/dom/reclaim.rs` and `crates/bare/src/browser_reclaim.rs`. `Document::reclaim` frees every tree that no node of the host's live list names. A freed slot goes on a free list, and `alloc` takes from it before it grows the arena. When the freed text and attributes are at least a fourth of the lists (and 256 KiB), `rebuild_lists` copies the live ones into new lists of exact size.
- The reclaim runs only at two safe points: after `Interp::collect` in `Browser::collect`, and after each task in `pump_inner`. No script runs and no host call is on the stack there, so no Rust local holds a `NodeId`. `Host::prune` only sets `due`.
- A walk waits until the arena grew by `max(2048, a fourth of the nodes after the last walk)`. (Changed by the lazy free below: the pace is in bytes.) Without this pace the cost matrix showed 79 rows over the limit, because every collect walked the arena.
- T1: `Interp::add_external` and `set_external_live`. `gc_due` is also true when the host added more than `max(4 MiB, a fourth of the native bytes live after the last collect)` since the last collect. The host adds the arena bytes of a parsed document (`parse_from_string`), and after a collect it says how many arena bytes are live.
- C1: a plain array (`is_array`, `exotic == 0`) skips the side-table probes in `Interp::collect` when no weak map waits for a key (`pending` is empty) and no class has private fields. No flag for weak keys is needed: `pending` holds the values of weak keys that were not reached yet, so it is empty exactly when no weak table needs the array. The test is made only when at least one object in eight is an array (`Heap::arrays_are_common`); otherwise the test costs more than it saves.
- Caps: `live_len`, `live_text_bytes` and `live_attr_slots` replace `len`, `text_bytes` and `attr_slots` in `room`, `attr_room`, the fragment limits and the namespace check.

### Why a `NodeId` needs no generation

A `NodeId` is a slot number. A freed slot can take a new node, so a stale id would read the new node. Each holder of a `NodeId` does one of three things, and the reclaim runs only where this holds:

- Root: the module has a `held` function. The tree of each node it gives stays. 17 modules have one (attr, style, cssom, controls, computed, loader, mutation, range, walker, motion, scroll, img, media, nodelist, scheduler, ui, frames).
- Weak: the module has a `forget` function. The reclaim calls it right after the walk, before any code can allocate a node. Four modules have one (computed, controls, loader, select), and the reclaim itself purges `inputs` and `dialogs`.
- Cache: the entry is stale because `Document::revision` moved and `mark_full` told the damage readers to start over. A walk that frees a node does both.

Holders outside the realm (the pictures of a page, the scripts of the loader, the refs of a driver) call `Dom::pin`, `Browser::pin` or `Page::pin`. Their trees stay for the life of the document. `drive::Refs::mint` now takes the page and pins. The JS `trace` hooks keep the wrapper of an object that names a node (attr, computed, style, dataset, platform, observers), so these nodes are in `by_node`.

Limits that remain:

- No node is freed while a custom element is defined (`ce.on`). The holders of custom elements are not listed.
- Some holders keep a dead tree until their owner is gone: mutation observer records, Range, walkers, queued tasks, and the pinned image, loader and driver items. This costs memory only, not correctness.
- The walk costs about 90 instructions for each freed node, and a reused slot costs about 26 instructions more than a push.

Test mode: `Document::set_poison` never reuses a slot and points every link of a freed node outside the arena, so a stale id panics. `BARE_RECLAIM_STRESS=1 cargo test -p bare --lib` collects and walks after each script and each task with poison. `=collect` collects only. The `bare` lib suite under `=1` has 31 failures on the PR head `b3f873c7` and 31 on the lazy free below. 28 are the `=collect` baseline (tests that read GC counters), and 3 are tests that hold a `NodeId` outside the realm or read the walk pace. This line first said "no failure beyond the 28". That was wrong.

### Caps

Each cap is still needed. It bounds the live memory of a page, and the live count is the right measure for that. The caps do not protect against a slow algorithm. The `max_nodes` of `computed` and `geometry` (they use `doc.len()`) and the work charge `it.charge(doc.len())` are unchanged: they measure work on the arena, not live memory. The cap `dom-nodes` can now be reached later, because freed nodes do not count.

### Numbers

`python-docs-search-results`, `--clock virtual`, corpus `virtual-settled`, this machine (archMachine, shared, instruction counts under load), 0 replay misses everywhere:

| Build | Peak RSS (MiB) | PSS (MiB) | Instructions (M) | Runs | Collects |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| Baseline `f6415364` | 111.3 (94.7 to 117.7) | 92.0 | 3,187 (spread 37%) | 6 | |
| Main `95bd7864` | 94.5 (93.6 to 95.2) | 86.4 | 2,453.6 (0.05%) | 6 | 1 |
| This branch | 81.6 (81.4 to 82.9) | 80.2 | 2,554.5 (0.05%) | 6 | 3 |

Criterion 6 (at most 90.7 MiB): met, 81.6 MiB. Instructions are +4.1% against main on this page. Build steps, 3 runs each, against main 94.5 MiB: R1 alone 95.4 MiB (the dead trees stay until a collect runs); R1 and T1 81.8 MiB and 2,788 M; R1, T1 and C1 82.1 MiB and 2,561 M. C1 removes 227 M of the 326 M that T1 added. The baseline varies much from run to run in this page (the old settle loop), so the baseline row is a range.

T1 limit: the design measured 6 MiB at 87.4 MiB and 2 MiB at 80.0 MiB. 4 MiB gives 81.6 to 82.1 MiB with 3 collects, so a smaller limit gains under 2 MiB and adds collects.

The 47 journeys, `tools/bench/journeys.sh compare --clock virtual --runs 3 --pss`, main against this branch: sum of instruction medians 42,317.3 against 42,325.0 M (+0.02%, max spread 0.4%); other journeys within +0.3% except `python-docs-search-results` +4.2% and `python-docs-search` -6.2%, `go-dev-home` -0.9%; PSS sum 1,059.2 against 959.1 MiB (-9.4%); cpu_ms sum 6,437 against 6,326 (-1.7%); 47 of 47 pass, no replay miss. ### Cost rule

Causes (callgrind, exact counts):

- `select_load churn`, `fragment_load`, `browser_load svg*`, `mutation`, `observer_load mo`, `range_load iter`: these rows make and drop many trees. Freeing a node costs about 90 instructions, and reusing a slot costs about 26 instructions more than a push. This is the cost of R1, not noise. `fragment_load parse 10`: the walk is +6.8 M and the reuse path +2.2 M of a 476 M row. Other costs the first builds had were removed: a hash set for the live trees (now a bit set), a stack for the free walk (now post-order, no stack), a walk at each collect (now paced by growth), the push path of `alloc` inlined (the reuse path is out of line), and a SipHash set for the pins (now `IdHash`).
- `dataset_load keys`: the same code-layout effect as in the Custom Elements PR (an inlining flip in `from_fn` closures; callgrind: +4.5 M in `FromFn::next`, -2.5 M in `call_mut`, no code of this change runs in the loop). Arjun approved this row as a layout effect on 2026-11-07.
- `navigation_load subclass`: `Interp::collect` +0.35 M of 73 M and no new work (the example makes subclasses with private fields, so the array path is off). Hypothesis: layout in the large `collect` function.

I did not find a design that frees a tree for less than one pass over its nodes. A change that would lower the rows: free a tree lazily, by chunks, when a slot is needed (the memory gain would come later). I did not build it. The owner decides whether the rows that make and drop trees are an accepted cost of R1.

## R2-C2 lazy free: dead trees wait on a list and the arena takes slots from it (2026-11-14)

Owner decision 2026-11-14: try lazy freeing of dead DOM trees, so that the free cost vanishes from the paths that make and drop trees. The PR #543 head `b3f873c7` has 11 cost rows over +0.5% under both allocators. This section records the decision and the result.

### What changed

- `Document::reclaim` no longer visits the nodes of a dead tree. It finds the roots of the dead trees (one scan of the arena, as before) and puts each on a list with one store: the root gets the parent `GONE`, and its `next` link is the list. No node of the tree is touched.
- `alloc` takes the head of the list. If that node still has children, the whole chain of children (`first_child` to `last_child`) goes in front of the list in one step. So a dead tree of N nodes costs N small steps, and each step is made by the node that needs a slot. There is no side vector: the list lives in the dead nodes.
- `drain` turns the rest of the list into free nodes. It runs at a collect when the text and attribute lists grew by `DRAIN_BYTES` (1 MiB) since the last drain, and in `Free::Now` mode (see below). `rebuild_lists` runs when the dead text and attributes are at least 256 KiB and a fourth of the lists. Dead text and attributes are counted when a node takes the slot (`retire`, `retire_attrs`) or at `drain`.
- `Free::{Wait, Collect, Now}`. The scheduler calls `reclaim(false)`: dead trees wait. `Browser::collect` calls `reclaim(true)`. A page over half of a cap (`dom-nodes`, `dom-text`, `dom-attrs`) uses `Now`: the caps count live nodes, and a tree that waits counts as live.
- Side tables (`foreign`, `class_sets`, `shadow_*`, `states`, `ui`, `images`, `sheet_made`, and the host tables) are purged when the tree is queued, with a memo of the climbs (`dead_memo`). A node that waits is never named by a table when a new node takes its slot. `scan_sheets` runs before the first root is queued, so a node that waits is never a sheet candidate. A walk that finds no dead tree does not run it.
- The pace of a walk is in bytes of nodes, text and attributes (`arena_bytes`): `FLOOR` is 1 MiB, the same as the native-byte limit of the collect trigger. A walk that finds no dead tree doubles the wait for the next one, up to 4 doublings (`MISSES`, 16 times the floor).
- C1 uses `Heap::plain_array_edges`: one lookup for the test and the edges. It replaces the separate test (`is_plain_array`) that cost about 15 instructions on rows where the side tables are cheap (`navigation_load subclass`, `observer_load mo`).
- `new_node` is `inline(always)`. Without it the inlined `alloc` made `new_node` a call, and `fragment_load` paid 8 instructions for each node.
- `BARE_RECLAIM_STRESS=1` keeps the poison and the eager `free_tree` (a stale id panics). `BARE_RECLAIM_STRESS=lazy` is new: no poison, a walk after each task, so the lazy path runs under the whole `bare` lib suite.

### Numbers

Main `4a27b7a9` (built with `base-build`: `--release --workspace --examples`, and `-p bare-stress`, `-p bare-drive`) against this branch rebased on it. Machine archMachine, shared.

| Step | Rows over +0.5% under both allocators |
| --- | ---: |
| PR head `b3f873c7` (eager free, from the section above) | 11 |
| Lazy free, first full matrix after the rebase on `4a27b7a9` | 4 (`browser_load svgparse 10`, `fragment_load deep 10`, `fragment_load parse 10`, `select_load churn 1000`) |
| `new_node` inline | 2 (`svgparse 10` +0.60%, `churn 1000` +0.78%) |
| `scan_sheets` only when a tree is found, back-off after an empty walk | 1 (`select_load churn 1000`: +0.743% glibc, +0.717% jemalloc) |

Full matrix of the last build: 803 rows, mean change glibc -0.001%. `browser_load svgparse 10` +0.31%. Failed to run: `parse_load deep 1` and `10` (stack overflow, on main too). Counts are the minimum of 3 `perf stat` runs (`tools/js/cost_matrix.sh`); the base counts are cached.

Why `select_load churn 1000` stays over. `callgrind` on the row (`diff.py` of the two profiles, self cost): `reuse` 1,125,600 for 20,010 calls (56 each), `retire_attrs` 420,000 (21 each), the reclaim walk 438,855, `IdTab::retain` and `is_free` (the purge of the host tables) 504,544, `scan_sheets` 228,240. The gain is `edges_of` against `stored_edges` (-0.72 M) and a few smaller ones. Net +2.5 M of 332 M. The row makes and drops an `<option>` with attributes 20,010 times, so every node pays the slot take. I did not find a cheaper take: it must read the old node, count its text and attributes (`retire`), and splice the children. The first brief said "26 instructions more than a push". On this row the take costs 77 (56 and 21), so that figure holds only for nodes with no attributes. This is hypothesis for the gap to a push in the base: I did not profile the base push path on this row.

`dataset_load keys` is within +0.1% now (it was +0.6% on the PR head).

`python-docs-search-results` (`tools/bench/journeys.sh compare --clock virtual --corpus virtual-settled --runs 3 --pss`, base `4a27b7a9`): peak RSS 94.4 against 81.3 MiB (-13.8%), instructions 2,453.8 against 2,545.9 M (+3.8%). Criterion 6 (at most 90.7 MiB) stays met. A pace of 4 MiB removes the row cost but gives 92 MiB there, because the walk then misses the collect that the native-byte trigger starts.

The 47 journeys, 3 runs, `--pss`: sum of instruction medians 70,462.3 against 69,844.3 M (-0.9%, max spread 0.4%); the sum falls because `substack-home` -5.2%, `python-docs-search` -6.4% and `go-dev-home` -1.3% (the same corpus as before the PR); `python-docs-search-results` is +3.8%, all others within +0.3%. PSS sum 1,413.7 against 1,282.7 MiB (-9.3%). cpu_ms -1.3%. 47 of 47 pass. Replay misses are the same on both binaries (6 journeys, same counts). `bare-stress scale html`, 108 cases: no case has a peak over 5% worse, and no case is 1.5 times slower. `keycost`: `#a1` 278.3 M, `#f0` 283.7 M, 31.2 MiB at 50 keys (main 278.5 and 283.8).

### Checks

- `cargo test --release --workspace --no-fail-fast`: the 7 known openssl TLS tests and the flaky `a_hidden_iframe_download_is_saved` fail, nothing else.
- Stress. `BARE_RECLAIM_STRESS=1`: 31 failures on the lazy branch and 31 on the PR head; the same tests except the renamed `the_walk_waits_until_enough_bytes_were_made_since_the_last_one` (was `..._nodes_...`). 28 are the `=collect` baseline. `=lazy`: 30 failures, none beyond those. `a_held_list_sees_changes_made_to_the_native_document` fails under `=1` on the PR head too: the test holds a detached node in Rust across a task.

### Result

STOPPED on one row. `select_load churn 1000` is +0.74% under both allocators. I made two tuning rounds after the first full matrix (inline `new_node`; scan and back-off). The rule says stop after two failed attempts. The branch is pushed and not merged. The owner decides: accept this row, or ask for a cheaper take for nodes with attributes.

## `SharedWorker` as a worker that fails to start (2026-11-15)

Owner decision (2026-11-14): build option 1 of `docs/design-craigslist.md`. Define `SharedWorker` the same way bare defines `Worker`: a constructor that exists, whose worker fails to start, with the same `error` event behavior. The decision is also in `docs/decisions.md`.

### What was built

- `crates/bare/src/browser_worker.rs`: a second lazy accessor `SharedWorker` on the global. It uses the host record of `Worker` (the `objs` map, the cap `MAX_WORKERS = 64` for both kinds, the `Task::Worker` error task). The constructor and URL checks of `Worker` moved into `check_url`, `start` and `check_type`, and both constructors call them. The prototype has `onerror` and a read-only `port`. It has no `postMessage` and no `terminate`. A new table `ports` (shared worker to its port) holds the roots; `prune` drops the entry with its worker. `Worker.prototype.postMessage` and `terminate` refuse a shared worker (`dedicated_of`).
- `crates/bare/src/browser_scheduler.rs`: `Dom::new_port` makes one `MessagePort` with no peer, under the same two caps as `MessageChannel`.
- Tests (`browser_worker_tests.rs`, written first and seen failing: 6 of them with `SharedWorker is not defined`): 7 new tests (the last one checks the GC), and the line that asserted `typeof SharedWorker === "undefined"` now asserts the opposite.
- It does not read `credentials` or `extraInfo`, and `port` is a getter on the prototype that reads a table, not an own slot.

### The corpus

`tools/bench/journeys.sh fill --corpus /data/bare-tmp/corpus/virtual-load --clock virtual` with the new binary: every journey ended with 2 runs in a row with 0 misses. One new file, no file removed or changed:

No other journey changed its set of requests. `substack-home` tests `SharedWorker` in Sentry's list of event targets; with the global defined its instruction count did not move against main (10,960.1 M both).
