## GC inside a long call: a design (2026-11-15, docs only)

Owner decision (2026-11-14): write a design for collecting inside a long call. Cause (#544): on the ES5 path of `craigslist-home` one `load` listener is a 45 G call chain that makes 3.15 M objects (432 MiB accounted, peak RSS 749 MiB). `gc_due()` needs depth 0, so a trigger at depth 0 cannot fire. Design: `docs/design-gc-in-call.md`. No product code changed. The temporary instrumentation and its patches are outside the repository (`/data/bare-tmp/r2/gc-in-call/`).

### Measured (archMachine, shared; instruction counts under load; `craigslist-home` ES5, `virtual-load`, main `4a27b7a9`)

- Objects at 48 MiB used: 336,800; 88% arrays (294,930); 72% of the arrays with elements have length 1 (213,295). Byte-weighted sampler (one run): `z` (`n.split("-")`) 43.6%, `E` (`__spreadArray`: `arguments`, `slice`, `concat`) 30.5%, `R` (rule scan loop) 15.9%, the `reduce` callback 3.1%, others under 6%.
- Live set with exact active roots (fork probe, one run): 3 MiB (7,391 objects) from 48 to 384 MiB of use; 9 MiB at 432 MiB. The all-environments roots gave 6 to 39 MiB, an over-approximation.
- Cost of one collect (fork probe): about 14 M instructions fixed plus about 256 per freed object (100 M at 336,800 objects, 858 M at 3.15 M). A real in-parent collect of 210,720 objects: 67.8 to 69.8 M. A 32, 16 or 8 MiB trigger adds about 0.2, 0.38 or 0.76 G (+0.4%, +0.8%, +1.6% of 47 G): arithmetic, not measured end to end.
- Bytes per object (micro cases, 500,000 objects, 3 runs, RSS): empty object 121.8 B, 1-element array 198.1 B, `concat` 314.8 B, closure 185.7 B, `arguments` 384.2 B. Slab record 117 B (104 + 8 + 4 + 1); an array adds 76 to 80 B (`Vec` minimum capacity 4). RSS is about 1.7 times the accounted bytes. Exact-fit element buffers: a 1-element array 198 to about 154 B (-22%).
- Largest growth inside one outermost call on the 47 journeys (one run each): `craigslist-home` 421 MiB, `rust-book-search` 75, `substack-home` 40, `nodejs-org-home` 14, `react-docs` 10, `nextjs-docs` 8; the others 6 or less.
- In-parent unsafe collect (trigger 32 MiB): 13 collects, 44.1 G instructions, peak RSS 152 MiB, `ok:true`, empty console, but a `Stale` remains in `ao_reduce`, so the run is cut short. **Not a valid number.** The first unrooted runs panicked (`browser_events.rs:221`) or ended at 4.0 G with `ok:true`: a missed root fails silently.
- Hot path probe of design A (unoptimized, 3 of about 25 sites, no elision), `cost_matrix.sh -a -g`, 60 rows, both allocators: mean +0.79% (glibc) and +1.06% (jemalloc); 35 rows over +0.5%; `fib` +3.1% to +3.6%.

### Recommendation

Design A: a shadow root stack, a pin counter that blocks the collect in every frame that is not audited, and a safe point through `tick()`. Five slices after a stress mode; the first gates are the cost matrix (no row over +0.5%). Expected, as hypotheses: `craigslist-home` ES5 peak RSS 749 to 80 to 100 MiB; about -130 MiB of 1,831 MiB over the 47 peaks after the `SharedWorker` stub (7%); instructions +0.4% to +1.6% on one journey. After the stub this is a robustness feature more than a benchmark lever. Exact-fit element buffers (design D) are cheaper and independent. Rejected: conservative stack scan (unsound for Rust, per-OS unsafe code), RAII handles (83 files), generational (write barrier), window pinning.

### Not measured

A clean in-parent run with all holders rooted; the cost matrix for the final form; test262 and `exec_diff` under a stress mode; the 47 journeys with in-call collects; wall time; Windows and macOS; the audit size in `crates/bare`; the `Limit::Bytes` retry; exact-fit buffers in a build.

### Noticed, not changed

- The design touches the GC trigger and `Host::prune` of the DOM-arena work (a collect in a call can free a tree under a binding that holds its `NodeId`). It needs the old corpus for `craigslist-home` after the `SharedWorker` stub. It does not touch class atoms.

## Gmail: bare against Chrome (2026-11-15)

Goal: compare one Gmail inbox tab in bare and in Chrome, on archMachine. Measure only. No product code changed. The account is the one bare has a saved session for. The same account is the live account `u/0` of the `chrome-auto` profile. No cookies were copied between the browsers. No account detail is in this document.

Setup.
- bare: release build of `c4848ecc` (`bare-mcp`, own target dir). One new `bare-mcp` process and one new page per run. `open` with the saved session, URL `mail.google.com/mail/u/0/#inbox`, 1280x800, no cache. No login step ran.
- Chrome: 155.0.8059.39, headless, `chrome-auto` profile, CDP. One new tab per run, closed after the run. Before each run, the service workers were stopped and the extra renderers were left to exit, so no renderer was reused (Gmail's Meet worker kept one alive in the first attempt; that attempt was dropped). Main table: 1280x800, HTTP cache on.
- Ready: the first `tr.zA` row exists in the DOM (50 rows in every run). Polled every 100 ms in Chrome.
- Window: from navigation start to ready plus 30 s idle.
- CPU: user plus system, from `/proc/<pid>/stat`, sampled every 0.5 s. bare: the `bare-mcp` process. Chrome: the browser, GPU and network service processes, and every renderer that did not exist before the runs (7 per run, one of them Chrome's spare renderer).
- Instructions (`instructions:u`): bare, `perf stat` on `bare-mcp` (all threads). Chrome, `perf stat -a -G` on the whole `chrome-auto.service` cgroup, minus the idle rate of the first 2.5 s. Interval 0.5 s; the edges of the window are prorated.
- Memory: `smaps_rollup` Rss and Pss. Chrome: the 7 new renderers, plus the browser, GPU and network service processes shown apart.
- Requests: Chrome, CDP `Network` events of the tab and its frames and workers. bare, the `network` tool.
- Machine: archMachine, 16 cores. n = 3 per column. Format: median [min to max].

| | Chrome (1280x800, cache on) | bare, idle machine | bare, loaded machine |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| Load average at start | 3.8, 3.2, 2.3 | 1.3, 1.2, 2.7 | 12.2, 5.6, 8.0 |
| First list row | 1.2 s [1.1 to 1.2] | about 9 s (see below) | not measured |
| `open` returns (bare's own settle) | no equal event | 23.3 s [19.9 to 24.0] | 33.3 s [32.5 to 39.5] |
| CPU time, start to ready | 3.0 s [2.9 to 3.1] | 16.0 s [15.9 to 16.1] (to `open` return) | 27.9 s [27.2 to 34.1] |
| CPU time, start to ready + 30 s | 11.7 s [11.7 to 13.1] | 18.3 s [18.0 to 18.4] | 29.8 s [29.3 to 37.4] |
| `instructions:u`, start to ready | 14.5 G [14.4 to 15.4] | 120.5 G [120.3 to 122.8] | 142.2 G [138.9 to 145.2] |
| `instructions:u`, start to ready + 30 s | 57.7 G [57.3 to 60.8] | 133.9 G [133.1 to 135.0] | 152.4 G [149.3 to 155.7] |
| PSS at ready | 412 MiB [409 to 429] renderers, +52 MiB others | 470 MiB [460 to 478] | 480 MiB [466 to 483] |
| PSS at ready + 30 s | 660 MiB [658 to 664] renderers, +51 MiB others | 470 MiB [462 to 481] | 486 MiB [474 to 489] |
| Peak | 811 MiB PSS [808 to 813] renderers (sampled every 2 s); RSS sum 1,428 MiB (shared pages counted twice) | 472 MiB RSS [472 to 495] (`VmHWM`) | 492 MiB RSS [477 to 494] |
| Requests (http and https) | 490 [489 to 495] | 176 [176 to 178] | 186 [183 to 187] |
| Bytes | 2.8 MB [2.0 to 3.2] on the wire | 6.3 MB (bare's body size) | 6.5 MB (bare's body size) |

Other Chrome runs, n = 3 each, within the same spread: default headless viewport (about 800x480), instructions 13.5 G to ready [13.5 to 16.2] and 61.5 G at ready + 30 s; cache disabled, 13.6 G [11.0 to 13.7] and 61.1 G, 8.5 MB on the wire, 522 requests. Ready took 1.3 to 2.5 s in these runs (loads 5.6 to 15).

Reading.
- To ready, bare runs about 8.3 times the instructions of Chrome (120.5 G against 14.5 G). Over ready + 30 s the ratio is 2.3 (133.9 G against 57.7 G), because Chrome keeps working after the first row: it adds about 43 G in the next 30 s, and bare adds about 13 G.
- Chrome never went quiet. In every Chrome run, CPU stayed above 0.15 s per 3 s until the end of the window. bare's page was quiet by its own rule when `open` returned. The two "quiet" points are not the same event, so they are not compared.
- Memory: at ready, bare's PSS (470 MiB) is close to Chrome's total (412 + 52 MiB). After 30 s, Chrome grows to about 711 MiB and bare stays at 470 MiB.
- The first row in bare comes before `open` returns. On a machine with load 3 to 9, `open` with a 9.5 s limit already had 50 rows when it returned. With limits of 5, 6.5 and 8 s, the next `eval` call (the call itself runs the page) took 2 to 6 s before it showed 50 rows. So the first row comes at about 8 to 10 s (n = 1 per limit, plus or minus 1 s). The 23 s is the time until bare calls the page settled.
- bare instructions rise with load: 120.5 G idle, 142.2 G loaded, for the same page. Hypothesis: time-driven work (timers, polling) runs more when the page stays longer. Not checked.

Does the inbox work the same? No. In bare the inbox opens with 50 rows, the unread count (115) and "1-50 of 523", the same as Chrome. A visual check (screenshots, deleted after the check because they show mail) found these differences:
- The icon font does not paint: no icons in the left rail, no Compose pencil, no row checkboxes, stars or importance markers, no icons in the right app column.
- The row columns are squeezed: sender, subject and date are cut off or overlap. The category tabs are cut off.
- The right side panel stays on "Loading..." (Chrome shows the Calendar panel there).
- Requests fail with "connection refused": `ogads-pa.clients6.google.com` (3 in all) and `mail-ads.google.com`. One request to `mail.google.com` (`act=oetsha`) gets HTTP 403. `diagnose` says "site problem". Hypothesis: the first two are ad hosts that this machine's DNS blocks (both resolve to `::`). Chrome was not checked for the same failures.

Caveats.
- Chrome is cold for the page only. The browser, GPU and network processes are warm, and the HTTP cache is warm in the main column (the cache-disabled runs are given above). bare starts a new process with an empty cache each run. bare restores the session from a file; Chrome uses its live profile.
- The two browsers do not do the same work. Chrome loads more (about 490 requests against about 180) and runs side panels and the Meet service worker that bare does not show. Bytes are not comparable: Chrome's value is the wire size, bare's is the body size it reports.
- Chrome instructions are for the whole `chrome-auto` cgroup, so other idle tabs add a little. The idle baseline of the first 2.5 s is subtracted (0.06 to 1.4 M instructions per second, small). The 0.5 s intervals and a start delay of `perf` (about 0.1 to 0.3 s) give an error of a few percent on the "to ready" value.
- The window to "ready + 30 s" lasts 31 s in Chrome and about 53 s in bare, because bare reaches ready later.
- `instructions:u` counts user mode only. CPU time includes the kernel.
- bare's "ready" is `open` returning with rows present, so it is an upper bound for the first row.
- A first Chrome attempt reused a renderer that Gmail's Meet worker kept alive. It was dropped, and the cleanup step was added. The Meet worker was stopped with `ServiceWorker.stopAllWorkers`. I cleared no cookies or storage.

Not tested: opening a message, scrolling, search, compose, a second account, a Chrome run with the same empty cache as bare, and bare on a symbol build (no hot-function split).

Scripts and raw output: `/data/bare-tmp/gmail-compare/` (`chrome-run.mjs`, `bare-run.py`, `clean.mjs`, `analyze.py`, `raw/`). They are not in the repository.

## 2026-11-15: criterion 3, design H built: `getComputedStyle` styles the way down to the element

### Owner decision (2026-11-15)

Build design H of `docs/design-compm-10x.md`, slices H1 to H3. One PR for the three slices: H1 alone changes no behavior and H3 is the numbers of H2. Decision text: `docs/decisions.md`.

### What was built

- `RuleSet::style_chain` and `StyleChain` (`crates/css/src/cascade.rs`): the styles of the elements from the root element down to the element asked about, in a `Styles` that is `partial`. The ancestor filter stays open on the path of the last read, so the next element in document order costs one style and no filter work for its ancestors. The `kept_cx`/`put_back` pair now moves `Sets` with no allocation (`Sets::moved_out`, `into_inner`): it cost 2.5 k instructions for each chain read.
- `cascade_inner` (`browser_computed.rs`) takes the chain when `built.last[0]` is empty (no cascade of the whole document is kept), the rule set has no motion, and the style of the element has none. A value that layout may decide is read from the chain first; if `layout_wanted` says it needs the box, the read takes the whole cascade as before (`Snap::partial`). `length` and `item` use the chain too.
- Not used for: a document with a shadow root, a rule set with `transition-*`, `animation-*` or `@keyframes`, an element with such a style, a page that has a kept cascade (it lays out: the old restyle path stays). The limits `computed-work` and `computed-nodes` still run first, so `compm_24000` and larger are still refused. Chain reads make them unneeded; lifting them is a separate decision.

### Tests (written first)

`crates/bare/src/browser_computed_chain_tests.rs`, 10 tests. The oracle is a second browser that read layout first, so it answers from the full cascade. Every element and every property that needs no layout (about 110 properties and the custom properties) is compared in document order, reverse order and a mixed order, on a page with inheritance, `em`, `rem`, `currentColor`, custom properties with `var()` and `calc()`, `:nth-child`, `+`, `~`, `>`, descendant, `:checked`, `:empty`, `:first-child`, `:last-child`, an inline style, a `display: none` subtree and the `hidden` attribute. The same after each of: a class change on an ancestor, a class and an attribute change on a sibling, a checkbox, an added and a removed node, a text edit, an inline style write, a new `<style>`, a changed `<style>` text, the root font size, and a subtree hidden and shown. Also: reads and writes in one script, hidden elements, a layout read after a style read (`getBoundingClientRect`, `offsetHeight`, `width`, `height`, `padding`, `margin`: same values as the oracle, one full cascade), fixed-length shorthands on the chain, a detached element, a page with a shadow tree, and pages with motion. Each test asserts that the lazy browser made no full cascade and that the chain ran. I broke the invalidation on purpose (kept a stale chain): 2 tests failed. `:has()` is not supported by the engine (`selector.rs`), so it has no case.
Five tests of `browser_computed_tests.rs` counted the full cascade of a first style read (`computes == 1`). The counts changed on purpose: three now start with a read of `width`, which keeps the cascade of the page (the machinery they test), two expect `(computes, chains) == (0, 1)`, and one reads `width` after to reach the full cascade.

Rules with motion and elements with a motion style take the whole cascade, so only this inline case is open.

## Exact-fit array element buffers (2026-11-15)

Owner decision (2026-11-15): build exact-fit array element buffers (option D of `docs/design-gc-in-call.md`, PR #547) and park the GC-in-call build (option A); the design stays in `docs/`. Decision record: `docs/decisions.md`.

### What was built

- `crates/js/src/heap.rs`: `alloc_object_cap` (the old `alloc_object` calls it with 0), `Heap::new_array_cap`, `Heap::new_object_cap`, `Heap::reserve_elems`, and `ELEMS_RESERVE_MAX = 4096`. The accounted bytes follow `elems.len()`, so a reservation changes no limit and no `heap_bytes`.
- Callers: `new_array_from_proto` (literals through `Array(...)`, `split`, rest parameters, `Array.of`-style helpers), `eval_array` (the literal list length, and a spread of an array adds its length), the `arguments` object, the regexp `exec` result, `ao_new_array(len)` (so `slice`, `map`, `Array.from` of an array-like and `splice` results), `concat` (a hint: the sum of the array lengths, 1 for the rest) and `Array.from` of an iterable array.
- Not exact (the size is not known when the array is made): `filter`, `JSON.parse`, results that grow by `push`. They keep the normal growth.
- Tests, written first (`crates/js/src/eval_exact_fit_tests.rs`): the capacity tests failed before (48,384 spare bytes for 1000 one-element arrays), the behaviour tests (length, holes, push after an exact-fit array, sort, splice, `length` set larger and smaller, big lengths) held before and after. `cargo test --release -p bare-js`: 979 pass.
- The 117 B slab record: no field can go without a new layout. The 104 B `Object` has `proto`, `shape`, the flags (in padding), the `elems` header (24 B), `repr` (48 B for the three inline values, an array uses one), `n` and `dict`. The unused part of an array is two inline slots (32 B). Removing it is design 2a of `docs/design-js-memory.md` (a different array layout), not a small safe change. Not done.

### Numbers (archMachine, shared; base = main `2889fa06`, new = this branch; 3 runs, medians)

- Micro cases, 500,000 garbage objects, RSS per object (`wait4` peak minus the empty page, spread under 0.5%): 1-element literal 197.1 to 149.3 B (-24%); 3-element literal 197.1 to 181.3 B; `split` of one piece 197.3 to 149.6 B; `slice` 196.6 to 149.2 B; `[...a]` 197.1 to 149.5 B; `concat` 314.2 to 266.4 B; call with `arguments` 384.0 to 336.5 B; `map` of one element 384.0 to 336.3 B; ES5 `__spreadArray` helper 511.4 to 416.0 B (-19%). - `craigslist-home` ES5 path: `virtual-load` (which now holds the modern bundle too) with both binaries built with `SharedWorker` hidden (a temporary one-line patch to `browser_worker.rs`, not committed; the binary of main also has it). 47,009.1 to 46,826.5 M instructions (-0.4%), peak RSS 749.6 to 624.9 MiB (-16.6%), PSS 746.7 to 620.0 MiB, spread 0.0%, 0 replay misses. (`virtual-settled` and `virtual-load.bak-pre-sw` with normal binaries do not take the ES5 path: 43 M and 3,750 M.)
- 47 journeys (`journeys.sh compare --clock virtual --runs 3 --pss`, `virtual-load`): all pass, 0 misses. Instructions 73,245.5 to 73,179.0 M (-0.1%, max spread 0.4%). Peak RSS sum 1,796.9 to 1,781.2 MiB (-0.9%), PSS sum 1,508.6 to 1,374.2 MiB (-8.9%, one sampled run). Largest: `substack-home` 188.9 to 180.9 MiB (-4.2%), `rust-book-search` 127.5 to 124.2 (-2.6%), `wikipedia-search` 57.0 to 55.3 (-2.9%).

No row up by more than noise: the largest rises (`arrobj_load queue 100` +2.6%, `sort 10` +2.4%) have equal live bytes and are allocator wobble of 5 to 8 MiB runs.

## 2026-11-15: the `computed-work` limit counts the path of a chain read, not the page

### Owner decision (2026-11-15)

Design the removal of the `computed-work` limit, now that a `getComputedStyle` read that needs no layout styles only the root-to-element path (design H, #551).

### Plan (written before the code)

Where it is counted: `cascade_inner` (`browser_computed.rs`) computed `nodes x (rules + 1)` (or `styled elements x (rules + 1)` over `STYLED_FROM`, one tree walk for each document revision) before everything else, and refused over `max_work` (2^30). It ran before the cache hit, the chain and the restyle.

What it protects: one native operation that cannot be interrupted. `RuleSet::compute` and `RuleSet::restyle` run to the end, and the steps are charged for the candidates they tested after the work.

Path by path (N nodes, E elements, R rules, d depth of the element, c candidates that the rule index gives for an element):

| Path | Work now | Needs the limit? |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Cache hit (`built.last` is current) | O(1), charges 1 | No. It ran the cap check first; that was wasted. |
| Chain read (`style_chain`) | O(d x c) for a new path; O(c) for the next element in document order (the filter stays open); worst case d x R | Only as d x (R + 1). The page size N does not matter. |
| Restyle of a kept cascade | O(elements that the marks reach x c) | Yes, as before (a restyle cannot be interrupted). |
| Full compute: a layout read, `keep`, `want`, a page with shadow roots, motion, an element with a motion style | O(E x c), worst case E x R (rules that no index key holds) | Yes, as before. |
| Read-all loop | one chain read for each element: O(E x c) in all, plus O(d) filter work for each | Steps bound it. No limit needed per read. |

Change:
1. The cap check moves behind the cache hit and the chain, so a hit and a chain read no longer pay for it (and no longer walk the tree for `styled_work` after each change).
2. A chain read has its own bound: the number of elements on the path times (rules + 1), against `max_work`. The cheap test (nodes x (rules + 1)) comes first, so a page that is under the limit pays nothing and does not walk up. Only over it, the read walks up from the element (charged `d / 8 + 1` steps) and compares `d x (rules + 1)`.
3. The full compute and the restyle keep the old bound. They are still E x c work in one uninterruptible call. A cap by real work needs a candidate count inside `RuleSet::compute` (`sources_capped` in `cascade.rs`); that is a change of the hot cascade loop, larger than this limit, so it is not part of this PR.
4. `computed-nodes` (2^17 nodes, one `u32` for each node in the chain's `of_node` table) stays. `compm_43000` (129,000 nodes) is the largest page of the ramp that it lets through.

### What was built

- `cascade_inner` (`browser_computed.rs`): the `computed-work` check moved from the top of the function to the place where the whole cascade starts (a restyle or a full compute), behind the cache hit and the chain read. A hit and a chain read no longer pay for it, and no longer walk the tree for `styled_work` after each document change.
- A chain read has its own bound: if `nodes x (rules + 1)` is over `max_work`, the read walks up from the element (charged `depth / 8 + 1` steps) and compares `depth x (rules + 1)` with `max_work`. A page that is under the limit pays nothing. A path that is too long for the rule count (200 nested elements and 1,000 rules against a limit of 100,000) is still refused before any style is made.
- Unchanged: the bound of the full compute and the restyle, `computed-nodes`, and the step charge.

### Tests (written first; the three new tests failed on main)

`browser_computed_chain_tests.rs`:
- `a_chain_read_runs_over_the_default_work_limit_and_reads_the_right_value`: pages of 24,000 divs and rules, 40,000 and 43,000 divs (129,000 nodes, just under `computed-nodes`); three chain reads each, `(computes, chains) == (0, 3)`.
- `the_work_limit_of_a_chain_read_counts_the_path`: a short path reads, a deep path is refused with `computed-work` and styles nothing.
- `a_layout_read_loop_and_a_read_all_loop_stay_bounded`: a layout read (`offsetWidth`) on a page over the limit is still refused; a read of every element runs as chain reads with no full cascade; with a small step budget the read-all loop ends with `Limit(Steps)`.
`browser_computed_tests.rs`: `work_bound_counts_styled_elements_not_text_nodes` now asks for the refusal with a layout read (`offsetWidth`); a style read of one element is no longer refused there.

### Numbers (instructions:u, `bare-drive`, 3 runs each, spread at most 0.03%)

Machine archMachine (loaded). MAIN `2889fa06` (the base of the branch), NEW the branch before the rebase. Pages: the `compm_N` shape of the earlier rounds, regenerated for 40,000 and 43,000 in `/data/claude-tmp/cwpages/` (not in the repository). "refused" means exit 1 with `Limit(Host("computed-work"))`; its count is the load and the parse up to the refusal.

| Page | MAIN M | NEW M | Peak RSS MiB MAIN / NEW |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `compm_22000` | 400.1 | 391.2 (-2.2%) | 33.4 / 33.3 |
| `compm_24000` | refused (421.7) | 429.9 | 31.3 / 33.0 |
| `compm_30000` | refused (524.4) | 534.4 | 38.3 / 40.1 |
| `compm_34000` | refused (591.5) | 602.7 | 42.8 / 44.2 |
| `compm_40000` | refused (691.9) | 705.0 | 42.1 / 45.0 |
| `compm_43000` | refused (742.2) | 756.2 | 48.3 / 50.9 |
| `rest_13` | 1,042.5 | 1,042.5 | 46.2 / 46.1 |
| read-all, document order | 1,511.6 | 1,509.8 (-0.1%) | 69.5 / 69.4 |
| read-all, reverse order | 1,479.9 | 1,478.1 | 69.5 / 69.5 |

The cost grows linearly from `compm_22000` to `compm_43000`: 391 M, 430 M, 534 M, 603 M, 705 M, 756 M (about 17.5 K instructions for each div). `compm_22000` is 2.2% cheaper because the tree walk of `styled_work` is gone.

47 journeys (`tools/bench/journeys.sh compare --clock virtual --runs 3 --pss`, corpus `virtual-load`, `nextjs-docs` skipped): 47 pass on both, no replay miss, sum of medians 73,245.4 M (MAIN) against 73,243.4 M (-0.0%), no journey over +0.1%, spread at most 0.3%. cpu_ms -0.1%. PSS +0.1% by the sum of the medians (one run each, noise; `crates-io-home` +10.4% and `devto-home` +5.0% have no change in instructions). The journeys lay out first, so they keep a cascade and never reach the chain path.

### Gates (after the rebase on main `294f1c01`, which has #554)

- `cargo test --release --workspace --no-fail-fast`: 4,060 passed, 9 failed: the 7 openssl TLS tests, and `a_hidden_iframe_download_is_saved` and `a_changed_file_starts_again_from_zero` (the known flaky ones: the second passed alone, the first passed 1 of 4 alone, with "0 bytes" running).
- Cost matrix against `294f1c01` (805 rows, 803 measured, glibc, jemalloc for rows over the limit): mean glibc +0.001%, 0 rows over +0.5% under one allocator, 0 under both. `parse_load deep 1` and `deep 10` fail to run (the known stack overflow).
- test262: exit 0 (no regression; the "newly passing" lines are from a checkout that is newer than the baseline). `exec_diff.sh`: 79 runs, 0 differences. No file of `crates/js` changed.
- `keycost.sh`: 278.3 M for each key (`#a1`), 283.6 M (`#f0`), load and mount 591.1 M, RSS 30.8 MiB at 50 keys; equal on main and branch.

### Limits that this change makes unneeded, and the ones that stay

- Unneeded: `computed-work` for a chain read, as `nodes x rules`. It is now `path length x rules`, which a page of any size does not reach. It is also no longer checked on a cache hit.
- Stays: `computed-work` for a full compute and a restyle (a layout read, a page with a shadow root or motion, `getComputedStyle` with a value that needs a box). That path is still elements x candidates in one call that cannot be interrupted, and a page of rules that no index key holds (`*:not(.zN)`) is elements x rules. A bound by the real count of candidates needs a counter inside `RuleSet::compute` (`sources_capped` in `cascade.rs`). It is a change of the hot loop, so I did not do it here. With it, the full compute of `compm_34000` (3 G) would no longer be refused by the model.
- Stays, and is now the limit that stops the ramp: `computed-nodes` (2^17 nodes). `compm_44000` and larger (more than 131,072 nodes) are refused by it. The chain makes one `u32` for each node (`of_node`), so its memory bound is 512 KiB at the limit; lifting it for the chain is a separate decision.

### Not tested

- Wall time on an idle machine. Journeys after the rebase on #554 (they were run on the branch before the rebase; the rebase brought array-buffer changes only, which the cost matrix and the workspace tests cover). Pages over 131,072 nodes. A deep path with a real page (the deep-path refusal is tested with 200 nested divs and a low limit).
- A page where a layout read first needs the cascade after chain reads: the whole cascade is then refused above the limit, as before (tested with `offsetWidth`).

### Noticed, not changed

- A document change makes `plan()` walk the document for its sheets again (`stamp` includes the revision), so a loop that writes and reads one element is O(nodes) for each read. Not measured here.
- `a_hidden_iframe_download_is_saved` fails 3 of 4 runs alone on this machine under load.
- `base-build` with `--workspace --examples -p bare-stress` does not build the `bare-stress` binary; the matrix then fails every stress row. A second `base-build origin/main --release -p bare-stress` fixes it.

## Final benchmark of the perf goal, round 2 (2026-11-15)

Task: measure the 8 success criteria of `docs/perf-goal.md` again on a frozen commit after exact-fit arrays (owner decision of 2026-11-15). No product code changed. Raw logs and TSV files are machine-local under `/data/bare-tmp/r2f/out/`. The method is the one of the section "Final benchmark of the perf goal (2026-11-14)".

- NEW: `294f1c01` (main after PR #554). Main moved to `1545792b` (PR #555, the `computed-work` limit) while I measured. I did not measure it.
- Baselines. Journeys (criteria 1, 2, 4, 6): local branch `bench-base-vclock`, commit `300b8c53` (`f6415364` plus the replay patch, the virtual clock, the settled driver and the `load` end point; never pushed), corpus `/data/bare-tmp/corpus/virtual-load`. The baseline total of 138,272.1 M instructions is the same to the last digit as in the load-end baseline of 2026-11-14, so the baseline is reproduced. Ramps, sheet ramp, suite, limits (criteria 3, 5, 7, 8), test262, `exec_diff`, cost matrix: `f6415364`.
- Machine: archMachine (AMD Ryzen 9 5900HX, 16 cores, 30 GiB). Journeys and ramps ran from 09:58 to 10:09 with a load average of 5 to 17 (other agents built at the same time). The suite ran at a load average of 1.9 to 2.7. The machine was never idle, so wall times are weak and I give instruction counts. RSS comes from `wait4`.
- Builds: `cargo build --release -p bare-drive` in `/data/bare-tmp/target-r2f-new` (NEW, worktree `/data/bare-tmp/r2f/src`) and `/data/bare-tmp/target-r2f-base` (`300b8c53`). The gates and the cost matrix use a second call, `--release --workspace --examples -p bare-stress`, in the NEW target dir. The `bare-drive` binary was the same file after the second call (checked with `cmp`).

Seven of the eight criteria are met. Criterion 5 fails because a later merge broke the page: see "Criterion 5". Criteria 2, 3, 4 and 6 were not met in round 1 and are met now. Criterion 8 was half met and is met now.

### Criteria 1, 2, 4 and 6: the journeys

Inputs: corpus `virtual-load`, 47 journeys, 3 runs plus a PSS run 0 for each journey and binary (94 journey-binaries, 4 runs each, runs interleaved). Command: `tools/bench/journeys.sh compare --clock virtual --runs 3 --pss --out /data/bare-tmp/r2f/out/journeys.tsv <base bare-drive> <new bare-drive>`, run in `/data/bare-tmp/r2f/src` (the step files of `294f1c01`). Log: `journeys.log`.

- All 47 journeys pass in all runs on both binaries. The runner reports "Replay misses: none": 0 misses on both. The same-binary spread of instructions is 0.31% or less on every journey (runs 1 to 3).
- Totals, sum of medians of runs 1 to 3: instructions 138,272.1 M to 73,186.4 M (-47.1%, ratio 0.529). CPU (user+system) 18,126 ms to 11,550 ms (-36.3%, loaded machine). Peak RSS 2,750.2 MiB to 1,800.4 MiB (-34.5%). PSS (run 0) 2,425.9 MiB to 1,369.4 MiB (-43.5%); see the PSS note below.
- Median change of a journey: -18.3%. Geometric mean of the ratios: 0.649. 42 journeys are more than 5% lower, 5 are within 5%, none is more than 5% higher. Three are more than 1% higher: `mdn-reference` +4.3%, `substack-home` +3.4%, `paulgraham-home` +1.5%.
- **`craigslist-home` is a changed page input, not engine speed.** It costs 48,249.9 M on the baseline and 2,643.2 M on NEW (-94.5%); its peak RSS goes from 783.6 MiB to 81.5 MiB. The baseline binary has no `SharedWorker`, so the page stays on its ES5 path there (PR #546 added `SharedWorker`; the corpus holds the replies of the new path). NEW runs a different, smaller set of scripts. So criterion 2 is 52.9% with it and 78.4% without it. Both meet the target. Only the 78.4% number measures the engine and style steps on unchanged page input, and it passes by 1.6 points. The load-end baseline of 2026-11-14 gave 80.0% without `craigslist-home`.
- Criterion 2, other split: the five heaviest journeys on NEW (`react-docs` 12,429.5 M, `substack-home` 10,941.5 M, `rust-book-search` 10,146.8 M, `nodejs-org-home` 5,809.4 M, `github-docs-home` 4,618.4 M) are 60.0% of the NEW total. They went from 50,944.5 M to 43,945.6 M (86.3%). The other 42 journeys went from 87,327.6 M to 29,240.8 M (33.5%), and 41 of them without `craigslist-home`: 39,078 M to 26,598 M (68.1%).
- Criterion 4 (3 runs, instructions, spread 0.03% or less): `python-org-docs-link` 1,434.2 M (1,433.9-1,434.4) to 1,094.5 M (1,094.3-1,094.6), 1.310 times; `rust-book-search` 16,606.1 M (16,605.9-16,607.0) to 10,146.8 M (10,146.7-10,146.8), 1.637 times. Wall (loaded, weak): 189 ms to 158 ms and 1,867 ms to 1,291 ms.
- Criterion 6: peak RSS of `python-docs-search-results` 113.1 MiB (113.0-115.0) to 80.5 MiB (79.6-81.1), -28.8%. PSS (run 0, one sample): 108.0 to 73.0 MiB. Instructions 3,392.6 M to 2,559.6 M (-24.6%).
- PSS note: the 20 ms sampler of run 0 misses short journeys. 26 of the 94 run-0 samples are under 10 MiB (12 on the baseline, 14 on NEW). Over the 33 journeys with a valid sample on both sides PSS goes from 2,395 MiB to 1,369 MiB (-42.8%). PSS is not a criterion.

### Criterion 3: the ramps

Pages `/data/bare-tmp/bm/b/pages`, steps `run.steps`, local server, `bare-drive` of BASE (`f6415364`) and NEW, `perf stat -e instructions:u`, 3 runs each, interleaved. Script: `/data/bare-tmp/r2f/ramp.py` (the script of round 1 with the NEW path changed). Peak RSS by `wait4`.

| Page | BASE M instr (min-max) | NEW M instr (min-max) | Ratio | Target | Peak RSS BASE / NEW (MiB) |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `compm_22000` | 11,664.3 (11,664.3-11,664.4) | 400.1 (400.1-400.2) | 29.15 | 1,166 M | 69.1 / 33.8 |
| `rest_13` | 10,873.3 (10,873.3-10,873.4) | 1,042.5 (1,042.5-1,042.6) | 10.43 | 1,087 M | 52.6 / 46.4 |

Met for both. `compm_22000` improved from 1,828 M at round 1 and `rest_13` from 1,238 M. Hypothesis, not bisected: design H (PR #551, `getComputedStyle` styles only the way down to the element) for `compm_22000`, and H1 (PR #536, a restyle styles each element once) for `rest_13`. The shape of the cost of `rest_n` on NEW (spread under 0.001%): `rest_2` 529.2 M, `rest_30` 1,835.3 M, `rest_50` 2,768.3 M. Each added restyle costs 46.65 M (round 1: 60.0 M). About 436 M is fixed cost (parse of the page and of 36,000 rules, the index). `rest_13` is 10.43 times lower, only 4% over the target: a later change that adds 45 M to the fixed cost would lose it. Wall (weak): `compm_22000` 1,112 ms to 55 ms, `rest_13` 988 ms to 167 ms.

### Criterion 5: the 16 MiB sheet ramp. Not met: regression since PR #541

Page `sheety_16383` (a 16 MiB sheet of 187,852 rules, `getComputedStyle` of one element, then one `cssRules.length` read), steps `run2.steps`.

| Build | Peak RSS | Instructions | Outcome |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| BASE `f6415364`, 3 runs | 947.5 MiB (947.4-947.8) | 18,182.7 M | stops on `cssom-objects` |
| NEW `294f1c01`, 3 runs, `timeout 60` | no result | no result | killed after 60 s each |
| NEW, 1 run, no timeout | `ps` showed 200 to 215 MiB while it ran (not a peak) | at 98% CPU for more than 10 minutes, then I killed it | does not finish |
| `4a27b7a9` (#544), 3 runs | 274.0 MiB (274.0-274.3) | 5,404.1 M (5,403.8-5,405.6) | passes |

NEW does not meet the 300 MiB target because the page does not finish. The step `timeout 120000` of `run2.steps` and the `--timeout 300000` of `bare-drive` do not stop it, so a script that waits for the process to exit waits for ever.

Bisect: I ran `sheety_16383` with a 40 s limit on the binaries of the merge commits in between (`-p bare-drive` builds, or the earlier `base-build` trees). They pass (5,403.7 to 5,404.4 M instructions) at `c59e1bcf`, `476c04f9` (#531), `c9ead755` (#536), `95bd7864`, `49d6475d` and `4a27b7a9` (#544). They hang at `79829d19` (#541, class atoms), `c4848ecc` (#543), `2889fa06` (#551) and NEW. I built `79829d19` for this (`base-build 79829d19 --release -p bare-drive`). So the first bad merge is PR #541, "criterion 3, step 1: class atoms". PR #543 and later only keep it. `sheety_8192` (half the sheet) is fine on NEW: 2,680.2 M, 116.1 MiB (2,713.9 M and 143.7 MiB at round 1). The pages that read the sheet through the CSSOM only (`rd_y_sel`, `rd_x_sel`; no `getComputedStyle`) are fine on NEW too.

Where it spins (verified): I ran the page under `gdb` as a child and stopped it after 12 s. The page thread is in `bare::browser_computed::<impl Dom>::plan::add`, called from `Browser::style_availability`, from `browser_loader::sheets::Run::feed_styles`, from `Run::resume`, `Session::drive_loop` and `Page::wait_load`. The top frame is a libc copy (an AVX `memmove` loop); `perf record` of the running process shows the same libc loop (about 77% of the samples, plus about 14% in the kernel). Hypothesis (not verified): `feed_styles` runs again and again, and each run calls `plan()`, where `add` does `text.to_string()` of the 16 MiB sheet. At a few ms for each copy of 16 MiB (copy and page faults), 10 minutes is of the order of 100,000 to 200,000 calls, the same order as the number of rules (187,852). I did not count the calls. I did not find why #541 started it and why a sheet of half the size does not. I did not change code. Main moved to `1545792b` (#555) after the freeze; I did not run it.

### Criterion 8: the limits

- Restyle charge, same method as round 1: the page `/data/bare-tmp/fb/pages/rest_3000_j.html` restyles 6,002 elements in a loop of 3,000 and runs until the 500 M step budget of a task (`LIVE_TASK_STEPS`, `crates/bare/src/page.rs:83`) ends the script. NEW: the budget ended after 1,700 to 1,724 restyles (the loop logs every 25; last line `j=1700`) at 80,397.6 M instructions: 160.8 instructions for each charged step (47 M for each restyle). Round 1 gave the same restyle count at 102,842 M (205.7 for each step). The restyle got 22% cheaper (#536); the charge did not change (`STEPS_PER_RESTYLED_ELEMENT` is still 32, `crates/bare/src/browser_computed.rs:237`).
- A step of a plain JS loop (pages `steps_5000000` and `steps_50000000`, 3 runs each, spread under 0.0002%): NEW 9,037.6 M and 90,307.6 M, so 1,806 instructions for each iteration, 198.5 for each step at 9.1 steps for each iteration (BASE: 9,053.1 M, 90,458.1 M, 198.8). Round 1: 198.
- So the charge was about 9 times too small on BASE (23 against about 200), 1.04 times the cost at round 1, and is 1.23 times the cost now (198.5 against 160.8: a restyle step costs 81% of a JS step). A budget of 500 M steps now allows 80 G instructions of restyling, not 100 G. Met (the goal asks that the charge match the cost), but it moved to the safe side after #536. Not changed.
- `cssom-objects` cap: the string `cssom-objects` is in no file under `crates` (PR #531, CSSOM objects follow the collector). Verified by `grep`, and by the probe `rd_x_sel` above: the dense sheet with 844,366 rules is read in full (545.7 MiB), where round 1 stopped at the fixed 524,288 cap. Met.
- Other limits still in the code that guard a cost. These are notes, not fails:
  - `computed-work`: `max_work` is `1 << 30` (nodes times rules, `crates/bare/src/browser_computed.rs:128`, checked at line 655). It is a bound on a slow algorithm. Another agent removes it (PR #555, merged after the freeze; not measured).
  - `style-objects`: 65,536 `.style` objects for a page (`browser_style.rs:282`); it stops `rd_y_sty` and `rd_x_sty` above. `computed-objects` (`max_objects` 65,536) and `computed-sources` (1,024 sources, 32 MiB of sheet text) also stay.
  - `cssom-rules` (`MAX_RULES` 1 << 21, 2,097,152 rules) and `cssom-text` (`MAX_TEXT` 32 MiB) in `browser_cssom.rs:23,25`. These bound memory and text, not an algorithm.
  - `computed-nodes` (2^17 nodes, `browser_computed.rs:64`) stays; the section of PR #555 says it stops `compm_44000` and larger. Not measured here.
