## 2026-11-19: collector stress mode (plan step S0.x)

`BARE_GC_STRESS=1` makes `Interp::gc_due` true at every safe point of the old engine. The depth and statement-frame conditions stay: a collect still never runs inside a call. `Interp::set_gc_stress(bool)` sets the mode for one interpreter (tests). The environment is read once for the process (`OnceLock`); an `Interp` copies it into a `bool` field when it is made. Off, `gc_due` reads one more `bool`. The old engine's `Scope::safepoint` is an empty function and no code calls it, so the browser safe points are the callers of `Browser::collect_due` (the loader rounds, `browser_ui` after a key or click). The collector itself is unchanged.

Tests:

- `bare-js`: `gc_stress_is_due_at_every_safe_point_and_live_values_survive`. 20 collects at safe points, a global object and its array survive, a call after each collect works.
- `bare`: `a_page_gives_the_same_results_when_a_collect_runs_between_all_tasks`. One page with an interval, a timeout, a promise job, a click listener on a node that only the document holds, a node list and a dataset map. It runs twice, without and with stress. The log of both runs is equal, and the stress run makes at least 50 collects (the plain run makes none).

Journeys under stress (archMachine, debug test binaries of `crates/drive/tests`, each file run once plain and once with `BARE_GC_STRESS=1` in the environment of the test and of the `bare-drive` it starts). Collections are a lower bound: the sum over processes of the last `collections` of the `browser_stats` event (`BARE_OBSERVE=metrics`); 0 can mean that no event came. Wall time is from a machine that ran other builds; do not compare it.

## 2026-11-19: fetch roots in persistent handles (plan step S0.4, F1)

Step F1 of `docs/design-host-fetch.md`. The four `roots` calls of fetch, streams, abort and XHR leave the old hook (`Dom::roots`). A `Persistent` of `bare-js-api` roots each value that they gave.

Changes:

- `Pending` holds one `Persistent` (`root`): the promise of a `fetch`, or the `XMLHttpRequest` object of an XHR. The design names two fields (`promise`, `xhr`); one handle covers both, because the XHR object id is already in `xhr`. `OpenStream` holds one for its XHR object. A request that settles, is aborted or is dequeued drops its handle. `run_network_tasks` reads the promise from the handle inside the scope, so the promise stays rooted while `finish` allocates. `queue_xhr`, `queue_xhr_blob` and `queue_xhr_stream` take `it` for this.
- `Fetch::{fixed, json_parse, json_stringify, drain}`, `AbortHost::held` and `XhrHost::held` hold the prototypes, constructors, templates and intrinsic functions as `Persistent`. The six reaction templates of the streams moved from `Streams::roots` into `fixed`. The id fields (`protos`, `Fns`, `AbortHost::objs`, `Made`) stay: handler bodies still use `ObjId` and move in one later PR (owner decision).
- `browser.rs`: the four `roots` calls are gone. The old `trace` and `prune` calls are not changed.
- No change to `bare-js-api` or `bare-js`.

## 2026-11-19: XHR and abort objects as owners (plan step S0.4, F2)

Step F2 of `docs/design-host-fetch.md`. An `XMLHttpRequest` object, its upload object, an `AbortSignal` and an `AbortController` are owners of their entries. The `xhr` and `abort` lines of the old `trace` and `prune` hooks leave `Dom`.

Changes:

- `Owner::Xhr(o)` (an XHR object or its upload object), `Owner::Abort(o)` (a signal) and `Owner::Ctl(o)` (a controller). Each object gets its key when it is made and registers with `set_host_owner_obj`. The key is in the entry (`Xhr::key`, `Sig::key`, the value of `ups` and `ctls`). `Dom::own` takes that key for the first listener of such an object, so an object has one key (an XHR object and a signal are also event targets). `Owner::target` maps the three variants to the listener target; `Host::trace` visits the listeners and then the entry.
- Edges are `Traced`: `Xhr::{upload, cache}`, `Sig::{reason, Algo::Fetch}`, the signal of a controller. `Sig::sources` and `Sig::deps` are weak lists of host keys. A key resolves through the owner table (`Owner::Abort(o)`).
- `prune(dead)`: an XHR or upload object goes with its key (`xhr::forget`); a dead event drops its progress numbers (`xhr::forget_event`, `prog` is keyed by the `ProgressEvent` object). Signals and controllers go in one pass over the tables after the keys are released (`browser_abort::prune`): an entry whose key is free goes, a live signal drops the free keys from its weak lists and the abort algorithms of listeners that are gone. The pass runs after the old host's prune of the listener table, as the old order rule asks. A per-key `remove` of each signal cost +1.05% on `web_apis_load abort 1` (a hash remove for each dead signal); the single pass has the complexity of the old `retain`.
- `XhrHost::active` is gone, with its four stores. `Dom::trace` and `Dom::prune` have no `xhr` or `abort` line.
- Test-only: `Dom::xhr_entries` and `Dom::abort_entries` count the entries.
- No change to `bare-js-api` or `bare-js`.

Cost matrix (archMachine, base = F1 head `fabd5458` built in `/data/bare-tmp/s0/base-f2`, 807 rows, 3 runs per row, `-j4`; jemalloc for the rows over the limit under glibc): rows over +0.5% under both allocators: 0. Mean change -0.043% (glibc). Over under glibc only: `resources_load small 1` +0.75% (jemalloc +0.28%; known noise). `parse_load deep 1` and `10` fail to run on both trees. Rows of this change (glibc): `web_apis_load abort 1` +0.340% (jemalloc +0.320%), `abort 10` +0.476% (jemalloc +0.441%); `xhr_load 1` -0.700%, `100` -0.448%; `fetch_load post 1` -0.207%, `post 10` -0.224%, `bytes 1` -0.117%, `bytes 10` -0.440%, `objects 1` -0.257%, `objects 10` -0.276%, `iterate 1` -0.111%, `iterate 10` -0.114%. A first version that removed each dead signal by key was +1.049% and +1.199% on the abort rows under glibc and +0.972% and +1.181% under jemalloc. Callgrind of `abort 1` (symbols, one run for each tree) showed `abort::forget` at 1.14 M against 0.54 M for the old `abort::prune`; that led to the single pass. The abort rows keep a small cost: each of the 7 objects of a round makes an owner key and a `set_host_owner_obj` push (about 70 instructions, 0.5 M for 1 000 rounds), and the interface `prune` is a second hook.

## 2026-11-19: host-filled objects as owners for tracing (plan step S0.4, host-filled properties step 3)

Step 3 of `docs/design-lazy-properties.md` (see "Build of the second PR" there). Node lists, token lists, style declarations, attribute maps, CSS rule lists and dataset maps are owners now. The collector calls `Host::trace(key)` only for them, and `Host::prune(dead)` drops their entries.

Changes:

- The host key has two parts: the kind (`browser_sources::Source`) in the low `KIND_BITS` (4) bits and a slot of `Owners` above them. Other owners (wrappers, listeners, events) have kind 0. `Dom::new_source` reserves the slot, makes the object with the key, and registers the owner (`Owner::Source(ObjId)`).
- `Host::trace` and `Host::prune` of the interface call one subsystem by the kind in the key. The subsystem finds its state by the object, as before. The `retain` over the tables of these kinds is gone.
- The wrapper owner traces the edges from an element to its host-filled objects (`browser_sources::trace_node`: dataset, style, token lists, attribute map, `Attr` objects, a frame's window and document). A frame's edge is one lookup by node, not a scan of all frames. The call is behind one flag (`Dom::wrapper_edges`): it is set where such an object is stored (`new_source`, the `Attr` tables, the frame tables) and never reset.
- The old hook lost the calls of `browser_nodelist`, `browser_dataset`, `browser_style` and `browser_frames`. `browser_platform`, `at::` and `browser_cssom` keep what is not host-filled (token list iterators, `Attr` objects, rules, sheets, style rules, media lists).
- Captions, storage and the frame names are not owners: the page roots them and they hold no entry that a collection frees.
- `Owners::key` gives `slot << KIND_BITS`. `Owners::get`, `set` and `release` take the key.

Versions (cost matrix, glibc, instructions of `range_load iter 10`, a row with 10,000 wrappers and many collections; base = origin/main `d5dac645`):

| Version | `range_load iter 10` |
| --- | ---: |
| `trace_node` asks each subsystem for each wrapper (no early return) | +0.795% (first matrix, against `37df5bd1`) |
| An early return in each subsystem | +1.09% (against `d5dac645`; the row was +0.26% against `37df5bd1`) |
| One flag for all (kept) | -6.41% |

Callgrind of the second version showed `trace_node` at about 166 instructions per wrapper (frames 47, `at::` 30, the rest 42 and the inlined subsystems). The old hook paid about the same for each marked object, so the sum was not smaller. With the flag a wrapper of a page without such objects pays one load. A test (`a_wrapper_alone_keeps_its_attr_object_and_its_frame_window`) fails when the `Attr` or frame flag is not set.

## 2026-11-19: collector stress mode (plan step S0.x)

`BARE_GC_STRESS=1` makes `Interp::gc_due` true at every safe point of the old engine. The depth and statement-frame conditions stay: a collect still never runs inside a call. `Interp::set_gc_stress(bool)` sets the mode for one interpreter (tests). The environment is read once for the process (`OnceLock`); an `Interp` copies it into a `bool` field when it is made. Off, `gc_due` reads one more `bool`. The old engine's `Scope::safepoint` is an empty function and no code calls it, so the browser safe points are the callers of `Browser::collect_due` (the loader rounds, `browser_ui` after a key or click). The collector itself is unchanged.

Tests:

- `bare-js`: `gc_stress_is_due_at_every_safe_point_and_live_values_survive`. 20 collects at safe points, a global object and its array survive, a call after each collect works.
- `bare`: `a_page_gives_the_same_results_when_a_collect_runs_between_all_tasks`. One page with an interval, a timeout, a promise job, a click listener on a node that only the document holds, a node list and a dataset map. It runs twice, without and with stress. The log of both runs is equal, and the stress run makes at least 50 collects (the plain run makes none).

Journeys under stress (archMachine, debug test binaries of `crates/drive/tests`, each file run once plain and once with `BARE_GC_STRESS=1` in the environment of the test and of the `bare-drive` it starts). Collections are a lower bound: the sum over processes of the last `collections` of the `browser_stats` event (`BARE_OBSERVE=metrics`); 0 can mean that no event came. Wall time is from a machine that ran other builds; do not compare it.

## 2026-11-19: CSS rule and sheet objects as owners (plan step S0.4, CSSOM)

`docs/design-host-cssom.md`, plan step 4, option A. Built on the branch of #716 (host-filled objects as owners) with the branch of #713 (the `cssom_load` rows) merged in, and `main` at `913abd26`.

Changes (`browser_cssom.rs`, `browser_sources.rs`, `browser.rs`):

- Rule, sheet and media list objects get a host key when they are made (`Dom::new_owned`, kinds `Rule`, `Sheet`, `Media` in `browser_sources::Source`) and are owners. `trace_rule` visits the sheet, the declaration, the nested list, the media list and the parent. `trace_sheet` visits its list. `trace_media` visits its rule. The tables (`rules`, `sheets`, `medias`) keep their `ObjId` keys.
- The declaration object of a rule is a `Source::Style` owner already. Its trace and prune now also call `trace_decl` and `prune_decl`, which handle the `style_rules` entry (declaration to rule). A page with no CSSOM object pays one `OnceCell` test for each style object.
- Rule lists were owners in #716 (items, sheet, rule).
- The wrapper of an element visits the sheet of that element (`by_node`). The wrapper of a document or shadow root visits the sheets that it adopted (`adopted`). Both go through `browser_cssom::trace_node`, behind the existing `wrapper_edges` flag, and test `is_empty()` first.
- `browser_cssom::trace`, `browser_cssom::prune` and the `by_node` and `adopted` loops of `browser_cssom::roots` (with `in_tree`) are gone from the old hook. `roots` still returns the prototypes and the constructors (`State::roots`, `style_p`); no persistent handles exist for them yet. The `style-objects` cap stays.
- A sheet that the collector frees also leaves its place in an `adopted` list. Without this, a detached shadow root that adopted a sheet and that no script holds lost its sheet and `adopted()` panicked on the missing entry (found by a new test; the old hook kept every adopted sheet as a root).
- Behaviour that changes: a sheet of an element in the tree stays while the wrapper of that element stays. `Dom::wrap` makes the wrappers of all ancestors and the document wrapper reaches them, so an element in the tree keeps its sheet as before. A removed element that no script holds loses its wrapper and its sheet. This was the old rule too, now through the wrapper instead of `in_tree`. A rule declaration with pending inputs (`has_pending`) belongs to its sheet and goes with it; the published sheet text is unchanged.

Tests (`browser_cssom_tests.rs`, 6 new): a sheet that a script holds keeps its identity after a collect, and `el.sheet === el.sheet`; a sheet of an element in the tree stays with no script variable; a removed element that no script holds loses its sheet; a held rule keeps its sheet, and a media list keeps its rule; an adopted sheet lives with its document and with a shadow root; a reused key answers for the new object only; a shadow root that no script holds in the tree keeps its adopted sheet and styles; a detached shadow root that no script holds leaves no `adopted` entry.

Results (archMachine):

- Linux debug, `bare` lib, filters `cssom` 27, `style` 96, `sheet` 67, all pass. Full run of `bare-js-api` 5, `bare-js` 1062, `bare` 1660 pass. With `BARE_GC_STRESS=1` the three filters together pass (153 tests).

New: this change before the merge of `main`. No row over +0.5% under both allocators. Mean change -0.003% (glibc), +0.000% (jemalloc, 0 rows measured). The largest rise is `preload_load style 10` +0.28% (a known glibc-only noise row); the next are `cssom_load sheets 10` +0.20% and `cssom_load sheets 1` +0.19%. Two rows failed to run on both trees: `parse_load deep 1` and `parse_load deep 10` abort with a stack overflow (stack limit 8 MiB here); they are not caused by this change.

## 2026-11-19: URL objects as owners (plan step S0.4, navigation)

Plan step 3 of `docs/design-host-navigation.md`: option A for the `URL` family and option D (persistent handles) for `Entry.cache`, `NavObjs` and the two `Storage` areas. Frames, structured clone and child pages are not in this PR. Handler bodies stay on the old `Interp`. The cap `max_objects` stays.

Changes:

- A `URL`, a `URLSearchParams` and an iterator object are owners (`Owner::Url`, `Owner::Params`, `Owner::Iter` in `browser.rs`). Each gets a host key when it is made, after its table entry is final.
- `UrlObj.sp`, `ParamsObj.url` and `IterObj.sp` are `Traced<Value>`. `Host::trace(key)` visits the one edge of the owner (`browser_navigation::trace_owner`). `Host::prune(dead)` removes the entry of each dead owner and takes its bytes off `param_bytes` (`prune_owner`).
- The old hook calls `browser_navigation::roots`, `trace` and `prune` are gone. The three `retain` loops and the sum over all lists are gone.
- `Entry.cache` is an `Option<Persistent>`: it lives as long as its entry, and a dropped entry frees its slot at once. `NavObjs` holds 6 handles (`url`, `params`, `iter`, `location`, `history`, `storage_proto`); the `ObjId` copies stay for reads and are valid while the handles live. `area_get` holds each area with a handle in `Nav.area_held`. `Dom::fixed` keeps only `loc_proto`, `hist_proto` and the constructors.
- The 6 `NavObjs` handles and the areas are in the persistent table now, so the bound of `a_cleared_or_finished_timer_frees_its_callback_at_the_next_collect` is 209 instead of 203 (observed 207).

Tests (5 new in `browser_navigation_tests.rs`): a dropped `URL`, its `searchParams` and its iterators are collected together and their keys are used again (the key table does not grow over 3 rounds); a held `searchParams` keeps its `URL` and a held `URL` keeps its `searchParams`; a reused key answers for the new object only (every owner points at a live entry and its trace gives exactly the edges of that entry); `history.state === history.state` after a collection; an evicted entry frees its handle (a `WeakRef` to its state is empty, and the persistent table does not grow over 3 rounds of 6 pushes).

Measurements (cost matrix, archMachine, 3 runs per row, 805 rows run; base = `98e7d328`, the head of #714, built fresh into `/data/bare-tmp/s0/base-nav`): mean change glibc -0.046%. No row over +0.5% under both allocators; no row over +0.5% under glibc. `navigation_load`: `url 1` -0.05%, `url 10` -0.04%, `iterate 1` +0.42%, `iterate 10` +0.39%, `subclass 1` -0.03%, `subclass 10` -0.10%, `history 1` -0.26%, `history 10` -0.31%, `storage 1` -0.58%, `storage 10` -0.50%, `route 1` -0.11%, `route 10` -0.18%. `session_load`: -0.02% to -0.15%. Other rows with a collection fell by up to 1.2% (`range_load iter 10` -1.21%, `streams_load pending 1` -0.89%). The design expected about -1.7% on `url 1`; the measure is -0.05%. Hypothesis: the 3,000 owners of the row cost about as much as the prune and trace work that went (the design's own estimate was -1.3% net). `iterate` is the row with the most objects for each unit; it is +0.4%, under the limit. Instruction counts only; no wall time.

`parse_load deep 1` and `deep 10` fail to run on every tree that was tried (the base of this PR, the new tree and `37df5bd1`): stack overflow in the example. This change does not cause it.

## 2026-11-19: promise and microtask interface (plan step S0.4, M1)

PR M1 of `docs/design-host-microtasks.md` (option A, decided 2026-11-19). No browser change, and the engine calls none of the new hooks (that is M3).

Changes:

- `bare-js-api`: the `Engine` methods `new_promise`, `resolve_promise`, `reject_promise`, `promise_then`, `promise_react`, `promise_status`, `queue_microtask`, `checkpoint`, `drain_microtasks`, `pending_jobs`, `clear_failed_job`, `iter_open`, `iter_next` and `iter_fail`, with thin `Scope` wrappers. New types `PromiseState<'s>` and `Iter<'s>`, and the constant `MAX_PENDING_REJECTIONS` (1024). The `Host` hooks `report_exception`, `between_jobs` and `promise_rejections` take `Scope` and `Local`. They have default bodies.
- Old engine (`eval_api.rs`): each method calls the `host_*` method of the same job, with one `Local` push for each result (`promise_status` pushes the value of a settled promise). The bound of the old engine, `eval_promise::MAX_PENDING_REJECTIONS`, was 1024 already; a test keeps both equal.
- `Iter<'s>` keeps the old engine's fast paths. The design says it holds two locals (the iterator and its `next`). The old engine has no iterator object for an array, a string, a Map or a Set (`It`: `Plain`, `Coll`, `Generic`), so `Iter` has two locals and a position of three words (`state`). The locals are roots. The old engine keeps its source or owner there, and the new engine can leave `state` at zero. The host reads none of it.
- Old engine behavior kept: `host_checkpoint` does nothing only when `depth` is not 1. A host function that a script calls at the top level of the script runs at depth 1, so its checkpoint runs the jobs. Inside a script function (depth 2 or more) it does nothing. The test uses the second case.

Cost matrix (archMachine, base = origin/main `d5dac645` rebuilt, because main moved by #707 after the brief; new = this branch; 3 runs per row, minimum; `-j4`; 805 rows; jemalloc for rows over the limit under glibc): mean change glibc +0.022%. 14 rows are over +0.5% under both allocators; all are `bare-js` rows that call none of the new code: `gen_load delegate 1` +1.72% and `10` +1.94%, `gen_load iterobj 1` +0.76% and `10` +0.82%, `intl_load cmp_opts 1` +0.81% and `10` +0.83%, `intl_load locale 1` +1.27% and `10` +1.29%, `intl_load make 1` +0.97% and `10` +1.30%, `intl_load nf_locale_opts 1` +1.46% and `10` +1.49%, `iterator_load generic 10` +0.57%, `sc_load custom_iter 10` +0.84%. Two more rows are over under one allocator only (`iterator_load generic 1`, `sc_load custom_iter 1`). `parse_load deep 1` and `deep 10` fail to run on the base too.

Cause: the codegen-unit split of `bare-js`, as in the earlier exceptions. With `RUSTFLAGS="-C codegen-units=1"` on both trees (`gen_load`, `intl_load`, `iterator_load` and `sc_load` examples, 16 rows, minimum of 3, glibc), every row is lower in the new tree: -0.04% to -0.16%. Example: `intl_load locale 1` 151,960,128 base and 151,760,554 new. A callgrind diff of `intl_load make 1` (16 units) shows the extra instructions spread over `get_prop_nat`, `intl_opt_for`, `HashMap::insert` and `intl::lookup`, with other inlining in each. Not fixed. The owner decides on a cost exception for these 14 rows.

Checks:

- New tests in `eval_api_tests`: a promise settles and a `promise_then` reaction runs on the drain (fulfilled and rejected, `promise_react` of a plain value, `Unsupported` for a value that is not a promise); `queue_microtask` runs once and `pending_jobs` counts it; a checkpoint inside a script function does nothing, and one from a host scope runs the queue; `iter_open` and `iter_next` over an array, a string, a Set, a generator and a script iterator; `iter_fail` calls `return`, runs the `finally` of a generator, keeps the thrown value, and keeps an abort with no script; a `Local` promise and its value survive the collections that an old host starts in `between_jobs` during `drain_microtasks`; the two bounds are equal. New test in `bare-js-api`: a host with no hooks gets the default bodies.
- Linux: `bare` lib 1647 passed, `bare-js` lib 1054 passed, `bare-js-api` 6 passed and 1 doc test (5 compile-fail doc tests pass).
- Windows 11 VM: `bare-js-api` 6 passed; `bare-js` filter `api` 17 passed.

Not tested: the hooks with a real call from the engine (M3); the wrapper cost in a browser row (nothing calls it); a full `bare` run on the Windows VM; wall time; `iter_next` over a Map (the `Coll` path is tested with a Set, and Map uses the same cursor code).

Owner decision (2026-11-19): exception granted for the 12 other rows above, and a standing rule from now on. A row that is over +0.5% under both allocators passes when both trees, built with `RUSTFLAGS="-C codegen-units=1"`, show it within +0.5%. The cause is then the codegen-unit split, not new work. The PR records both numbers.

## 2026-11-19: microtask hooks through the interface (plan step S0.4, M3)

PR M3 of `docs/design-host-microtasks.md` (option A). It stacks on PR #720 (M1). The engine now calls the three microtask hooks of `bare_js_api::Host`, and the old `Host` no longer has them.

Changes:

- Old engine: `Host::report_exception`, `Host::between_jobs` and `Host::promise_rejections` are gone from `eval_host.rs`. The engine calls the interface host (`api.host`) in the same places: before each job and when the queue is empty (`between_jobs`), at the end of a checkpoint (`promise_rejections`), a `queueMicrotask` callback that throws, and a `FinalizationRegistry` callback that throws (`report_exception`). Three helpers in `eval_api.rs` (`api_between_jobs`, `api_report`, `api_rejections`) open a scope, push the values as locals, call the hook and turn its error back into an engine error. Rejections are tracked when an interface host is set (was: an old host).
- Browser: `Dom` implements the three hooks on `bare_js_api::Host` (`browser.rs`). The bodies are the old ones. They reach the old `Interp` through `s.engine()` (owner decision: handler bodies move later).
- `run_script` is not added to the interface. The body of `between_jobs` calls `Interp::run_script` through `s.engine()`, so it needs no new interface method. The loader PR adds it with its first real use.
- Tests: the old-host tests of the hooks now use an interface host (`eval_host_tests`, `eval_rejection_tests`, and the collector test in `eval_api_tests`). New test: `between_jobs` runs before each of 3 jobs and once when the queue is empty, and an error of the hook ends the drain and repeats on the next drain.

## 2026-11-20: frames as owners (plan step S0.4, navigation)

## 2026-11-19: module interface (plan step S0.4, MD1)

PR MD1 of `docs/design-host-modules.md` (option A, decided 2026-11-19), plan step 2. No browser change. The loader (MD2) is not in this PR.

Changes:

- `bare-js-api`: the `Engine` methods `module_parse`, `module_requests`, `module_set_requested`, `module_url`, `module_link`, `module_evaluate`, `take_dynamic_imports`, `finish_dynamic_import`, `reject_dynamic_import` and `fail_dynamic_import`, with thin `Scope` wrappers. The three settle methods read the `ObjId` from the `Persistent`.
- The old methods have the semantics that the design lists. There is no difference to report.
- The toy engine of `bare-js-api` answers `Abort::Unsupported` for the methods that run code, and nothing for the others.

## 2026-11-20: fetch objects as owners (plan step S0.4, F3)

COMPLETE with an owner exception on `fetch_load objects 1` and `10`. PR is open and not merged. This entry replaces the first one, which said STOPPED at the cost gate.

Changes:

- `Owner::Fetch(ObjId)` in `browser.rs`: Headers, Request, Response, body stream, reader and headers iterator objects get a host key in `add_obj_in`. Their edges are `Traced` values. `Dom::trace` calls `browser_fetch::trace` for the key.
- The entries are `Ent { key, f }`. `browser_fetch::prune` runs once after the keys are released, in one pass over the entries. A dead owner takes its entry, and its bytes and reader leave `retained` and `readers`. The old `Fetch::trace` and `Fetch::prune` hooks are gone.
- Owner decision 2026-11-20: the dead-key loop in `Dom::prune` looks up each key once and dispatches with one `match` on the owner variant. Before, it called `owners.get(k)` up to six times for each key. Every per-variant action stays (Xhr and Event forget, node wrapper identity and listeners, Computed `drop_owner`, Source prune, navigation `prune_owner`, `Loc` to `prune_loc`). The arms exclude each other, so the order between them does not matter. `owners.release(k)` and the passes after the loop are unchanged. Fetch and Abort keys need no per-key action there.
- Rebased on origin/main `71273c8b` (frames, `Owner::Loc`). Both variants stay in `Owner` and in `Owner::target`.

History of the first attempt (base `7203937a`, before the one-lookup loop): per-key `forget` cost +2.5% on `fetch_load objects`. The one-pass `prune` gave `objects 1` +1.47% and `iterate 1` +0.51%. ## 2026-11-20: persistent remote windows (plan step S0.4, navigation step 6)

Plan step 6 of `docs/design-host-navigation.md`: child pages and the session keep their remote windows in persistent handles. No interface change.

Changes:

- `Kids::wins` (`browser_child.rs`) holds `(Win, Vec<Persistent>)` for each window object. The window entry holds its target and its proxy. The `location` entry holds the `location` object. `Kids::common_held` holds the 10 shared functions of `Common` (handler, `Proxy.revocable`, `closed`, `replace`, the two `href` functions, four no-ops). `Kids::add_win` and `Kids::set_common` make the handles.
- `Kids::roots` and its call in `Dom::roots` are gone. `Kids::sync` drops the entries of a child that left the document, so the handles of its windows go with it. `Drop for Kids` frees the rest.
- The design named `window.open`, `opener` and the session as other holders. In the code `window.open` gives `null` (`browser_basics.rs`) and `opener` is `null`. The session makes a new `Browser` for each document, and a `Browser` owns its `Kids`. So `Kids` is the only holder, and no other code needed a change.
- Observation: in the parent page a live iframe wrapper also reaches its window through the frames owner (`browser_frames::trace_node`). In a mutation run with no handles at all, a window that no script held still survived three collections. So in the parent page the handle is a second root. A test that waits for a collection cannot show a missing handle. The tests count the handles through a test-only `Kids::handle_count`.

Tests (`browser_child_tests.rs`): a remote window that no script holds has its 3 handles and the 10 shared ones while its page lives (this test fails when `add_win` makes no handle). Removing the iframe leaves only the 10 shared handles, and a `WeakRef` to the window is empty after a collection. A window that a script holds, with its `location` object, answers the same after 3 collections.

COMPLETE. PR is open and not merged. No cost row is over +0.5% under glibc, so the codegen-unit and jemalloc checks were not needed.

Changes:

- `bind` in `bare-js-api`: `Engine::bind(target, this)` and `Scope::bind`. The adapter in `crates/js/src/eval_api.rs` calls `Interp::host_bind`. The toy engine of `crates/js-api/src/tests.rs` answers `Unsupported("bind")`. Adapter test `bind_fixes_this_and_reads_no_script_bind`: `this` is fixed, a script that replaces `Function.prototype.bind` changes nothing, and a target that is not a function throws a `TypeError`.
- `Owner::Stream(ObjId)` in `browser.rs`. A stream, its controller and its reader each get a host key in `browser_streams::own`. The entries (`Stream`, `Ctl`, `Rdr`) hold their key. Every edge is a `Traced` value: the links between the three objects, `source`, `start`, `pull`, `cancel`, the queued chunks, the bound pull reactions, the errored reason and the pending reads of the reader.
- `Dom::trace` has one arm for `Owner::Stream`. `Dom::prune` calls `browser_streams::prune` once, after the keys are released and next to the fetch call. `prune` is one pass over the three maps. It takes the queued bytes of a dead controller out of the total. There is no arm in the dead-key loop, because a stream key needs no per-key action (the F3 cost finding). `self.streams.trace` and `self.streams.prune` are gone from the old hook.
- `host_bind` sites: 6 calls in 3 places of `browser_streams.rs` (`pull_if_needed`, `cancel_stream`, `construct`). They stay on `Interp::host_bind`. The handler bodies have no `Scope` yet, and the design moves them in one later PR.

The old engine collects only at a safe point, never inside a call, so a collection inside `pull` is not possible there. That case needs the new engine.

## 2026-11-20: style accessors at first use (plan step S0.4, CSSOM)

COMPLETE. PR is open and not merged.

Owner decision (2026-11-20): host-only fill, no engine change. The 250 style accessors and the computed prototype members are made at first use, not at page start. Option F of `docs/design-host-cssom.md` was not built. It planned `Host::lazy_member` for the two prototypes. The old engine asks the host only for `on*`, `HTML*Element` and a fixed list of names (`Heap::lazy_step`, `lazy_own`, `lazy_miss` gate on `on_name`), and only `EventTarget.prototype` has `LAZY_CHAIN`. So option F needs an engine change.

Changes:

- `browser_style::install` defines only the lazy global `CSSStyleDeclaration` (`browser_lazy`) and the `style` accessors of `HTMLElement` and `SVGElement`. `browser_style::ensure` makes the prototype, the 250 accessors, `constructor` and (through `browser_computed::fill`) the computed prototype. `Style.proto` is the flag. It is set last, so a failed `ensure` does not leave a half-made prototype behind.
- `ensure` runs at the three places that make a style object or hand out the prototype: `style_of` (the first `el.style`, and `rule.style` through `rule_declaration`), `get_computed_style` (after the argument checks) and a read of the `CSSStyleDeclaration` global. There is no other path: `Style.proto` and `Computed.proto` are read only in `style_of` and `get_computed_style`.
- Kept: handler ids in `style.fns` (handler id to property index), the computed prototype inheriting from the style prototype, and the key order base members, 250 accessors, `constructor`. `getComputedStyle` stays a global at its old place; `computed::install` only defines it.
- `computed` accessor names use one buffer, as `style` does (no `format!` for each of the 250 names). The two `transform` names keep `format!`.
- Deviation, as for every lazy global in `browser_lazy.rs`: until the first read, `Object.getOwnPropertyDescriptor(window, 'CSSStyleDeclaration')` shows an accessor. A write replaces the global and installs nothing. The names list, `in` and `Object.keys` do not read it.
- Owner decision (2026-11-20): this deviation is accepted. It matches the other lazy globals.

Tests (`browser_style_tests.rs`): a page that never touches style does not install; `el.style`, `getComputedStyle(el)` and `rule.style` each work as the first use; `'color' in CSSStyleDeclaration.prototype` is true with no style object; the prototype has 260 own names (8 base members first, `constructor` last) and the computed prototype 262. The two counts were also checked on the base tree with the same test. A write to the global installs nothing.

## 2026-11-20: module loader on Persistent (plan step S0.4, MD2)

Changes (`docs/design-host-modules.md`, option A, plan step 3), all in `crates/bare/src/browser_loader/modules.rs`. The loader still calls the old `Interp` methods. Three raw references became `Persistent` handles:

- `Modules::evals` holds a `Persistent` of the evaluation promise of each module graph, made in `run_graph`. `settle_evals` reads the promise from the handle at each checkpoint, and the handle drops when the promise is seen settled.
- `Load::Throw` holds a `Persistent`, made where `module_parse` throws and where a bad specifier makes a `TypeError`. `finish_module` and `reject_dynamic_import` read the value from it.
- `serve_imports` takes the `import()` queue with the interface method `Engine::take_dynamic_imports`, so each request's promise is a `Persistent`. The loader reads the promise object from the handle where it settles the request (`import_promise`).

No `Host::roots` line is removed: there was none. The design already says so ("Old-engine calls that leave the old hook: None"); `evals` was rooted only by the engine (`ModRec::cap`). A link error from `module_link` and a rejection read in `settle_evals` stay raw values: the loader reports them at once, with no engine call between.

## 2026-11-20: structured clone design (plan step S0.4, navigation)

COMPLETE. Design only: `docs/design-host-clone.md`. No code changed. The PR is not merged and has no auto-merge. The owner reviews it before any code.

Why: option E (the `CloneOps` sub-trait, commit `55594ea6`, not merged) gave the same output as the old walk but was +2.76% on `navigation_load history 1` and +3.00% on `history 10` (figures from the task brief, not rebuilt). The owner chose option F: a native clone algorithm in the engine, with a host `Delegate` as in V8.

Measured (archMachine, origin/main `a8049517`, release build with symbols in `/data/bare-tmp/s0/design-clone/target`; `tools/js/instr.sh`, minimum of 3 runs; callgrind, 1 run per row):

| Row | Instructions | Walk | `materialize_with` |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| `navigation_load history 1` | 85,956,359 | 13.31 M (15.3%) | 8.38 M (9.6%) |
| `navigation_load history 10` | 792,321,020 | 132.5 M (16.6%) | 83.6 M (10.5%) |
| `web_apis_load clone 1` | 182,540,980 | 53.3 M (28.9%) | 19.7 M (10.7%) |
| `scheduler_load messages 1` | 31,125,968 | not on the path (scalar messages skip the walk) | |

One `history` state is 13.3 K (walk) + 8.4 K (materialize) = 21.7 K instructions, for 3 objects and 8 properties. The +0.5% limit is 434 instructions per state. Per-call costs: `own_keys` 750, `get_value` 232, `get_own_property` 138, `HashMap::insert` 346 (+ SipHash), `clone_class` 229, `is_host_object` 199, `define_data` 473, `put_value(length)` 1,228, `intern_units` 155. Type sizes of the old `State` (scratch program): `SV` 24, `SKey` 16, `SKind` 88, `SNode` 112 bytes.

Design: F2 (the engine walks plain data and writes a byte record in the V8 style, with a string table for property names) plus F3 (a fused copy with no record for `structuredClone` and same-heap `postMessage`). The host sees only host objects, the transfer list and the error, through `CloneHost`. The format, the cost model and the limit checks live in `bare-js-api`, so the old engine and js2 share one copy. The page gives the interface, the format, the walk rules, the js2 route, and a plan with a spike first (gate: at least 8.5 M fewer instructions on `history 1`).

Hypothesis (not measured): the native walk costs about 4.4 K per `history` state against 21.7 K, about 17 M less on `history 1`. The record is about 48 bytes against about 1.1 KB.

Not tested: every "Expected cost" number, the cost of option E (taken from the brief), `jemalloc` and codegen-units=1 runs, the Windows VM, the new engine. The V8, WebKit and Ladybird record layouts are verified only as far as the public headers show; statements marked "from memory" in the page are not verified.

## 2026-11-20: structured clone spike (design-host-clone.md step 1)

COMPLETE. GATE PASS: `navigation_load history 1` has 10.93 M fewer instructions (glibc), against the gate of 8.5 M. The spike is not merged and has no PR. Code: branch `t3/clone-spike`, commit `e64c76ad` (reference only).

What the spike is: `Interp::clone_out_fast` and `Interp::clone_in` in `crates/js/src/eval_clone.rs` (about 300 lines), `Heap::clone_peek` and `Heap::clone_install` in `heap_shape.rs`, and a hook in `browser_navigation_state.rs` (`State.rec`). They handle primitives (not Symbol and not BigInt), strings, plain objects, dense arrays without holes, and the cycle. The record has one byte buffer with a tag for each value, varints, a string table for property names and back-references by id. The fast path reads shape entries and slots straight from the object. It builds each new object with its final shape at once (`new_object` then `clone_install`, `fill_array` for an array). An object with an accessor, a dictionary, an exotic kind, a hole, a symbol or index key, a BigInt, or any other class makes the fast path return `None` before anything changed. The old walk then runs. A limit also gives `None`, so the old walk makes the error. No getter runs on the fast path, so the spec order of getters is not at risk. The cost model and the step charges are the old ones. Used for `serialize` (history) and for `clone_state_with` with an empty transfer list.

Behavior: `state_bytes=17600` and `checksum=ok` on `history 1` are unchanged. `browser_clone_ops_tests.rs` of `55594ea6` (65 cases and 2 cap tests, in 2 test functions) passes, and so do the filters `browser_history_state_cap_tests` (3), `browser_navigation_tests` (56) and `structured` (4). Many of the 65 cases hit other classes and run the old walk, so they do not all test the fast path.

Measured: archMachine, release with symbols, base = origin/main `42018c02` built fresh (`/data/bare-tmp/s0/base-spike`), spike = `e64c76ad` (`/data/bare-tmp/s0/spike-rel`). `perf stat -e instructions:u`, 3 runs each, glibc with `tcache_count=65535`, and jemalloc.

| Row | Allocator | Base (3 runs) | Spike (3 runs) | Change |
|---|---|---:|---:|---:|
| `navigation_load history 1` | glibc | 85,906,173 to 85,907,348 | 74,978,320 to 74,980,030 | -10.93 M (-12.7%) |
| `navigation_load history 1` | jemalloc | 93,604,719 to 93,606,048 | 83,130,182 to 83,130,305 | -10.47 M (-11.2%) |
| `navigation_load history 10` | glibc | 791,783,803 to 791,786,563 | 683,148,598 to 683,153,852 | -108.6 M (-13.7%) |
| `navigation_load history 10` | jemalloc | 835,740,559 to 835,885,870 | 731,617,830 to 731,707,101 | -104.1 M (-12.5%) |
| `web_apis_load clone 1` (information) | glibc | 182,467,781 to 182,470,428 | 186,380,593 to 186,381,972 | +3.91 M (+2.1%) |
| `web_apis_load clone 1` (information) | jemalloc | 191,770,000 to 191,807,492 | 195,686,081 to 195,723,331 | +3.93 M (+2.0%) |

The spread of the 3 runs is under 0.002% for glibc and under 0.02% for jemalloc. Allocations on `history 1`: 72,267 to 62,267 (10 fewer per state).

Callgrind, `history 1`, 1 run per tree (86,857,469 and 75,929,967 instructions in all), per state (1,000 states):

| Part | Base | Spike | Design hypothesis |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| Serialize (`serialize`) | 13.29 K | 4.93 K | 2.4 K |
| Materialize (`materialize_with`) | 8.37 K | 6.32 K | 2.0 K |
| Both | 21.7 K | 11.2 K | 4.4 K |

The gain is 10.9 M of the hypothesis of 17 M (64%). The serialize part came near the hypothesis. The materialize part did not.

Where the remaining cost sits (per state, callgrind inclusive):
- Serialize 4.9 K: `CloneW::val` 4.5 K, of which `CloneW::key` 1.44 K for 5 keys (0.44 K in `units`, the rest is the key table scan and the cost add), `is_host_object` 0.2 K, `clone_class` 0.22 K, `id_put` 0.19 K, `clone_peek` 0.11 K. The rest is the record `Vec` growth and `into_boxed_slice` (a realloc), the `ids` and `keys` `Vec`s, and the recursion.
- Materialize 6.3 K: `clone_units` (intern of 4 keys and 2 strings) 1.9 K, with 0.63 K self time (a zeroed 128-byte stack buffer on each call); `clone_install` 0.33 K; the new objects and the `fill_array` call; the two scratch `Vec`s.
- The hypothesis counted interning at 1.1 K. It is 1.9 K. The intern cost is now the largest part of the read. A cache of the last keys, or interning from the Latin-1 bytes with no copy to a `u16` buffer, would cut it. Neither is built.

`web_apis_load clone` goes up by 2%: its graph holds a Map, a Set, a Date and a typed array. The fast path (hypothesis, not profiled) walks the plain prefix, meets the first other class and drops its work. The old walk then runs from the start. The real design (step 3, every class native) has no such waste. This row says nothing about the gain of F3.

Decision for the owner: the gate passes, so the series may go on. The gain on `history` is 64% of the hypothesis and the spike has no transfer, no other class and no getters.

Not tested: codegen-units=1 runs, the cost matrix (only 3 rows ran), the Windows VM, `clone_copy` (F3), the other classes, accessors and getters, the transfer list, the full `bare` test suite (only the 4 filters above ran), peak memory and the record size of the `history` state (48 bytes by hand in the design, not read from the spike), wall time. The disk of `/data` was full once during the work. The first release build of the spike failed with "No space left on device" and was built again after space was freed.
## 2026-11-20: clone record format (design-host-clone.md step 2)

COMPLETE for Linux. The Windows run did not happen (see "Windows"). PR is not merged and has no auto-merge. Base: origin/main `511d3eb4`.

Changes: the `clone` module of `bare-js-api` (`crates/js-api/src/clone.rs`, tests in `clone_tests.rs`). No engine change and no browser change.

- `RecordWriter` and `RecordReader`: the tags (32, with `Host` reserved), LEB128 varints, zigzag `Int`, the key table (`KNew8`, `KNew16`, `KRef`, `KIdx`), ids (an object takes its id at its tag, a view after its buffer), and `Text`, `Key`, `ErrorField`, `ReadError`. The reader checks every bound. A length is compared with the bytes that are left before any use, so a damaged length makes no allocation.
- `Meter`: the cost model and the limit checks with their names (`bytes`, `depth`, `nodes` as `Abort::Limit(name)`), and the steps (`take_steps`). The constants are those of `browser_navigation_state.rs`: 48 a node, `2 * len + 16` a string or a name key, 20 an index key, 16 an entry, `8 * limbs + 16` a BigInt, `n` a buffer, `64 + n` a listed item; `len / 32` and `n / 64` steps. Check order is the old one: depth, nodes, bytes for a node; nodes, then bytes for a listed item.
- `IdMap`: 8 inline pairs, then a hash map with a cheap hash. The writer uses it for the key table. The engines can use it for their identity table.

- Three `Engine` methods (`clone_out`, `clone_in`, `clone_copy`) with default bodies that return `Abort::Unsupported`. Neither `bare-js` nor the test engine changes.

Two small differences from the design page: `KNew` is two tags (`KNew8` for Latin-1, `KNew16` for UTF-16), like `Str8` and `Str16`; an error record has its fields as tagged entries (`ErrMessage`, `ErrStack`, `ErrCause`, then `End`) so that the walk can write them in the order it reads them.

One deviation from the design page. `Engine::clone_in` takes `&mut Cloned` and not `Cloned`. A record with no moved item can be read again. `entry_state` takes the record out of the entry, reads it and puts it back, so no navigation borrow is held during the read.

## 2026-11-20: long-session row and ready time (plan steps M4 and M5)

COMPLETE for M4. M5 is built and run, but its check (spread under 5% on 5 runs on an idle machine) is NOT met: the machine was never idle. Linux only. PR is not merged and has no auto-merge.

Changes: `tools/bench/journeys.py` has two new modes, `journeys.sh session` (M4) and `journeys.sh ready` (M5). No change in `crates/*`. The existing `record`, `run` and `compare` are not changed.

- `session [--rounds N] BARE_DRIVE`: one `bare-drive --repeat N` process for each journey (default N = 20). Each round opens a new page in the same process. It prints RSS and peak RSS (`VmHWM`) after each round, and the glibc heap in use. It fits a least-squares slope over rounds 2 to N (round 1 pays the one-time costs). The session total is the sum of the slopes over the journeys.
- `ready [--runs N] BARE_DRIVE`: one cold replay for each run (default 5). `ready_ms` is the time from the start of the process to the stderr line of the first step after `open`. `open` itself ends at about 0 ms: the next step waits for the page. At that moment the tool reads the CPU (all threads, `schedstat`) and the RSS of the process and all its descendants, and counts them. It also prints `load1` and the spread of `ready_ms` and of the CPU.
- A bare-drive run has one process (`procs` is 1 in every row), so "all processes" is one process today. The tool counts the whole tree, so a later multi-process browser is counted.

Inputs: bare-drive built from this branch (origin/main `1aa1bc6a`), release. Machine archMachine, 16 cores. Corpus recorded live on 2026-11-20 with `journeys.sh record` into `/data/bare-tmp/s0/m4m5/corpus`, real clock (the old `/data/bare-tmp/corpus` does not exist any more). 45 public journeys recorded; 3 did not pass live (`curl-se-home`, `duckduckgo-html-search`, `nextjs-docs`) and are not measured. The staging journey and the typing page are not in `tools/drive/public` (login and local fixture), so they are not in these rows.

### M4: long session, 20 rounds, today's engine

Two full passes (`journeys.sh session --rounds 20`), machine busy with other agents (load 5 for the first pass, 20 for the second; memory does not depend on load as much as time does).

| Pass | Journeys with 20 rounds | Sum RSS slope | Sum peak RSS slope | Sum heap slope | Sum of RSS, round 1 to round 20 |
| ---- | ----------------------- | ------------- | ------------------ | -------------- | ------------------------------- |
| 1    | 42                      | +17.9 MiB/round | +23.7 MiB/round  | +8.9 MiB/round | 1,437 to 2,105 MiB              |
| 2    | 42                      | +12.7 MiB/round | +18.2 MiB/round  | +4.2 MiB/round | 1,366 to 1,938 MiB              |

- Mean per journey: about +0.3 to +0.4 MiB/round of RSS (42 journeys). The two passes differ by 30%, so the slope has a spread of that size. Hypothesis: allocator slack and a timing change in what a page loads under different load. Not checked.
- One journey, one pass: the slope is rough. Passes differ by more than 0.3 MiB/round (RSS or peak) for 12 of 42 journeys (largest: `python-docs-search` +3.86 then +1.33, `rust-book-search` RSS -2.41 then -0.25 with the peak +2.02 then +1.72). `example-page` and the three `httpbin-*` journeys stay under +0.06 MiB/round. Pages with large scripts grow most: `crates-io-home` +1.0 and +0.3, `nodejs-org-home` +1.0, `debian-org-home` +1.3 and +0.7.
- The slope is not a proof of a leak. The process keeps its HTTP cache and style and script caches across rounds, and they grow with the first rounds. I did not split the slope into caches and leaks. A leak check needs rounds past the point where the caches are full.
- Three journeys stop at round 2 in both passes: `python-docs-search-results`, `rust-book-chapters`, `rust-book-sidebar`. They pass in a single run. In round 2 of `rust-book-chapters` the style sheets come back as 304 with no body (the HTTP cache of the first round asks the replay again), the `click` fails with `hidden`. Hypothesis: the replay answers a conditional request with the recorded 304 and no body. Not checked, and I did not change the browser or the replay. The slopes of these three are `n/a`.
- A round after the first sees the cache of the first round, so rounds 2 to 20 do less network work than round 1. The row measures what stays in memory, not the cost of a cold page.

Best run (the only one with a lower load): load average 3.1 to 4.2 on 16 cores, so NOT idle. `ready_ms` has a median of 9.2 ms over the journeys (2.6 ms to 95.5 ms; the sum of the medians is 903.7 ms). Spread (max - min over the median of 5 runs): 23 of 45 journeys are under 5%, 31 under 10%, the median spread is 5.0%, the largest is 159% (`httpbin-cookies`, 2.7 ms). The slower journeys (median 20 ms or more, 16 journeys) have spreads of 2.1% to 16.6%; 6 of them are over 5%.

Two later runs at load 10 to 27 and 17 to 11 gave sums of medians of 1,703 ms and 979 ms and 37 to 42 journeys over 5% spread. Under load the CPU at ready time (all threads) has a spread above 5% for 41 to 45 of 45 journeys, so the CPU is not a stable gate here either.

The 5% target is not verified. At 3 to 100 ms, 5% is 0.15 to 5 ms: hypothesis, the noise of the scheduler and the process start is of that size even on an idle machine. ## 2026-11-20: strings and atoms (plan step S1.7)

`bare-js2` has strings and atoms (`crates/js2/src/string.rs`, `atoms.rs`, `cell.rs`; design 6.10 items 13 and 14).

- A string is one heap cell: an 8-byte header, a length and a cached hash (16 bytes), then the units inline. A one-byte (Latin-1) string takes `16 + len` bytes and a two-byte string `16 + 2 len`, each rounded up to a size class. Every flat string is inline, also a long one: a string above 8,192 bytes takes a large cell of its own. A flat string has the narrowest form, so two flat strings of equal length and different form are different strings.
- `Str::concat` copies a result of fewer than 32 units. A longer result is a rope node (one 32-byte cell, no copy). `Str::flatten` copies a rope once into a new cell, with a heap stack (no recursion), and turns the root into an `Indirect` cell that holds only the copy. So the two parts of a flattened rope are free for the collector. A concatenation that meets an `Indirect` string takes the copy.
- Shared atoms (`SharedAtoms`): one table for a session, with a heap of its own that nothing collects. Its cells have `FLAG_SHARED`. The collector must not mark them (`Str::is_shared`), because they are in no heap of a realm. One mutex guards interning and finding an atom by content. A realm reads the cell of a shared atom it already has with no lock: the cell is complete before it is published and never written again. Run-time atoms (`RuntimeAtoms`) are in the heap of the realm. The table is weak and has one hook, `Atoms::sweep(&heap)`. S1.5 calls it after the mark phase and before `Heap::finish_mark`. It needs the new `Heap::is_marked`.
- One atom per content in each realm: lookups go to the realm table, then the shared table, and a new atom is made in the realm only when both miss. If a source atom appears after the realm made a run-time atom for the same content, the realm keeps its own atom. Shared code must name a source atom through `Atoms::adopt` (once per realm). It must not compare a shared atom with a run-time atom by address. Open question for the owner: design 6.11 item 11 puts per-realm constants in the feedback vector, which is where `adopt` fits.
- The cell header is the new `CellHeader` (`cell.rs`): a 32-bit layout code and 32 flag bits. String code reads it only through `new`, `layout` and `flags`, and takes every offset from `CellHeader::SIZE`. If S1.4 picks the 8-byte shape pointer, only `cell.rs` changes: the header stays 8 bytes, `layout` reads the code through the pointer, and the flags move into the shape or a second word.
- `unsafe` code is now allowed in `value`, `heap`, `string` and `atoms`. The comments in `lib.rs`, `Cargo.toml` and the Miri job of `ci.yml` say so.

Checks: 31 `bare-js2` tests (21 new) pass on Linux, under Miri (nightly 2026-11-17; 143 s) and on the Windows 11 VM (`cargo xwin test`). They cover narrow forms, copy and rope thresholds, ropes grown at either end (left-deep and right-deep, 100,000 parts), shared sub-ropes, mixed widths, a string over the length limit, hash equality across forms, atoms, source atoms shared by two realms and three threads, a run-time atom against a later source atom, atomize in place, the sweep hook with a table that shrinks, and a mark of a rope through `children`.

Micro rows (`crates/js2/examples/string_load.rs`; archMachine, release, 3 runs; user instructions from `perf stat` with `tools/js/instr.sh`'s glibc setting; peak RSS from `rss_peak`). QuickJS 2026-06-04 runs the same loop as JS (`s += 'ab'`, `s = 'ab' + s`, `t = a + b`). The JS loop is part of the QuickJS count, so the table also gives the QuickJS count of the same loop without the concat (`t = a`). The js2 rows have no loop of script; the table subtracts the run with N = 0 (336,621 to 337,026 instructions, 2.2 to 2.4 MiB).

| Row, N = 100,000 | js2 instructions (3 runs) | js2 per step | QuickJS instructions (3 runs) | QuickJS per step, loop removed | js2 peak RSS (KiB) | QuickJS peak RSS (KiB) |
| --- | --- | ---: | --- | ---: | --- | --- |
| append (`s += 'ab'`, one flatten) | 15,898,284 to 15,898,698 | 155.6 | 86,633,918 to 86,634,181 | 633 | 5,576 to 5,736 | 3,804 to 3,820 |
| prepend (`s = 'ab' + s`, one flatten) | 18,408,321 to 18,408,546 | 180.7 | 84,461,815 to 84,462,027 | 611 | 6,336 to 6,584 | 3,484 to 3,784 |
| short (`'ab' + 'cd'`, copy, collect each 100,000) | 20,481,911 to 20,482,384 | 201.5 | 57,242,105 to 57,242,244 | 339 | 5,332 to 5,488 | 3,232 to 3,376 |

QuickJS loop without concat: 23,339,978 to 23,340,267 (N = 100,000). N = 1,000 gives the same order: js2 append 495,115 to 495,635, QuickJS append 2,117,693 to 2,118,237 (loop 1,459,888 to 1,460,570). QuickJS empty program: 1,194,130 to 1,194,279 instructions, 3.3 to 3.5 MiB.

- The js2 spread is under 0.01% in instructions. Peak RSS spread is up to 5% (page effects).
- Instructions: js2 costs 0.25 to 0.30 times the QuickJS count on the append and prepend rows and 0.59 times on the short copy. This compares a Rust loop with a script interpreter, so only the order is meaningful. The js2 rows include flatten and, for `short`, the sweep of 100,000 cells per round.
- Memory is the other way on the two rope rows. js2 grows 3.3 MiB over its start for 100,000 appends (100,000 rope nodes of 32 bytes, then the copy). QuickJS grows about 0.4 MiB. Cause, read in `quickjs.c` (5065 to 5110): when a short string (up to 512 units) is appended to a rope whose right part is a short flat string, QuickJS copies the two into a new right part and frees the old one at once through its reference count, so the rope stays a few nodes long. Without reference counts, the same rule in a GC heap would leave each old right part as garbage until a collection: copy cost up to 512 units for each append, and more memory between collections. Not built or measured here; an option for S1.5 when the trigger and the allocation volume are known.
- Atom hit (`atoms.intern`, 1,000 names of 5 to 7 bytes, no allocation): 233,860,153 instructions for 1,000,000 (`string_load atom`; 1,303,657 for none), so 232.6 per hit. This includes `i % 1000` and the name lookup of the loop. No QuickJS row.
- Cell sizes: a one-byte string of 1 to 16 units takes a 32-byte cell, the empty string 16 bytes, a rope 32 bytes.

Findings, not changed: (1) `Heap` rounds a cell above 8,192 bytes to a 64 KiB mapping (S1.3), so a flat string of 8 to 64 KiB wastes up to 56 KiB and costs a system call. The flatten of a long rope hits this. (2) `ROPE_MIN` = 32 is not tuned. (3) `Chars::hash` is one multiply for each unit: no measurement of its spread beyond the table tests. (4) The Miri run of the crate takes 143 s of test time (not split by test).

Not tested: a collection inside a task (S1.5 and S1.6 do not exist); the shared table under a real second heap that collects; the cost matrix (js2 is not wired into the browser); arm64; substrings, `Value` of strings in objects (S1.8 and S1.9).

## 2026-11-20: clone fast paths (design-host-clone.md step 4)

Linux and Windows pass the filtered tests. The cost matrix has no row over the limit, and `history 1` and `10` drop by about 12%. The PR is not merged and has no auto-merge. Base: origin/main `3a0c7bf9`, which has #737 (step 3). Since `b72ac7d9`, the head of #737, main changed only `crates/js2`, the CI file and docs (`git diff --stat`). So the `bare` and `bare-js` sources of the base are the ones of `b72ac7d9`, and all numbers below come from a fresh build of `b72ac7d9`.

Changes.

- `crates/js/src/heap_shape.rs`: `Heap::clone_shape`, `clone_prop`, `clone_elem`, `clone_keys` and `clone_install`, with `CloneShape` and `CloneShapes`. `clone_shape` accepts an ordinary object or a dense array in shape mode, with only plain data properties, string keys and no hole. `clone_prop` and `clone_elem` read one value at its turn and give `None` when the shape or the element count is not what `clone_shape` saw. A shape never changes, so the same shape id means the same keys. `clone_install` gives a new object its keys and values at once. It refuses (and the caller defines key by key) for a key that is not a string, a key that is there twice, more than 128 keys, or an object that is not new and empty.
- `crates/js/src/eval_clone.rs`, walk: `CloneWalk::props_fast` reads the keys and the values straight from the shape and the slots, and writes an array as `ArrD`. The steps and the byte charges are the ones of the generic `props`, in the same order. After each read it needs the object to be as it was. When a child (which can run a getter) changed it, `props_back` gives the keys that are left to `props`, which reads them as the spec does. `props` has a new argument `dense`: for an array that `props_fast` began, an index below it is written as a value with no key, and a key that a getter deleted is written as `Hole`.
- `crates/js/src/eval_clone.rs`, reader: the keys and values of an object go to two scratch stacks and `clone_install` makes the shape at once. A dense array gets its elements and its `length` from one `fill_array`, with no `put_value`. The string scratch is a reused `Vec<u16>` (the old 64-unit zeroed buffer cost 0.63 K a state in the spike). The vectors of the reader have room for 8.
- Shape map: `CloneShapes` keeps the last 4 key lists of one read, by a hash. A hit is checked against the keys of the shape, so a clash of the hash cannot give a wrong shape. It makes no allocation.
- Test-only switch: a thread-local in `eval_clone.rs` (`GENERIC_OUT`, `GENERIC_IN`) turns off the fast path of the walk or of the reader. It does not exist outside `cfg(test)`: `clone_generic` is `false` there.

Differential test: `clone_fast_path_gives_what_the_generic_path_gives` (`eval_clone_tests.rs`). A seeded generator makes 2 to 5 objects and arrays with plain keys, holes, Maps, Dates, BigInts, a function (refused), and getters. A getter deletes, adds, overwrites or redefines (data, accessor, enumerable or not) a key of any object, also of the root that the walk is inside, pushes, pops, cuts or deletes in an array, and some throw. Some cases run under small byte, depth and node limits. Each case runs in 4 realms: both generic, fast walk with generic reader, generic walk with fast reader, both fast. The answers must be the same text: the copy, the source graph after the walk, the log of the getters, and the cost (or the error). The test counts the objects that took the fast path (1,474 in the 1,000 default seeds), the objects that fell back half way (59), the throws (51) and the limit stops (297), and asserts a floor on each. `CLONE_FUZZ_SEEDS=N` runs more seeds: 30,000 and 20,000 seeds pass (53,716 fast objects and 3,348 half-way fallbacks in the 30,000).

The test found one bug before it passed. A dense array that fell back half way wrote the `ArrD` header for all `n` elements, then keyed pairs for the rest. The reader then read the keys as values and reported a damaged record. The fix is the `dense` argument of `props`.

Step 3 review items.

1. The reader now checks a view against its buffer: `len * size + offset` with checked arithmetic against the buffer length, and a buffer that is not a buffer. A bad view is `Unsupported("damaged clone record")`. The test `clone_view_outside_its_buffer_is_a_damaged_record` has 7 bad views (offset, length, element size, overflow) and one good view. It failed before the check (the error was not `Unsupported`) and passes after.
2. Peak RSS of `history 1`, base (`b72ac7d9`) against new, `cp --reflink=never` copies of both binaries, 3 runs each, idle machine, no glibc tunable: base 13.2, 13.0, 13.1 MiB; new 13.4, 13.3, 13.5 MiB (`VmHWM`). ## 2026-11-20: layout census of the old engine (plan step M3)

COMPLETE for Linux. The PR is not merged and has no auto-merge. Base: origin/main `1aa1bc6a`.

Changes (`bare-js`, no change to a hot path):
- `layout_census.rs`: `LayoutCensus`, 18 buckets, and `stats_on()` (reads `BARE_JS_STATS` once per process).
- `eval_census.rs`: `Interp::layout_census()` walks the realm. `Heap::census` (in `heap.rs`) does the heap part. A sample is taken at the start of `Interp::collect`, again just before the sweep (with the collector scratch), and when the `Interp` drops. The sample with the most bytes prints as a `layout total=... bucket=bytes ...` line after the `gcstats` line.
- Every size is a capacity in bytes (what the engine asked of the allocator, no malloc headers). A shared tree, source text or compiled function counts once.
- `Interp` now has a `Drop`, so `into_heap` takes the heap with `mem::take`. Nothing in the repo calls `into_heap`.
- `tools/js/layout_census.sh` runs a command under massif (`--pages-as-heap=no`) and prints the census line and the engine bytes of the massif snapshot where they peak. `tools/js/massif_engine.py` does the second part: an allocation is the engine's when the nearest crate frame to the allocator is `bare_js`. With `--host-parse` it leaves out the tree that an example parses itself (`eval_load` keeps its copy after `Interp::new` clones it).
- Tests: `eval_census_tests.rs`, 5 tests.
- The `new` engine (`bare-js2`): no hook. Its heap has `mapped_bytes()` already, but no cell has a kind or a layout yet, so a census by layout has nothing to count. The hook belongs to S1.4 (cell header).

Buckets: `objects` (records and slab tables), `slots` (inline and vector value slots), `dict`, `elements`, `shapes`, `strings` (records, units, interner, ropes), `binary`, `heap_other` (symbols, BigInt), `bytecode`, `feedback` (inline caches), `source`, `ast`, `tables` (per-script tables of the tree walker), `scopes`, `envs` (environments and the function table), `names`, `stacks` (pools kept for reuse), and `collector`.

`collector` is a bucket the plan did not list. A collect holds the mark bits, the gray stack, the root vector and the work lists at the same time as the garbage. In `eval_load objects 10` it is 42% of the peak, because the 200 000 element array puts 200 000 values in the work list.

## 2026-11-20: cell header, shape id against shape pointer (plan step S1.4)

Decision: the cell header is two 32-bit words, a shape id and a word of layout code plus 24 flag bits. A raw 8-byte shape pointer lost. `crates/js2/src/cell.rs` now holds only the id form, with a stub `Shape` and a `Shapes` table (S1.8 builds the real shapes). Both forms were built and measured at commit `f6d06f8e` (feature `shape-ptr` in `cell.rs`); the next commit removes the pointer form. The header stays 8 bytes in both forms. Only `cell.rs` changed for the header; `string.rs` got one arm for the new `Layout::Object`.

The two forms:
- Id (kept): `shape: u32` (0 for a string) and `bits: u32` (layout code in the low 8 bits, flags above). The marker reads the layout from `bits` and sets one bit per used shape id (`Shapes::note_live`). After the marking, `finish_marks` marks each shape cell once. A cache compares the id. `Shapes::of(header)` is a table load and then the shape.
- Pointer: one `NonNull<Shape>`. The shape holds the layout code and the flags, so a string needs one static shape for each pair of layout and flags (4 × 8 = 32 here), and a flag change swaps the pointer. The marker reads the layout through the shape and marks the shape cell of every object it visits.

Micro rows (`crates/js2/examples/header_load.rs`; archMachine, Ryzen 9 5900HX, release, `perf stat` user instructions, 3 runs each with the N = 0 or R = 0 run subtracted; spread of every cell below is under 0.01%). Object cells of 32 bytes (header and 3 words); S is the number of shapes.

| Row | Id, instructions per op | Pointer | Pointer against id |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| `alloc` (header write; each 100,000 cells a collection keeps 1,000), S = 1 / 64 / 4096 | 41.59 / 41.60 / 41.90 | 41.70 / 41.69 / 41.71 | +0.3% / +0.2% / -0.5% |
| `mark` (a graph of 59,333 reachable cells, 3 in 4 are objects with 2 children), S = 1 / 64 / 4096, per visited cell | 81.39 / 81.43 / 83.90 | 86.39 / 86.38 / 86.88 | +6.1% / +6.1% / +3.6% |
| `hit` (the check against the cached shape matches) | 22.00 | 21.00 | -4.5% |
| `miss` (the check fails, the shape is read), S = 64 / 4096 | 27.91 / 28.00 | 23.95 / 24.00 | -14% / -14% |
| `flags` (read the flags, flip a bit, write the header back) | 33.0 | 35.0 | +6% |

Cycles (`cycles:u`) were not trusted: other builds shared the machine. Five runs of each form side by side, run in turns: `miss` with S = 4096 took 147 to 150 M cycles for the id form against 110 M for the pointer form (about 7.2 against 5.3 cycles per read; the extra table load misses the L1 cache). `mark` with S = 64 took 130 to 132 M for the id form and 131 to 135 M for the pointer form (equal within the spread). `flags`: 151.5 to 152.3 M against 185.0 to 187.1 M (3 runs each).

Reading of the rows:
- Allocation is the same: both forms write one 8-byte word. The pointer form adds the shape marks of the kept cells only.
- The id form is cheaper in the marker by 5 instructions per cell, because the pointer form marks the shape cell of each object through `Heap::mark` (a block header lookup and one division by the cell size). A one-entry "last shape" test would cut this in both forms; not built.
- The id form is dearer where code needs the contents of a shape: 4 instructions and one more dependent load (header, table base, table entry, shape field; the pointer form has header and shape field). An inline cache hit does not need it: the cache compares the id with the header word, one load, no table. Only a cache miss, a megamorphic site and a generic operation read the shape through the table. The hit row differs by 1 instruction in this loop (a zero-extending load of the 32-bit id); the cycles are equal (106 M against 107 M).
- A variant that makes the id an index into a `Vec<Shape>` (no table of pointers) gave the same instruction count for `miss` (27.9 and 28.0) and no better cycles, so it was dropped.
- Per-cell flags are the main structural reason. A string changes its flags after it is made (atom, rope that is flattened), and objects will (frozen, has overflow). In the id form that is a bit operation. In the pointer form every flag combination is a shape: 32 static shapes for strings alone, and a transition for each flag change of an object. Hypothesis, not built: shape counts grow by the number of flag combinations in use. The alternative, a second header word with the flags, makes the header 16 bytes.

Memory side, from the old engine at its census peak (`BARE_JS_STATS=1`, `BARE_JS_EXEC=auto`, M3 census of #740 at `c3607163` plus a scratch patch that also prints counts, `/data/bare-tmp/s14/census-counts.patch`, not in the repository; 1 run each, the census is deterministic). A cell here is an object or a string of the old engine; the new engine makes each of them one cell, so this is an approximation.

| Case | Census total | Objects | Strings | Shapes | Cells (objects + strings) | 16-byte header costs (8 bytes for each cell) | Id table (8 bytes for each shape) |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| `eval_load objects 10` | 8,240,509 | 521 | 2,457 | 177 | 2,978 | 23.8 KB (0.29%) | 1.4 KB |
| `eval_load closures 10` | 26,257,250 | 50,521 | 457 | 49 | 50,978 | 407.8 KB (1.55%) | 0.4 KB |
| `eval_load webpack 10` | 1,912,740 | 3,526 | 974 | 30 | 4,500 | 36.0 KB (1.88%) | 0.2 KB |
| `browser_load event 1` | 819,435 | 1,457 | 1,239 | 558 | 2,696 | 21.6 KB (2.63%) | 4.5 KB |
| `browser_load lookup 1` | 900,644 | 1,801 | 1,440 | 557 | 3,241 | 25.9 KB (2.88%) | 4.5 KB |
| `browser_load mutation 1` | 1,191,402 | 2,301 | 1,439 | 557 | 3,740 | 29.9 KB (2.51%) | 4.5 KB |
| `browser_load rel 1` | 1,203,008 | 2,525 | 1,748 | 574 | 4,273 | 34.2 KB (2.84%) | 4.6 KB |

- Both 8-byte forms cost the same for the cells (8 bytes each). The 16-byte header (pointer and a flags word) is the form that would cost 0.3% to 2.9% of the old total, more as a share of the cell bytes alone. The id table is 0.2 to 4.6 KB, under 0.6% of each total. Shape counts are small (30 to 574): the table never matters; nor does the cache effect of the shapes at these counts.
- Records that hold a shape: with ids, the hot part of a cache record (shape and offset, design 6.11 item 12) is 8 bytes; with pointers it is 16. The old engine has 87,088 to 123,304 bytes of feedback in these cases (24-byte `Ic` records, not all of them records of this kind). Hypothesis: about 8 bytes less for each record, not measured.
- The census counts are at the sample with the most bytes, and the old engine counts garbage that its sweep has not freed. No `new` census hook was added: `bare-js2` has no collector or heap walk yet (S1.5), so there is nothing to count.

32-bit targets: not built or measured. The design lists no 32-bit target and `Value` holds 48-bit addresses in 64 bits. On a 32-bit target a pointer is 4 bytes, so the pointer form would fit the header with a flags word in 8 bytes. Verify if a 32-bit target is ever added.

Checks: `bare-js2` tests: 35 pass on Linux (4 new in `cell_tests.rs`: header round trip, shape lookup, a shape that a marked cell uses survives and an unused one is freed) and 35 on the Windows 11 VM (`cargo xwin test`); the three `header_load` rows also ran on the VM. Miri (nightly): 35 pass in 150 s of test time. The pointer form passed the same unit tests at `f6d06f8e`. Clippy shows no new finding in `cell.rs` (the existing findings in `heap.rs` and `bare-os` are not touched).

Not tested: a real shape (S1.8); the marker of S1.5 (the mark row is a stand-in with a work stack); the cost matrix (js2 is not wired into the browser); arm64; a 32-bit target; a "last shape" test in the marker; objects with flag combinations (no count of flag combinations exists yet); wall time (the machine was shared; cycles above are indicative only); Windows instruction counts.

## 2026-11-20: shapes (plan step S1.8)

`bare-js2` has real shapes (`crates/js2/src/shapes.rs`; design 6.4, 6.11 items 12 and 15). They replace the stub `Shape` and `Shapes` of S1.4 in `cell.rs`. The header keeps its 32-bit shape id. Base: the S1.4 branch (#743), which is based on origin/main `1a323b46`.

What it has:
- Transition tree. A shape is a node: prototype, parent, table, slot count, inline capacity, layout (48 bytes). The first child sits in two fields; the others are in a map. A root is `(layout, prototype, inline capacity)`. The prototype is in the shape. `Shapes::literal` gives the final shape of an object literal (exact capacity, no slack).
- Shared descriptor tables (design 6.11 item 15). The keys of a chain are one table of 12-byte entries (key address, slot, attributes). A shape uses the first `count` entries. A shape that adds an entry that the table already has at that place reuses the table. So shapes that differ only in prototype or inline capacity share one table. Only a branch that adds another entry copies the prefix. A table of more than 8 entries gets an open-addressing index (4 bytes for each of 2 times the entries) at its first probe.
- Dictionary mode. `to_dict` gives one object its own shape and a table that changes in place. Its slots keep their numbers, a deleted slot is reused, and the id stays, so no value moves. A cache must not fill for it (`cacheable`). It happens for a delete in the middle of an object of more than 8 properties, for an attribute change (`reconfigure`: freeze, seal, data to accessor), and for more than 128 properties. A small object (8 properties or fewer) stays in the tree when it deletes a key: the shape before the key takes the later keys again, as the old engine does (`remove_prop`). The caller shifts the later slots (`Removed::shifts`).
- `with_proto` makes one node with the same table and the new prototype, so `setPrototypeOf` does not cost a dictionary.
- Slack (`Site`): a site gives its first 8 objects `initial` inline slots, then the most that they used (at most 30). A later object that needs more widens it, twice at most. The new capacity is a new root; objects that exist keep their shape.
- Collector hooks. `note_live(heap, header)` and `finish_marks(heap)` keep the parameters of S1.4, and `cell::Shapes` is still a path to the table (a `pub use`). The S1.5 collector (`gc.rs`) can name it as before; its tests use the stub `Shape` and `Shapes::add(heap, shape)`, which are gone. `note_live` now returns the prototype of a shape the first time the shape is seen in a collection (it returned nothing), and the collector must push that cell on its work list. `finish_marks` frees every shape that no marked object uses and that is not a parent of one that is used, frees the tables that only they used, and marks the key atoms of the shapes that stay (not a shared atom). It runs every collection (O(shapes + entries)); no id is renumbered. A freed id can be reused, so `Shapes::epoch` changes when a tree shape was freed: a record that holds an id must drop it then. Order for S1.5: marking, then `finish_marks`, then `Atoms::sweep`, then `Heap::finish_mark`.
- The shape ids of freed shapes are reused at once, and a shape id that is in no live header is valid only until the next `finish_marks` (a shape that a native function made and has not put in an object yet, when a collection runs).
- `header_load` (S1.4) now builds its shapes with the real API (a root for each prototype and 2 to 6 keys). Its rows were not run again.

Checks: 52 `bare-js2` tests pass on Linux (18 new in `shapes_tests.rs`; `cell_tests.rs` lost its 2 shape tests and has 1 new) and 52 on the Windows 11 VM (`cargo xwin test`). Miri (nightly): 52 pass in 165 s of test time. The tests cover roots, memoized transitions, accessors (2 slots), table sharing across prototypes and capacities, branch copies, the hash index (128 keys), the 129th property, literals, a delete of the last, first and a middle key of a small object (the same shape as an object that never had the key), the dictionary path (slot reuse, 300 keys, packing), attribute changes, prototype change, the header, a collection (freed shapes, id reuse, tables cut, key atoms marked or not marked, prototypes returned once, dictionary shapes freed with their object without an epoch change, a shared atom as key) and slack.

Shape census on a synthetic React-like trace (`crates/js2/examples/shape_census.rs`; the same trace as a script in `tools/js/shape_trace.js`; xorshift32 from one seed, so both make the same objects). 8,000 steps; each step makes a props object (a template of 1 to 8 of 16 names, 40 templates, biased to the first; one in 8 swaps two keys; one in 16 deletes its first key), an element (a literal of 6 keys), every second step a hook (a literal of 5 keys), every fourth step a fiber (a constructor that sets 24 keys; every 20th deletes `f3`, so it goes to dictionary mode). 22,000 objects, all alive. The census is deterministic (no timing), so one run each. archMachine.

| | Value |
|---|---:|
| Shapes (live, after a collection in which every object is live) | 1,661 (1,561 tree, 100 dictionary); 1,697 before it (36 freed) |
| Descriptor tables / entries / entry room | 473 / 4,484 / 5,276 |

Object cells, 22,000 objects (bytes by size class, per object): props 79.9 (avg 4.5 slots used, 8.0 inline), element 64.0 (6 of 6), hook 48.0 (5 of 5), fiber 255.9 (24 of 23.9). Layout A (the overflow pointer word exists only in an object that overflows): 84.3 per object, 96.9 with the shape bytes. Layout B (a pointer word in every object): 87.3 and 99.8. Overflow: 4 props objects and 8 fibers (the first objects of their sites, before the slack settles). There is no object module yet (S1.9): a cell is the 8-byte header, the inline slots, the pointer word and the overflow record (an 8-byte header and the extra slots), counted by size class; no object was built.
