## 2026-11-20: compiler in js2 (plan step S2.5)

New modules in `crates/js2`: `compile.rs` (scope analysis, registers, labels, root maps, entry points), `compile_expr.rs`, `compile_stmt.rs`, `compile_pat.rs`, and the example `examples/bc_hist.rs` with the `eval_load` sources in `examples/data/`. The compiler turns the tree of one function into a `Code` through `Asm`. It never holds more than one function tree. It needs no interpreter: the tests run the S2.4 verifier on every function that it compiles. Base: the S2.4 branch plus the pre-parser (S2.2, PR #756).

What it does:

- Scope analysis. A variable that no inner function names lives in a register. A captured variable lives in a context slot, one `PushCtx` per scope that has one. The pre-parser facts say which names a child captures, and the parent passes a chain of context levels to each child (`Child::chain`), so a child compiles alone. A name that no scope declares is a global. The top level of a script has only globals. `let`, `const` and `class` get the hole (`LoadHole`) only when the name can occur in the text before the end of its declaration (a scan of at most 4,096 bytes, then it assumes yes). A read from a child function uses `GetCtxTdz`.
- Contexts. `to(e, dst)` (value into a register chosen by the caller), `any(e)` (a register variable is read in place), `effect(e)` and `cond(e, jump_if, label)` (a test: `&&`, `||`, `!` and the comparisons make jumps, no boolean value). Compare-jumps take a constant on either side (the operator is mirrored) and `null`, `undefined`, `true` and `false` use their own ops. `x += 2` on a register is one `AddI` in place. A register variable is copied only when the right side may assign it (a text scan of the right side for `=`, `++`, `--` and the variable name).
- Literals. An object literal with plain names is `NewObjLit` (keys in a recipe), an array literal is `NewArrLit`, up to 64 items; larger or computed ones use `NewObject`/`DefField`/`DefElem` and `NewArray`/`ArrayPush`. A template literal is one `Concat`.
- Loops, `break`, `continue`, labels. A loop is `head: test; body; cont: JmpBack head; exit:`. `if (t) break;` and `if (t) continue;` are one conditional jump when nothing must be popped or run first. A `for (let ...)` whose variables are captured pushes one context for the loop and makes `CopyCtx` at the end of each iteration. `for-in` and `for-of` use the iterator record ops. A `for-of` has a handler on the body that runs `IterClose` and throws again.
- `try`, `catch`, `finally`. The finalizer is compiled in line, after the block, after the `catch` clause, in front of each `break`, `continue` and `return` that leaves it, and once more for an exception. The handler ranges are split so that no inlined copy is inside the range of its own `try`. `return` keeps its value in a temporary when a finalizer or an iterator close runs first.
- Destructuring in declarations, assignments, parameters, `catch` and `for` heads (objects, arrays with holes, defaults, rest of arrays).
- Root maps. At each safepoint the compiler lists the registers that every path has written (a register joins on its first write and leaves when freed; at a join the set is the intersection of the sets of all jumps to it). That is the exact condition that the verifier checks. It is not liveness: a variable stays in the map until its scope ends.
- Dead code is not emitted (after `return`, `throw`, `break`, and so on, until a label that a jump reaches).

Check: 34 tests in `compile_tests.rs`. 25 golden tests (the disassembly of one function per construct, in the order of the listing; each was read by hand against the JS meaning), and the others: the 9 `eval_load` sources compile with nothing unsupported; 36 functions of control-flow and scope shapes (labels, `finally` with `break` and `return`, `switch` with lexicals, closures in loops, patterns in `for-of`, and so on) with 10 more inner functions; the list of unsupported constructs; the handler ranges of `try`/`catch`/`finally`; a root map; the literal fallbacks; the hole; the register limit (a call with 70,000 arguments is refused); the script top level. `build` in the tests runs `verify` on every function. Linux: `cargo test --locked -p bare-js2 --lib` 260 pass (226 before this change). Windows 11 VM (`cargo xwin test --no-run`, exe through `winssh`): `compile::tests` 34 pass; the whole lib run is 258 pass and 2 fail: `parse::tests::corpus_status_matches_acorn` and `parse::lazy_tests::a_lazy_parse_finds_the_same_errors_as_a_full_parse_on_the_corpus` (parser corpus tests of S2.2, panic at the corpus read; hypothesis: the corpus is not found on the VM; not changed here and not run on main on the VM). `cargo clippy -p bare-js2 --all-targets`: no warning in the new files.

`bc-hist` (`cargo run --release -p bare-js2 --example bc_hist [-v] [FILE...]`, archMachine, Ryzen 9 5900HX, 3 runs; the jQuery compile time was 19.4 to 19.9 ms, the small cases 0.03 to 0.11 ms). It counts the instructions that the compiler emits (static). It cannot count executed ops, because there is no interpreter yet, so it does not compare with the executed-op histograms of `tools/js/bc_hist.sh`. The comparison is with the static dump of the old compiler that S2.4 made (`/data/bare-tmp/s24/dumps`, 7 programs, functions only, because the old engine runs the script top level in the tree walker). Every function passes the verifier.

| Case | Old words (functions) | New words (functions) | New words (script top level) |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| loopfn | 11 | 12 | 5 |
| calls | 5 | 6 | 20 |
| fib | 14 | 12 | 6 |
| closures | 20 | 16 | 41 |
| objects | 5 | 4 | 61 |
| webpack | 990 | 776 | 241 |
| loop, throws, concat | 0 | 0 | 21, 44, 18 |
| total of the 6 with functions | 1,045 | 826 (-21.0%) | |
| jQuery 3.4.1 minified | 47,934 | 34,678 (-27.7%) | 29 |

- S2.4 estimated 839 to 844 words for the same 6 programs by rewriting the old instructions one to one; the compiler needs 826. For jQuery the estimate was 35,664 to 42,593 words; the compiler gives 34,678, but 88 of 949 functions are partial (see the unsupported list), so this number is a lower bound.
- The 1,214 instructions of the 9 programs (functions and script): `LoadI` 224, `GetField` 121, `CallU` 106, `Mov` 104, `GetGlobal` 86, `Add` 68, `RetUndef` 61, `Closure` 59, `SetGlobal` 57, `Mod` 52. Most `LoadI` and `Mov` are in `webpack`: the arguments of `require(0)` and the window of each call.
- `loopfn` and `calls` get 1 word larger: the modulus 1,000,003 and 65,521 do not fit the immediate, so `LoadI.w` and `Mod` take 3 words where the old `ModK` took 1. The constant is loaded again in each iteration. A `ModK` with a constant table, or hoisting the constant out of the loop, would remove it (not built).
- Compile time of the whole file, pre-parse and parse of each function included: `eval_load` programs 0.03 to 0.09 ms, `webpack` 0.42 ms, jQuery 19.1 ms (949 functions, 33,758 instructions).

Not built (recorded in `Compiled::unsupported`, the code must not run): classes, generators and async functions, `await` and `yield`, spread (calls, arrays, objects), rest parameters, object rest, `arguments`, regexp and BigInt literals, tagged templates, private names, `super`, `new.target`, `import()`, getters and setters and `__proto__` in object literals, `with` and direct `eval`, `delete` of a global name, a named function expression that may use its own name (needs a callee op), and a `break` or `continue` that has no target. jQuery has 88 functions with one of these (58 `arguments`, 28 regexp literals, 2 own-name function expressions, 1 `eval`).

Judgment calls and known gaps:

- `switch` is a chain of compare-jumps, not a table. A jump table needs a new op (a table of jump offsets in `Code`), a verifier change for its successors and an arm in the interpreter (S2.6). Both S2.4 and S2.6 are in other PRs, so I did not add it. The plan lists it for S2.5, so it needs a decision.
- Script-level `var x;` with no initializer emits nothing, so the global is not created. It needs a declare-global op.
- An iterator opened by an array pattern is not closed when a binding throws. A `for-of` closes it. An `IterClose` that throws inside a `for-of` body is caught by the loop's own handler and runs a second time.
- A block-level function in sloppy code is a function-level `var` that is set at the start of the block (Annex B, simplified). Parameters and the function body share one scope.
- `enter` and `find_var` scan the variables of a scope linearly (a test with 70,000 locals took 87 s).
- The root maps list written registers, not live ones, so a dead variable stays a root until its scope ends. Liveness would make maps smaller but the verifier only knows "written".
- `delete a` on a local variable is `false`, and `void e` evaluates `e` for effect.
- `Code::disassemble` (S2.4) writes a space after an op name of 12 or more characters, so `JmpNotNullish r4` is readable.

Not tested: execution of any compiled code (S2.6), so the semantics are checked by reading the disassembly and by the verifier, not by running; Miri; arm64; a modern React bundle; the cost matrix (js2 is not wired into the browser); the compile time of the compiler alone (the example times the pre-parse and parse of each function too).
## 2026-11-20: interpreter for `bare-js2` (plan step S2.6)

Branch `t3/js2-interpreter`. There is no compiler yet (S2.5), so every test and measurement runs bytecode that `Asm` built, and each program goes through `verify` first.

Changes (all in `crates/js2`; `crates/js`, `crates/js-api` and `crates/bare` are untouched):

- `interp.rs`: `Vm`, `Program`, `Exit` and `run`. It has one `loop` with one `match`, one frame record on one `Vec<Value>` stack, and lazy field decode in each arm. `Wide` is a branch before the `match`; both branches run the same arms (the `step!` macro). Calls, returns, closures with contexts (`PushCtx`, `PopCtx`, `GetEnv`, `SetEnv`), jumps and loops (`JmpBack` is the budget and collection point), property get and set, elements, `for-in` over own keys, array iteration, exceptions with handler ranges, and a collection inside a call.
- `interp_rt.rs`: `Realm` (heap, shapes, atoms, globals), the per-realm `Feedback` of each code (one `Cache` of 16 bytes for each site, atoms made canonical for the realm, literal shapes), and the slow paths: property lookup and add, element access, arithmetic and compare for non-number values, `typeof`, equality, string concatenation.
- `object.rs`: a callable flag, `Obj::loc`, `read_loc`, `write_loc`, `set_shape_id`, `from_value_shape`, `is_indexed`, and the `Ctx` record (the parent context in slot 0). A function cell is an object with the hidden slots `code` and `ctx`.
- `asm_util.rs` (test and example helper, included by `#[path]`): an `F` builder over `Asm`, and a `roots` function that computes the live registers at each safepoint.
- Tests: 38 in `interp_tests.rs`. Example `crates/js2/examples/interp_load.rs`: the five micro loops.
- `lib.rs`, `Cargo.toml`, `ci.yml`: `interp_rt` and `interp` are in the list of `unsafe` modules (see below). `lib.rs` has only the two `pub mod` lines and the comment.

Frame record (8 words, `REC`, before register 0): function cell, `this`, current context, `pc` of the call in the caller, `pc` where the caller goes on, code index of the caller (-1 for a frame that the host entered), number of contexts pushed, result register of the caller (bit 24: `New`). A call copies the arguments, gives missing ones `undefined`, and does not fill other registers (the verifier proved write before read). The collector walks the record words and the registers that the root map of the safepoint names. `gate!` runs at the start of each op that allocates, so no collection runs inside an op.

Cache states (design 6.10 item 9): `FRESH` (never ran; the slow path runs, state `SEEN`, no entry) to `SEEN` (second run: the entry is made, state `MONO`) to `MONO` (one entry: shape, place, shape after an add) to `POLY` (2 to 4 entries in a pool, a scan on a miss in the slow path) to `MEGA` (a fifth shape; the record has shape 0 and the lookup runs with no cache work). A set that adds a property is a hit when the new slot is inline. A dictionary shape and a property of the prototype chain never get an entry. A collection that freed a shape (`Shapes::epoch` changed) clears every record.

Measurement. Machine: AMD Ryzen 9 5900HX, Linux, release build. Tool: `tools/js/instr.sh` (perf `instructions:u`, minimum of 3 runs). Each row is the count at N turns minus the count at N = 0 (the setup, which is 0.5 M for the new engine and 2.2 M for the old one). Old engine: the `crates/js` bytecode lane (`Exec::Byte`) at `1a61213f` (the base of this branch, which leaves `crates/js` as on main then), running the JavaScript that `interp_load CASE N --source` prints (one function, locals only, same loop as the hand-written bytecode); a scratch driver, not committed. New engine: `interp_load CASE N`, which checks its result against the same sum in Rust.

| Row | Turns | New instructions per turn | Old instructions per turn | Old / new | New instructions per op | Ops per turn, new / old |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| `loopfn` | 2,000,000 | 292.5 | 398.7 | 1.36 | 41.8 | 7 / 6 |
| `calls` | 1,000,000 | 645.5 | 943.6 | 1.46 | 53.8 | 12 / 11 |
| `fib(30)` | 1,346,269 calls | 985.7 | 1,180.0 | 1.20 | 75.8 | 13 / 11 |
| `closures` | 200,000 | 1,956.2 | 7,011.2 | 3.58 | 78.2 | 25 / 28 |
| `objects` | 1,000,000 | 738.3 | 1,977.1 | 2.68 | 61.5 | 12 / 16 |

- How the loops were matched: the five cases follow the shape of the `eval_load` rows. The JavaScript of each case is the same loop, written once, and the bytecode of the new engine is written by hand for the same loop with the new op set. I did not dump the old compiler's code; I only counted its ops, so the op counts differ (the old op histogram is from the `bc-hist` feature of `bare-js`, run through the scratch driver on the same files: 12.0 M, 11.0 M, 14.8 M, 5.6 M and 16.0 M ops). The sums are the same, and both sides check them. A compiler (S2.5) may emit other code, so these rows measure the interpreter, not a compiler.
- Caveats: the old row counts everything of the old lane (its compile of the source is in the N = 0 setup and is subtracted). The new rows have no built-ins and no `arguments`. `closures` is 3.6 times fewer; the cause is not known (hypothesis: the old lane allocates a context and a closure object in a slower path; not profiled). Wall time was not used. Instruction counts do not show cache misses or branch misses of the dispatch.
- The cost matrix is not applicable: `bare-js2` is not connected to `bare`.

`unsafe` (five places, each with a `SAFETY` comment, listed in `lib.rs`, `Cargo.toml` and `ci.yml`): (1) `r!`, a register with no bounds check; (2) `word!`, an instruction word with no bounds check; (3) the `Op` of the opcode byte as a `transmute`; (4) the cache hit and the element read (`Obj::from_value_shape`, `read_loc`, `write_loc`, `set_shape_id`); (5) the helpers in `interp_rt.rs` that do the same, and the fast path of `Realm::function`. Each of (1) to (3) rests on `verify`. Measured with the safe form of each, the same loops and the same counting: (1) and (2) together save 14% of the instructions (loopfn 18.2%, calls 14.6%, fib 8.3%, closures 8.3%, objects 14.0%); (3) saves another 6.1% to 8.4% (safe versions: `loopfn` 715.0 M against 585.0 M, 781.0 M with (3) also safe). The gains of (4) and (5) were not measured one by one (they hold the safe compare and one pointer load, and a safe form needs a checked cell type that S1.9 does not have).

Tests: `cargo test --locked -p bare-js2`: 166 passed on Linux (38 new in `interp`), and 166 passed on the Windows VM (before the last rebase on main, which added the S2.5 compiler: on Linux `cargo test --locked -p bare-js2` then gave 318 passed) (`cargo xwin test`, MSVC, run through `/data/vms/winssh`). The five micro loops pass their checksums on Windows. Miri (`cargo +nightly miri test --locked -p bare-js2 --lib interp`, 8 test threads, 22 minutes): 37 passed, 1 ignored. The ignored test is `a_long_jump_uses_the_wide_offset` (40,000 words; the liveness pass of the test helper takes over 10 minutes under Miri). Miri found two test problems and no memory error: a small collection trigger in the helper that cleared the caches the cache tests read, and a `powf` that Miri changes by a few ulps on purpose. Both are fixed in the tests. Miri prints three `integer-to-pointer cast` warnings, from `Shapes::finish_marks` in `shapes.rs` (S1.7 code, not changed here). CI runs Miri on the whole crate; I ran it on the `interp` tests only. Clippy (1.96) reports nothing in the new files; it reports `manual_is_multiple_of` in files that this step did not change (`heap.rs`, `bare-os` `pages.rs`, the two census examples), so `-D warnings` fails there before and after this change.

Known gaps (left for S2.5 and S2.7): no prototype-chain cache entries (a property that a prototype gives is looked up each time); no accessors, `ToPrimitive`, `arguments`, generators, iterator protocol beyond arrays, or built-ins; a number prints with Rust's rules, so `1e21` differs; the hidden `code` and `ctx` slots of a function cell show in `for-in` (to fix with the function layout of S2.7).

Not tested: a compiler or real JavaScript on this interpreter (S2.5); the cache-hit and helper `unsafe` against a safe form; wall time; the cost matrix (`bare-js2` is not connected to `bare`); arm64; Miri on the whole crate (only the `interp` tests) and with `-Zmiri-many-seeds`; Windows after the rebase on main and after the last two test edits (Linux was re-run: 318 passed).

### 2026-11-20 (later): the interpreter runs scripts end to end (S2.6, after the merge of #760)

Branch `t3/js2-interpreter` (PR #757). I merged `t3/extend-js2-bytecode-compiler` (#760, not merged to main at that time) into it. The merge did not compile: the `match` in `run` had no arm for the 38 new ops. Each of the 38 ops now has an arm, and no arm is `unreachable!`. `crates/bare`, `crates/js` and `crates/js-api` are untouched.

New and changed code (all in `crates/js2`):

- `interp.rs`: the 38 arms (`DeclGlobal`, `CreateArgs`, `CreateRest`, `LoadCallee`, `LoadNewTarget`, `NewRegExp`, `LoadBigInt`, `GetTemplate`, `ArraySpread`, `ArrayHole`, `CallSpread`, `NewSpread`, `CopyProps`, `ObjRest`, `SetProto`, `DefAccessor`, `DefAccessorElem`, `DefMethod`, `DefMethodElem`, `SetHome`, `MakeClass`, `MakeDerived`, `DefaultCtor`, `SetFields`, `NewPrivateName`, `GetPrivate`, `SetPrivate`, `HasPrivate`, `DefPrivate`, `DefPrivateMethod`, `DefPrivateAccessor`, `GetSuper`, `GetSuperElem`, `SetSuper`, `SetSuperElem`, `CallSuper`, `CallSuperSpread`, `RetDerived`). `GetField`, `GetElem`, `SetField`, `SetElem`, `Closure`, `Call` and `New` now call getters and setters as frames and run constructors and fields.
- Frame record: 10 words (`REC`), was 8. Word 8 is `new.target`. Word 9 is the arguments object (`undefined` when the function does not read `arguments`). The result word has two new flags: `CONSTRUCT` (bit 24) and `AFTER_SUPER` (bit 25). A frame whose call pc is `NOPC` has no root map: it is a base-class constructor that waits below its fields function.
- A base-class constructor runs its fields first. `construct!` pushes the constructor frame and, above it, the fields frame. A derived class runs its fields when `super()` returns (`ret!` with `AFTER_SUPER`).
- `Code::flags` (`CF_ARGS`: the function reads `arguments` or a rest parameter; `CF_LINK`: it uses `super`). `scan_flags` runs in `Vm::new` and spreads `CF_LINK` up through `Code::funcs`. A function cell has 5 hidden slots: `code`, `ctx`, `home`, `fields`, `link`. `link` holds the function and `new.target` that `super()` needs. An arrow takes both from its parent.
- Two synthetic default-constructor codes (`Vm::dctor`). The derived one is `CreateRest`, `CallSuperSpread`, `RetDerived`, with hand-made root maps.
- `interp_rt.rs`: `Got` and `Put` (a property access that must call a getter or a setter), `Slot`, `lookup_g`, `get_prop_g`, `set_prop_g`, `proto_setter`, `fields_of`, the `arguments` shape, and the template cache `Feedback::tmpl`. A class constructor called without `new` throws a TypeError.
- `interp_ops.rs` (new, no `unsafe`): the runtime side of the ops (`make_class`, accessors, private names, `super`, `copy_props`, `obj_rest`, templates, spread).
- `script.rs` (new, no `unsafe`): `script::compile`, `script::load` and `script::run` lex, parse, compile and run a script. `Loader::add` compiles each function when it loads the script, maps `Code::funcs` to program indices by position, and takes the code of a `ready` child from `Compiled::inline`. It stops with an error when the compiler reports an unsupported construct. `Vm::global`, `Vm::global_text` and `Vm::display` read the result.
- `examples/script_run.rs`: runs a file and prints globals, or runs an `eval_load` program with `--eval FILE EXPECTED`.
- `script_tests.rs`: 13 tests that run real JavaScript and check a global: arithmetic and strings, control flow, functions and closures, objects and arrays, exceptions, destructuring, spread and rest, tagged templates, regexp and BigInt (clean TypeError), classes (inheritance, `super`, `new.target`, fields, static blocks), private names and accessors, the load errors of generators, async and `with`, the budget, and a collection stress test. Each case also runs again with a 1 KiB collection trigger (4 KiB under Miri, where only a few programs run under collection).

Two compiler bugs found by these tests, both fixed here (the compiler is #760):

- A tagged template dropped its `${}` values: `tag`a${1}b`` called `tag` with the strings only. `call_parts` now receives the expressions of the template. The golden test `a_tagged_template` held the wrong output (no argument); I changed it.
- A compound assignment to a global (`log += 'f'`) did not name its result register in the root map of the `SetGlobal`. A collection at that point freed the new string. `assign_ident` now marks the register live before the store. The test `a_few_programs_under_constant_collection` has the program that failed.

Interpreter bug found by the same tests: `HasPrivate` read its operands in the wrong order. Fixed.

Tests. Linux: `cargo test --locked -p bare-js2 --lib`: 353 passed, 0 failed (13 of them are the new `script` tests, and `a_tagged_template` has a new golden). Windows (`cargo xwin test`, MSVC, run on the VM through `/data/vms/winssh`): 351 passed, 2 failed. The 2 failures are `parse::tests::corpus_status_matches_acorn` and `parse::lazy_tests::a_lazy_parse_finds_the_same_errors_as_a_full_parse_on_the_corpus`. They read a corpus by a path from the build machine, and the VM has no such path (`NotFound`). They do not touch this change. The first Miri run of the script tests took 29 minutes and failed `arithmetic_and_strings`: Miri adds a random error to the result of `pow`, so `2 ** 3` was 8.000000000000002. Under Miri the tests now skip the cases with `**` and run the collection stress only for a few programs. `cargo clippy --locked -p bare-js2 --all-targets` gives no new warning (the existing ones are in `heap.rs`, `crates/os` and the census examples).

Known gaps (S2.7 or later):

- Missing built-ins: `Object`, `Error` and its subclasses, `Array.prototype` methods (`push`, `forEach`, `bind`), `Function.prototype`, `Math`, `JSON`, `Symbol`, `Map`, `Set`, `Promise`, and the host globals (`self`).
- No `ToPrimitive`: `'' + [1]` and `'' + {}` throw a TypeError. No iterator protocol beyond arrays and strings. A plain function has no `prototype` property, so `class A extends F` with a plain function `F` throws.
- Regexp and BigInt literals, generators, async functions, `with` and direct `eval` are not supported. A literal throws a TypeError when it runs; generators, async functions and `with` stop the load; direct `eval` is not defined at all (`eval` is an undefined global).
- The loader compiles every function when it loads the script (no lazy compile).
- Top-level `let` and `const` are global properties: a `const` at the top level can be assigned, and there is no dead zone at the top level (inside a function or block both work).
- The expression statement `this;` in a derived constructor before `super()` emits no code, so it does not throw. `this.x` does.
- `arguments` is unmapped (a write to `arguments[0]` does not change the parameter).
- A private name is an atom with the text `\0#x\0N`. A script that builds that exact string as a key can forge it. S2.7 should use a symbol cell.
- `CopyProps` (`{...o}`) throws a TypeError for an enumerable accessor (no getter call in the helper yet).
- In strict code, an assignment to a property that has only a getter is ignored with no error.
- An add-transition cache entry can miss a setter that a prototype defines later.

## 2026-11-20: host handlers on the interface, A1b: the call path of a converted call (plan step S0.4 / A1b)

Status: the three rows pass and the full matrix passes. The per-call target (within 10 instructions of the old body) is NOT met: `hcn` +23 and `isc` +33. One design was built, with its levers. The owner decides whether a second design is worth it. Same PR (#758, branch `t3/scope-browser-dom-handlers`).

Owner decision (2026-11-20): a converted host call must cost about the same as the old one. It is in `design-host-handlers.md`, "Decisions".

Changes.

- Arguments are read in place. `call_api_host` copies nothing and pushes nothing for `this` and the arguments. It links a `Win` (`this`, the pointer and length of the caller's `&[Value]`, the previous window) in its own frame. The handles are slot numbers from `1 << 31` up: `this` is `WIN`, argument `i` is `WIN + 1 + i`. `api_at` reads the stack first (one bounds check) and the window second (`api_win`). A slot that names nothing is a panic, never a read outside the slice.
- `undefined`, `null` and `boolean` push nothing. The first four physical slots of the handle stack hold these values, with the slot numbers `u32::MAX - 3` to `u32::MAX`; a pushed slot of logical index `n` is at `n + 4`, so `stack_len` is still 0 for an empty stack. `values` (the roots) skips them. `escape_scope` keeps its slot with `number(0.0)`, which always pushes.
- One scope for each host call. The scope of the bridge is the only one; nothing nests under it.
- `call_api_host` borrows the interface host with a raw pointer instead of an `Rc` clone (SAFETY: `set_host` now asserts that no window is linked, and the `Rc` lives as long as the realm). It saves and restores `host_nt` only when `nt` or the running `host_nt` is set. The error mapping is the cold `api_unerr`.
- `Dom::call_scoped` spells out the hooks of `dispatch_host` in the same order with no closure (the closure environment was built in memory before the branch to the custom element path). `dispatch_host` stays for the old entry.
- `is_connected` takes `s.engine()` once before its loop.
- `bare-js-api` docs: a slot number is private to the engine; `Args` are consecutive slot numbers; arguments and `this` are roots for the whole call. `docs/design-host-interface.md` has the same text. No signature changed.

Rules of design 6.8, and how they hold. A handle into the arguments must not outlive the call: it is a `Local<'s>` of the call's scope, and the borrow checker stops it (the compile-fail tests of `bare-js-api` stand). The stack must not move under it: the arguments are not in the stack; they are the slice that the caller holds (`argv` from `arg_pool`, a bound function's `bargs`), and nothing writes it while the call runs. A collection inside the call must see them as roots: `ApiState::values` walks the chain of windows, so nested host calls keep every outer `this` and argument alive. `Interp::collect` refuses inside a call in this engine, so the tests collect with `Heap::collect(&Interp::roots())`.

Tests (new). `bare-js` `eval_api_tests.rs`: a collection inside a host call keeps `this` and the arguments alive (they are reachable only through the call), nested host calls keep each window a root and restore the outer one, also with `BARE_GC_STRESS`; a handle that names no slot panics. Negative control: with the window removed from `values`, the first two fail. `bare` `browser_scoped_tests.rs`: a converted handler collects while it runs, under `set_gc_stress(true)`, with an argument object and a string alive only through the arguments.

Method. Machine archMachine. Base: origin/main `2c0edc75` (the commit #758 merges), a fresh worktree and target directory; the branch built the same way. Micro-loop `host_call_load` (200,000 calls, `tools/js/instr.sh`, minimum of 3 runs, over the base with 0 calls to cancel start-up). Callgrind: 1 run, 20,000 calls, exclusive cost by function, with `--dump-instr=yes` and a script that sums the cost of each instruction of a function.

Per call over the base (symbol build, 16 codegen units):

| Step | `hcn` | `isc` | `get` | `has` | `match` |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| Head of #758 (reproduced) | +86 | +83 | -91 | -82 | -72 |
| Window, shared constant slots | +72 | +78 | -64 | | |
| `call_scoped` with no closure, no `host_nt` swap when none | +34 | +43 | -85 | -85 | -72 |
| Raw host pointer (no `Rc` clone), cold error mapping | +24 | +32 | -96 | -96 | -84 |
| `is_connected` hoist, final | +23 | +33 | | | |

Split of `hcn` now (callgrind, per call, exclusive, base then branch): `call_api_host` 85 against `call_host` 49 (+36); `call_scoped` 47 against `Host::call` 60 (-13); the handler 74 against 70 (+4); `call_fn_inner` -4. `isc`: the same bridge and `call_scoped`; the handler 125 against 112 (+13: the read of `this` through the window is 10 instructions, then one more in the result). In the 85 of the bridge (disassembly): 6 pushes and 6 pops, the window link and unlink (about 10), the scope (base, store, truncate: about 11), the `Local` to `Value` read of the result (about 12), the dynamic call setup. What is left is the price of the contract (a window, a scope, a handle result), not an unnecessary step. Tried and reverted: a table for the shared slots read in the bridge (+3), which was worse.

Rows. `codegen-units=1` on both trees (glibc, minimum of 3 runs): `browser_load rel 10` +0.314% (was +0.655%), `rel 1` +0.221% (+0.539%), `svg 10` +0.365% (+0.528%), `svg 1` +0.333%, `svgparse 1` +0.351%, `svgparse 10` +0.179%. The jemalloc run was skipped (no row over the limit). Default flags, the full matrix (`tools/js/cost_matrix.sh -j4`, 817 rows, glibc, jemalloc only for a row over the limit): mean -0.017% glibc and -0.023% (5 rows) jemalloc; no row over +0.5% under both allocators. Over under glibc only (jemalloc under +0.001%): `resources_load small 10` +1.739% (glibc-only noise, known), `interact_load asyncpriv 1` +0.771% and `10` +0.529%, `gen_load finally 1` +0.583% and `10` +0.501%. The three rows at default flags: `rel 10` +0.255%, `rel 1` +0.188%, `svg 10` +0.213%. `parse_load deep 1` and `10` do not run on the base tree either.

Tests. Linux: `cargo test --locked -p bare-js-api -p bare-js -p bare --lib`: 32, 1103 (1 ignored) and 1714 (6 ignored) pass. `bare --lib` filters `domexc exception dom attr custom mutation scoped` (128 pass, 1 ignored): pass plain, with `BARE_GC_STRESS=1` and with `BARE_ALL_API=1`. `bare-js` filter `api_tests` (45): pass plain and with `BARE_GC_STRESS=1`. Windows 11 VM (`cargo xwin test --no-run`, exes through `winssh`): `bare-js-api` 32 pass, `bare-js` filter `api_tests` 45 pass, `bare` the same filters 128 pass.

Levers left, not built (each saves a few instructions, none reaches 10): no `RefCell` borrow of `Dom::scoped` (about 5), a fast read of `this` first in `api_win` (about 3 for a handler that reads only `this`), a window that stores `this` by pointer (about 2). A design that removes the window link, the scope or the result read needs a different contract (for example a handler that returns a raw immediate); I did not build one.

Not tested: `BARE_GC_STRESS=1` with the whole `bare --lib` run; the unfiltered `bare-js` and `bare` runs on Windows; jemalloc for the six `codegen-units=1` rows; RSS and wall time; a panic inside a host call (the window stays linked; no code uses the realm after a panic); `bare-js2` (it has no `Engine` yet).
## 2026-11-20: compiler gaps and more constructs in js2 (plan step S2.5)

This entry continues "compiler in js2 (plan step S2.5)". Base: main with #759. New module `compile_class.rs`. The compiler is not wired into the browser, so there is no cost matrix.

Four gaps are fixed:

- A script-level `var x;` and each function name of a script now emit `DeclGlobal` (new op, one site). Before, `var x;` made no global.
- An array pattern closes its iterator when a binding throws (a handler on the pieces of code between the `IterNext` calls, and a cold block after the last `RetUndef` that runs `IterClose` and throws again). A throw from `next()` does not close it. A pattern whose bindings cannot throw (registers, literal defaults) has no handler.
- An `IterClose` that a `break` or `return` repeats inside a `for-of` body is now outside the range of the loop's own handler, so it runs once. A frame keeps a list of pieces; `pause` and `resume` cut the repeated code out.
- `enter` and `find_var` use a hash index for a scope or a level with more than 8 names. A scope with 20,000 locals compiled in 960 ms before and in 29 ms now. A scope with 70,000 locals is refused at once with `Limit` (a function has at most 65,535 registers; the test checks that it fails in under 20 s, it took 87 s to compile before).

Constructs that are built now. All are compiler only. Each compiled function passes the verifier:

- `arguments` (`CreateArgs` at entry, before the defaults), rest parameters (`CreateRest`), a spread in calls, `new` and array literals (`CallSpread`, `NewSpread`, `ArraySpread`, `ArrayHole`), an array hole, object spread (`CopyProps`), object rest in patterns (`ObjRest`; the keys of the other properties go to a window).
- Named function expressions that use their own name (`LoadCallee`; a variable in the function, in a slot when a closure captures it).
- Getters, setters and `__proto__` in object literals (`DefAccessor`, `DefAccessorElem`, `SetProto`). A method that uses `super` gets `SetHome`, and then the literal is not `NewObjLit`.
- Regexp and BigInt literals (`NewRegExp`, `LoadBigInt`), tagged templates (`GetTemplate`, the template object is cached by site).
- `new.target` (`LoadNewTarget`; an arrow takes it from a variable of the function around it).
- `super.x`, `super[x]`, assignments and updates of them, `super(...)` (also in an arrow), derived constructors (`this` is the hole until `super()` returns; `RetDerived` on each return).
- Private names: `#x` reads, writes, updates, `#x in o`, private methods and accessors, static ones too.
- Classes: methods, getters, setters, static members, computed keys, fields, static fields, `static { }`, a class name binding inside the class, class declarations and expressions.

How I ranked. I counted the functions that each construct made partial in 6 files (jQuery 3.4.1, axios, lodash, react-dom production, the clangd extension bundle, tauri's bundle; `/data/bare-tmp/s25b/corpus`, not in the repository), with the compiler before this change: `arguments` 158, regexp literal 123, class 85, spread and rest 74 (calls 18, arrays 5, object spread 8, rest parameter 20, `spread` expression 20, object rest 3), own-name function expression 18, getter, setter or `__proto__` in a literal 7, BigInt 0, tagged template 0. The eval_load cases use none of them. I built them in the order of the dependencies, not of the counts: `arguments` and rest first, then regexp, own name, spread, accessors, and classes last because they need most of the new ops. BigInt and tagged templates are cheap and are built, but no file in the corpus uses them.

Result of `bc_hist` on the 6 files (archMachine, release build, same binary before and after except for this change):

| File | Functions (partial) before | Functions (partial) after | Still partial because |
| --- | ---: | ---: | --- |
| jQuery 3.4.1 | 949 (88) | 949 (1) | direct `eval` |
| axios | 422 (56) | 423 (0) | |
| lodash | 691 (29) | 691 (0) | |
| react-dom | 493 (8) | 493 (0) | |
| clangd bundle | 3,197 (351) | 5,340 (275) | async 98, generators 18, `await` 144, `yield` 24, `for await` 1, `eval` 1 |
| tauri bundle | 122 (11) | 425 (23) | async 10, `await` 16 |

The function counts of clangd and tauri grow because the compiler now reaches the methods of the classes that it did not compile before. The jQuery numbers: words 34,678 to 34,739, instructions 33,758 to 33,789, registers 8,677 to 8,727, root-map bytes 261,168 to 263,664 (the 87 new complete functions). jQuery compile time, 3 runs: 19.1 to 19.55 ms at the start of the task, 18.9 to 19.2 ms after the scope index, 18.97 to 19.11 ms with all constructs (the old binary in the same session: 18.86 to 19.07 ms). So the scope index and the new code do not change the time for real code. The nine eval_load sources are still complete.

New ops (38). The format is in `bytecode.rs`; each has a line there that says what the interpreter (S2.6) must do:

| Group | Ops |
| --- | --- |
| Globals | `DeclGlobal` |
| Frame | `CreateArgs`, `CreateRest`, `LoadCallee`, `LoadNewTarget` |
| Literals | `NewRegExp`, `LoadBigInt`, `GetTemplate` |
| Spread and rest | `ArraySpread`, `ArrayHole`, `CallSpread`, `NewSpread`, `CopyProps`, `ObjRest` |
| Objects | `SetProto`, `DefAccessor`, `DefAccessorElem`, `DefMethod`, `DefMethodElem`, `SetHome` |
| Classes | `MakeClass`, `MakeDerived`, `DefaultCtor`, `SetFields` |
| Private names | `NewPrivateName`, `GetPrivate`, `SetPrivate`, `HasPrivate`, `DefPrivate`, `DefPrivateMethod`, `DefPrivateAccessor` |
| Super | `GetSuper`, `GetSuperElem`, `SetSuper`, `SetSuperElem`, `CallSuper`, `CallSuperSpread`, `RetDerived` |

`verify.rs` knows the register windows of the new ops (`CallSpread` 3, `NewSpread` 2, `ObjRest` x, `CallSuper` c). A `GetTemplate` recipe may hold `u32::MAX` as the cooked string (a bad escape), and its length must be even. A `RetDerived` and a `CallSuper` need no new rule.

Class design (`compile_class.rs`):

- A scope holds the inner class name and the names that the class makes: `#x` (the private name object that `NewPrivateName` makes, one per evaluation of the class), `%k<i>` (the key of a computed field), `%m#x`, `%g#x`, `%s#x` (the function of an instance private method, getter, setter). They are no identifiers, so the facts do not list them. `captured` puts each one in a context slot, and a method reads it through the chain.
- The constructor is a closure or `DefaultCtor`. `MakeClass` or `MakeDerived` gives it a prototype. A method, getter or setter is defined on the prototype or on the constructor (`DefMethod`, `DefAccessor` with bit 1 set: not enumerable). A private static method goes on the constructor at once.
- The text of a field initializer or a `static { }` block is in the tree of the function that holds the class. The facts have an entry for each (flag `INLINE`), but a later parse cannot find a body to skip. So the parent compiles them itself with a second `Fc` over the same tree: one synthetic function for all instance fields and private methods, and one for each static field or static block. Each is a child with `Child::ready = Some(i)`, and its code is `Compiled::inline[i]`. `compile_all` takes the code from there; the driver of S2.6 must do the same when it first runs such a child. The id of a synthetic function is the id of its first initializer entry.
- `SetFields ctor, fn` stores the fields function on the constructor. The interpreter runs it with `this` set to the new object: at the start of a constructor of a base class (the constructor has no op for it), and in `CallSuper` and `CallSuperSpread` after the parent constructor returns. The static functions are called once, in the order of the text, with `this` set to the constructor, after the inner name is set.

Deviations and known gaps (the interpreter or a later step must decide):

- `arguments` is not mapped to the parameters in sloppy code (writing `arguments[0]` does not change the parameter).
- Assigning to the own name of a named function expression assigns in sloppy code; the spec ignores it. In strict code it throws.
- A second `super()` is not detected; the spec throws a ReferenceError. The message for `this` before `super()` is the one of `CheckInit` with the name `this`.
- An arrow gets its home object from the function that makes it (S2.6: `Closure` copies it); the compiler emits `SetHome` only for a method, an accessor, a field function and a static function.
- `ObjRest` takes its keys from a window that holds atoms (names), numbers (index keys) or the result of `ToKey` (computed keys). The interpreter must compare them as property keys.
- No op sets the `name` or `length` of a method, an accessor, a class constructor or an anonymous function in a field. The class constructor is a normal closure.
- `static` private methods and instance ones use the same ops on a different object; the brand check is in the interpreter.
- A BigInt key (`{1n: x}`) and a private key in an object literal or a pattern are still listed as unsupported.
- Class name reads inside the class use `GetCtxTdz` (a hole check on each read), because the name is a `const` that is not set until the class is done.

Not built, design only. Each needs an interpreter change, and none is cheap enough to build now.

- Generators. A generator function compiles like a normal function. Its first call makes the generator object from the frame (`Code` has the same root maps at each suspend point). New op `Yield a, b`: store the pc and the registers, give `b` to the caller; when it resumes, `a` gets the sent value. A `throw(e)` resumes by throwing `e` at the `Yield`, so the existing handlers work. A `return(v)` resumes by throwing a sentinel (a `GeneratorReturn` record that holds `v`). The compiler's `finally` already runs on a throw and rethrows, so the finalizers run; the interpreter ends the generator with `v` when the sentinel leaves the function. `yield*` is one op `YieldDelegate a, b`: it keeps its pc until the inner iterator is done, and passes `next`, `throw` and `return` to it.
- Async functions. The same frame save as a generator, with `Await a, b` in place of `Yield`: the interpreter subscribes the resume to the promise in `b`. A rejection resumes by throwing at the `Await`. `Ret` resolves the promise. An async generator has both ops and a queue of requests. `for await` is `IterOpen` with a flag, then `IterNext` split in a call, an `Await` and a result check; `IterClose` awaits too.
- `with`. `PushWith r` puts the object `r` on the context chain as a level of a new kind. Inside the body, and in each function with the flag `IN_WITH`, a name that is not declared inside the `with` compiles to `GetName a, site, hops` (and `SetName`, `TypeofName`, `CallName` for the `this` of a call): it looks in each object level from the innermost out to `hops` (`Symbol.unscopables` included), then falls back to the slot or the global. `PopCtx` leaves it.
- Direct `eval`. A function with the flag `EVAL` or `INNER_EVAL` already keeps all variables in context slots. Two things are missing: a table in `Code` with the names, slots and kinds of each `PushCtx` (so that the interpreter can build the `Level` chain for the compiler at run time), and `CallEval a, base, n` (a call that checks whether the callee is the real `eval`). A sloppy `var` from the eval goes to a variable object that the function makes at entry (`PushVarEnv`), and the names of such a function that no scope declares are looked up in it first, as in `with`.

Check. `cargo test --locked -p bare-js2 --lib`: 282 pass on Linux (260 on main). `compile::tests`: 54 (34 on main): 14 new golden tests (one for each of: `arguments`, rest and spread call, spread in `new` and arrays, own-name function expression, regexp and BigInt, tagged template, object accessors and `__proto__` and spread, object rest, class with fields and static members, derived class with `super()` in an arrow, `super` property access, private names, `new.target`, class expression name), `field_initializers_and_static_blocks_are_ready_children_of_the_class`, `every_construct_of_a_class_passes_the_verifier` (12 sources), the gaps (script var, iterator close, `break` closes once, 60,000 locals in linear time), and the updated list of unsupported constructs (async, generator, `with`, direct eval, `delete` of a global). I read each golden against the JS meaning. Windows 11 VM: the whole lib run is 280 pass and 2 fail (the same two parser corpus tests as before: `parse::tests::corpus_status_matches_acorn` and `parse::lazy_tests::a_lazy_parse_finds_the_same_errors_as_a_full_parse_on_the_corpus`; they do not find the corpus on the VM); `compile::tests` 54 pass. `cargo clippy -p bare-js2 --all-targets`: no warning in the files of this change (old warnings remain in `heap.rs`, `object_census.rs` and `bare-os`).

Not tested: running any compiled code, so the semantics of the 38 new ops are checked by reading the disassembly and by the verifier only; class, `super`, private-name and spread behavior in an interpreter (S2.6); the S2.6 driver's use of `Child::ready`; mapped `arguments`; function names of methods and classes; Miri; arm64; a React bundle with classes beyond the clangd and tauri bundles; the cost matrix (js2 is not wired into the browser); the `bc_hist` example on Windows.

## 2026-11-20: core built-ins in js2 (plan step S2.7)

Real scripts now run end to end on the js2 interpreter. This step adds `Object`, `Function.prototype`, `Error` and its subclasses, `ToPrimitive`, `Array`, `String.prototype`, `Number`, `Boolean`, `Math`, `parseInt`, `parseFloat`, `isNaN`, `isFinite`, `globalThis` and `self`. Base: PR #757 (`t3/js2-interpreter`), merged with the newest main.

New files in `crates/js2/src`: `builtins.rs` (the native-call design, `Object`, `Function`, `Error`, `ToPrimitive`), `bi_array.rs`, `bi_string.rs`, `bi_number.rs` (`Number`, `Boolean`, `Math`, the global functions) and `prelude.js`.

Design:

- A native function is a cell with the flag `F_NATIVE` and the shape `s_native`. Slot 0 is an index in `Realm::natives`. The type is `fn(&mut Realm, this, &[Value]) -> R<Value>`. `Realm::function` skips natives, so the hot call path is the same as before. A call to a native is the `else` branch of `call!` and of the three other call ops.
- A native never collects and never calls a script function. `gate!()` runs before the native, so every value that the native holds is on the stack and rooted.
- A built-in that calls back (`forEach`, `map`, `filter`, `reduce`, `some`, `every`, `find`, `findIndex`, `sort`, `Array.from`, `replace` with a function) is written in JavaScript in `prelude.js`. The prelude compiles with each script and runs once at setup. Its helper `__def` defines a hidden method and is deleted from the global afterwards. This needs no re-entry of `Vm::run` from a native.
- `call`, `apply` and `bind` return `Outcome::Enter` (the "tail channel"): the interpreter pushes the frame of the target. A bound function is a native cell with the target, `this` and the argument array in slots 1 to 3.
- A plain function gets its `prototype` object on first read (a hook in `lookup` and `get_prop_g`). A function that nobody reads makes no extra object.
- `Error` objects have one prototype for each kind. `message` and `name` are hidden properties of the prototype. The engine throws `TypeError`, `ReferenceError`, `RangeError` and `SyntaxError` objects, so `e instanceof TypeError` works.
- `ToPrimitive` and `OrdinaryToPrimitive` are in `to_number`, `to_str`, `add_slow`, `compare` and `loose_eq`. They call only native `valueOf` and `toString`. A depth guard of 100 stops a cycle with a `RangeError`.
- A method on a string, number or boolean value looks up `string_proto`, `number_proto` or `boolean_proto`. No wrapper object is made.
- `class X extends Error` and `class X extends Array` work: `CallSuper` on a native parent runs `construct_native`, then the fields function of the class.

Acceptance. The four `eval_load` programs give the same result on js2 (`script_run --eval`) and on the old engine (`eval_load CASE 1`, checksum ok):

| Case | Old engine | js2 |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `closures` | 23222546 | 23222546 |
| `objects` | 19442497,119979 | 19442497,119979 |
| `throws` | 69629 | 69629 |
| `webpack` | 3890,150,50 | 3890,150,50 |

Cost of the interpreter hot loop. `interp_load`, release build, `perf stat -e instructions:u` with `GLIBC_TUNABLES=glibc.malloc.tcache_count=65535`, archMachine, 3 runs for each row. The three runs give the same count (spread 0). Net instructions = count(N) - count(0), in millions. "Base" is the tree of #757 without this change.

| Row | N | Base (cgu 16) | New (cgu 16) | Change | Base (cgu 1) | New (cgu 1) | Change |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| `loopfn` | 1,000,000 | 314.5 | 313.5 | -0.3% | 311.5 | 311.5 | 0.0% |
| `calls` | 1,000,000 | 692.5 | 685.5 | -1.0% | 693.5 | 695.5 | +0.3% |
| `fib` | 30 | 1391.7 | 1425.4 | +2.4% | 1417.3 | 1449.6 | +2.3% |
| `closures` | 200,000 | 412.8 | 411.6 | -0.3% | 417.3 | 418.3 | +0.2% |
| `objects` | 200,000 | 152.2 | 152.9 | +0.5% | 155.1 | 155.3 | +0.1% |

Setup of a `Vm` (count(0)): 0.53 to 0.72 M before, 0.76 to 0.95 M after. The extra 0.23 M is the install of the built-ins and the compile of the prelude.

`fib` is over the +0.5% bound at both codegen-unit settings. What I found (hypothesis for the cause, measured for the rest):

- `callgrind` on the release binaries with symbols (`fib 26`): 207.4 M instructions before, 212.3 M after. `Realm::function` costs the same in both (10,999,408 instructions, one call for each `fib` call). No native function runs in `fib`, and `native_id` is never called.
- The extra 4.9 M instructions (about 12 for each `fib` call) are spread over `Vm::run` in many lines (`Value::kind`, option matches, a jump-table label). I did not find one added instruction. Hypothesis: the new cold branches in `Vm::run` change the register allocation and the block layout of the hot ops.
- I tried three changes. (1) One `enter!` for all call kinds (a tuple from `native_call!`): `fib` +5.8% at cgu 1, worse. (2) No native branch in `call!` (an experiment only): `calls` equals base, `fib` +1.9%, so the call op is not the cause. (3) `#[inline(never)]` on `call_native` and `construct_native`: no change. The code in the PR is the first form.
- This row needs an owner decision under the cgu rule: it is still over at `codegen-units=1`, and I found no new work on its path.

Tests. `cargo test --locked -p bare-js2 --lib`: 362 pass on Linux (353 before this step, 9 new). Windows (`cargo xwin test`, run on the VM): 360 pass and 2 fail. The 2 failures are the known corpus-path tests (`parse::tests::corpus_status_matches_acorn` and `parse::lazy_tests::a_lazy_parse_finds_the_same_errors_as_a_full_parse_on_the_corpus`). Clippy on the crate: no warning in the new files. The warnings that remain are in `heap.rs`, `crates/os/src/pages.rs` and the census examples (not changed here).

New tests in `script_tests.rs`, one for each group. Each runs normally and under constant collection (`check`): `object_and_object_prototype`, `function_prototype_and_plain_function_prototypes`, `errors_and_their_subclasses`, `to_primitive`, `array_constructor_and_methods`, `string_prototype`, `number_boolean_math_and_global_functions`, `eval_load_programs_give_the_result_of_the_old_engine` (the 4 programs above) and `built_ins_survive_constant_collection_with_many_live_values`. Under Miri a group runs only its first 3 cases.

Known gaps:

- `Object.freeze` does not make the object non-extensible (there is no `preventExtensions`), and the elements of a frozen array stay writable. So `Object.isFrozen({})` is `true`; the spec says `false`.
- An `Array` method works on an array or an `arguments` object. A generic array-like gives a `TypeError`. `shift` and `unshift` are O(n).
- `ToPrimitive` calls only native `valueOf` and `toString`. An object with a `valueOf` or `toString` written in the script gives a `TypeError` in `+`, `==` and `String(x)`. This needs a re-entry of the interpreter from a native; it is the next step to design.
- No wrapper objects: `new String`, `new Number` and `new Boolean` throw. `Function(...)` throws. There is no `Symbol`, `Map`, `Set`, `JSON`, `Date`, `Promise`, `RegExp` or `Error.stack`.
- `String.prototype.replace` and `replaceAll` take a string pattern (or a function replacer through the prelude). A regexp pattern is not supported.
- The prelude compiles with each script. A cache of the compiled prelude across scripts is not built.

Not tested: Miri on the new code; arm64 and macOS; the new built-ins on real sites (only the 4 `eval_load` programs and the unit tests run them); `sort` on arrays larger than the unit tests (about 10 elements); `Math.random` quality; wall time (instruction counts only); a call of `Vm::run` from a native, because none exists; the `webpack` case under the cost rule on other scales than 1.
## 2026-11-20: switch jump tables in js2 (follow-up of S2.5 and S2.6)

Branch `t3/js2-switch-jump-tables`, on `t3/js2-interpreter` (PR #757, `9934d6d0`). Task: a `switch` whose cases are all integer constants or all string constants compiles to one table op, not a chain of compare-jumps. The chain stays when it is cheaper.

### Design (written before the code)

What other engines do (read in their sources on 2026-11-20, `main` of each; not in this repository):

| Engine | Integers | Strings | Where the table is |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| V8 (Ignition) | `SwitchOnSmiNoFeedback` when there are at least 6 Smi cases (`switch_table_min_cases`) and the spread is below 3 times the number of clauses (`switch_table_spread_threshold`). Before the op, bytecode checks that the value is a number in the Smi range and that `x\|0 === x`. Other cases stay a compare chain, behind the table. | A compare chain. | A jump table in the constant pool: base value, size, one target per value. |
| JSC | `switch_imm` for 3 or more cases. A dense table when the range is at most 1000 and range / cases is below 15; else a sorted list. Any non-constant case turns the table off. | `switch_string`: a hash map from the string to the offset, for 3 or more cases. | Side tables of the code block (`UnlinkedSimpleJumpTable`, `UnlinkedStringSwitchJumpTable`). |
| QuickJS (quickjs-ng) | No table op. The code is `dup`, the case, `strict_eq`, `if_true` for each case. | The same. | — |

Choice:

1. Integers: a dense table, like V8 and JSC. A sparse switch keeps the chain. A sorted list with binary search (JSC's second form) is not built: a case set that is both large and sparse is rare, and the chain is correct for it.
2. Strings: a hash table keyed by the 32-bit string hash. A sorted table with binary search would compare string content in each step, and a compare of a rope or of a string of another width is the expensive part of a chain step today. The hash is cached in the string cell (`Str::hash`), and an atom has it from the start. One probe and one equality test replace the whole chain. A discriminant that is not an atom pays one hash of its units the first time (O(length)); the cell caches it.
3. Both are one op each: `SwitchI a, t` and `SwitchA a, t`. `a` is the register of the discriminant and `t` is the offset of the table in the word pool `Code::tables`.
4. The table does not live in the instruction stream. `decode` and the verifier keep fixed-size instructions. A jump table needs no `Wide` form. The targets are absolute `pc`s (not offsets): the compiler fills them after the assembler fixed the widths, and the interpreter sets `pc` from the table with no add.
5. Semantics:
   - The discriminant is evaluated once, before the table (as before). Every case is a constant, so no case expression can have a side effect and no order of evaluation can be seen. A switch with one case that is not a constant, or two kinds of constants, keeps the whole chain.
   - The bodies stay in source order, so fallthrough and `default` in any position are unchanged. The table holds the target of each value, and `default` (or the end of the switch) for the gaps and for a value that no case has.
   - Duplicate case values: the first case wins, as in a chain. The later duplicate keeps its body (it can be reached by fallthrough) and no table entry.
   - `===` on integers: an `Int` value indexes the table. A double that is an integer value in the 32-bit range (`3.0`, `-0`) indexes it too, since `-0 === 0`. A NaN, a fraction, a value out of range, and any non-number go to `default`: a string `"1"` never matches `case 1`. A case written `-0` is not an integer constant for the compiler (`int_const`), so a switch that has it keeps the chain.
   - A string discriminant that is a rope is flattened by `Str::hash`, as `===` does today.

Memory layout. `Code::tables: Vec<u32>`, one pool for all the tables of a function. Each table starts at the offset in the op:

| Table | Words |
| --- | --- |
| Integer | `lo` (as `u32`), `default`, `len`, then `len` targets. The target of `v` is `targets[v - lo]`. |
| String | `default`, `mask`, then `mask + 1` slots of 3 words: `hash`, `atom`, `target`. An empty slot has `atom = u32::MAX`. The first probe is `hash & mask`; the next is the slot after (linear probing). |

A string table has a power of two slots, with at least 4/3 slots for each case (a load of at most 3/4), so a probe ends at an empty slot. The verifier checks this. (The first draft said 1.5 slots. A 3-case switch then took 8 slots, 26 words, against 7 words for the chain. 4 slots take 14 words.)

Thresholds (the V8 and JSC rules were the start; the numbers of this engine are measured below):

- Integers: at least 3 distinct values (`MIN_INT_CASES`), and `span < 3 * cases` where `span = max - min + 1` (`INT_SPAN`, V8's spread rule). The table has at most 3 words for each case, plus 3 words of header; a chain has 2 words for each case.
- Strings: at least 3 distinct strings (`MIN_STR_CASES`).

Check, defined before the code:

- Compile golden tests: the disassembly of a dense integer switch, a string switch, a small switch (chain), a sparse switch (chain), a mixed one (chain), a case with a side effect (chain), `default` in the middle, and duplicate values.
- Verifier: accepts what the compiler makes; rejects a table out of the pool, a target that is not an instruction or that goes back, a string table with no empty slot, a slot with an atom out of range or a wrong hash, and a table length that disagrees with the pool.
- Script tests (`check`: each runs normally and under constant collection): dense, sparse, strings, `default` in the middle, fallthrough, `-0`, NaN, a double that is an integer, a number against a string, a rope as the discriminant, duplicates, a `break` out of nested `switch` and loops, a `let` in a case. Each result equals what the chain gives (the old compiler's result, by reading the source and by running the same program with a case made non-constant).
- Measure: a 16-case integer switch and an 8-case string switch in a loop, instructions before and after, 3 runs; the loops `loopfn` and `fib` must not move.

### Result

Changes (all in `crates/js2`): `bytecode.rs` (the ops `SwitchI` and `SwitchA`, the letter `T`, `Code::tables`, `int_table`, `str_table`, `switch_targets`, and a table line under the op in `disassemble`), `verify.rs` (`check_table`, and the table targets as successors in the data flow), `compile.rs` (`reach`: the label bookkeeping of a forward jump, taken out of `jump_ins`; `tables` and `table_fix`, which `finish` fills with the `pc` of each label), `compile_stmt.rs` (`table_plan`, `switch_table`), `interp.rs` (the two arms, and the helpers `switch_int` and `switch_str`). `interp_rt.rs` and `script.rs` are untouched.

Two choices that the measurement changed:

- `switch_str` is a function that is not inlined in `run`. With the probe written inside the `SwitchA` arm, the string rows were 4% cheaper, but `fib` cost +1.74% (1,391.70 M to 1,415.93 M) and `calls` +0.43%, for code that has no `switch`. Out of line, `fib` is +0.19% and `calls` is -0.43%. Hypothesis (not profiled): the larger `run` changed its register allocation. A fast path in line for an atom that sits in its first slot gave only 5 instructions per turn back and was not kept. `switch_int` is a few instructions and stays in line (a call for it changed nothing in the plain rows).
- The threshold of 3 cases for both kinds. With 2 cases the table gives no gain (integers: 278.0 against 277.4 instructions per turn; strings: 404.0 against 407.5, and 14 words of table against 5 words of chain; both measured with the first build, where `SwitchA` was in line, which is cheaper than the final one). With 3 cases the table wins (rows below).

Measurement. Machine: archMachine (AMD Ryzen 9 5900HX, Linux, load average 5 to 6 from other jobs, so only instruction counts are used). Build: release, `cargo build --locked --release -p bare-js2 --example script_run --example interp_load`. Tool: `perf stat -e instructions:u`, with `GLIBC_TUNABLES=glibc.malloc.tcache_count=65535` as in `tools/js/instr.sh`. Before: `t3/js2-interpreter` `9934d6d0`. After: this branch. Each switch row is a JavaScript function with a loop of 1,000,000 turns and the `switch` in the loop body, run by `script_run`; the row is (count at 1,000,000 turns - count at 0 turns) / 1,000,000, so the setup (compile of the script) is out. The value is the discriminant of each turn cycling over the cases (`i & 15`, `ks[i & 7]` for strings from an array literal, so each is an atom). 3 runs each. The counts are almost exactly the same in each run: the spread is at most 0.1 instruction per turn (the table shows the three runs). The sources are made by a script in the session scratch directory (not in the repository); `int16` is the `switch (i & 15)` with 16 cases of `s += k + 1; break;` and a `default`.

| Row | Before (instructions per turn, 3 runs) | After | Change | Path after |
| --- | --- | --- | ---: | --- |
| `int16`: 16 integer cases, dense | 508.5, 508.5, 508.5 | 278.0, 278.0, 278.0 | -45.3% | `SwitchI` |
| `int4`: 4 cases | 310.5, 310.4, 310.5 | 278.0, 277.9, 278.0 | -10.5% | `SwitchI` |
| `int3`: 3 cases, `i % 3` | 302.0, 302.0, 301.9 | 286.0, 286.0, 286.0 | -5.3% | `SwitchI` |
| `int2`: 2 cases | 277.4, 277.5, 277.5 | 277.0, 277.0, 277.0 | -0.2% | chain (same bytecode) |
| `intsparse`: 8 cases, 1 to 10,000,000 | 474.5, 474.4, 474.4 | 471.0, 471.0, 471.0 | -0.7% | chain (same bytecode) |
| `str8`: 8 string cases | 706.0, 705.9, 706.0 | 432.4, 432.5, 432.5 | -38.7% | `SwitchA` |
| `str4`: 4 cases | 523.4, 523.5, 523.5 | 432.5, 432.5, 432.5 | -17.4% | `SwitchA` |
| `str3`: 3 cases | 472.0, 471.9, 472.0 | 443.6, 443.6, 443.6 | -6.0% | `SwitchA` |
| `str2`: 2 cases | 407.5, 407.5, 407.5 | 406.5, 406.5, 406.5 | -0.2% | chain (same bytecode) |
| `str8fresh`: 8 cases, the discriminant `'k' + (i & 7)` is a new string each turn | 2,245.2 (3 runs equal) | 1,310.8 (3 runs equal) | -41.6% | `SwitchA` |

The rows with the chain after have the same bytecode as before. Their change of -0.2% and -0.7% comes from the interpreter (I did not look for the cause; hypothesis: code layout). `str8fresh` is the worst case for the hash (a discriminant that has no hash yet: one hash of 2 units, then the compare), and it is still 41.6% below the chain, because each step of the chain flattens and compares the new string.

The plain loops of `interp_load` (no `switch`). Delta of the count at N turns and at the setup, 3 runs, in M instructions; the 3 runs differ by at most 0.003 M:

| Row | Before | After | Change |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| `loopfn` 2,000,000 | 629.00 | 629.00 | +0.00% |
| `fib(30)` | 1,391.70 | 1,394.39 | +0.19% |
| `calls` 1,000,000 | 692.50 | 689.50 | -0.43% |
| `closures` 200,000 | 412.84 | 412.44 | -0.10% |
| `objects` 1,000,000 | 763.29 | 762.29 | -0.13% |

No plain row is over +0.5%. They move with the code layout of `run`, not with a `switch` (none of these loops has one). I did not repeat them with `codegen-units=1`.

Size. Words of the function (instruction words, then the words of `Code::tables`), chain against table: `int16` 74 against 42 + 19 = 61; `int4` 26 against 18 + 7 = 25; `int3` 22 against 16 + 6 = 22; `str8` 52 against 36 + 50 = 86; `str4` 32 against 24 + 26 = 50; `str3` 27 against 21 + 14 = 35. An integer table is smaller than the chain from 4 cases on. A string table is larger: 3 words in each of the slots, and the slots are at most 3/4 full. A 2-word slot (the hash read from the atom cell) would save a third; not built, since it adds a load for each probe.

Tests. `cargo test --locked -p bare-js2 --lib`: 367 pass on Linux (353 before), 14 new:

- `compile` (4): the goldens `switch_with_integer_cases_is_a_jump_table` (fallthrough, `break`, `default` before the last case, a gap; and the words of the pool), `switch_with_string_cases_is_a_hash_table` (and the size of the pool), `a_duplicate_case_gets_no_table_entry`; and `a_switch_keeps_the_chain_when_it_is_cheaper_or_cannot_be_a_table` (25 sources: the minimum of 3 cases, duplicates, the span at its limit, negative values and the top of the 32-bit range, a case that is a variable, a call, a sum, `1.5`, `-0`, a string among integers, `null`, `true` and `undefined`, and `default` anywhere). Every function passes the verifier.
- `verify` (3): a table passes and its targets are the successors (the data flow finds a read of a register that a target path did not write); 15 bad integer tables (pool too short, empty, a target in the middle of a wide instruction, a target that goes back, a target past the end, a table past the largest integer, an offset that names no table, a register out of range); a string table passes and 8 bad ones (slot count not a power of two, cut off, no empty slot, an atom out of range, a wrong hash, a bad target, a bad default, a slot that its own probe cannot find).
- `script` (7): the tests run each program with the table and with the chain (every `case X:` changed to `case (void 0, X):`, which is not a constant, and the test checks that the table version has a table op and the chain version has none), normally and under constant collection. They cover a dense switch with `default` in the middle and fallthrough over 25 values (ints, `1.0`, `6 / 2`, `-0`, NaN, `1.5`, `2^31`, `1e300`, `Infinity`, `'1'`, `null`, `undefined`, booleans, an object), negative values and the top of the range, strings of one byte and of two bytes (`é`, `日本`, the empty string, new strings made by `+`), a rope of 66 units as the discriminant, 40 cases of each kind with each key and 5 misses (the string table has 64 slots, so keys collide and the probe runs), a non-constant case (the order of evaluation: log `12`, and the discriminant is evaluated once), and `continue`, `break`, a labeled `break` out of a nested switch, a closure over a `let` of the switch scope and a read in its dead zone.
- `bytecode`: the op table test covers the new letter, and that a switch does not fall through and is not a safepoint.

The first run of the script tests crashed (SIGSEGV): a test helper dropped the `SharedAtoms` before the verifier read the atoms of the code. Fixed in the test (the atoms must outlive the code, as `Code` says). It was not a bug of the new code. Windows 11 VM (`cargo xwin test`, MSVC, exe through `/data/vms/winssh`): 365 pass and 2 fail, the two known corpus-path tests (`parse::tests::corpus_status_matches_acorn` and `parse::lazy_tests::a_lazy_parse_finds_the_same_errors_as_a_full_parse_on_the_corpus`). `cargo clippy --locked -p bare-js2 --all-targets`: no new warning (the old ones are in `heap.rs`, `crates/os` and the census examples).

Known gaps:

- A sparse integer switch with many cases keeps the chain (JSC has a sorted list for it). A chain is correct, and the cost grows with the number of cases.
- A switch with one case that is not a constant keeps the whole chain. V8 and JSC also give up on the table there. A table for the constants before the first non-constant case, and a chain after it, would be right and is not built.
- `case -0:` is not an integer constant (`int_const` refuses it), so such a switch keeps the chain. The discriminant `-0` does match `case 0` in a table.
- A string discriminant that has no hash yet pays one pass over its units. The cell keeps the hash, so a string that is a key again pays once.
- A table with 3 cases of strings uses 14 words where the chain uses 7; the gain is 6% of one switch turn.

Not tested: Miri on the new arms (they are safe code in an `unsafe` module; the arms use the same string helpers as `JSEqA`); arm64; the effect on a real bundle (how many switches of jQuery or a React bundle become tables, and what it saves there); wall time; the cost matrix (js2 is not wired into the browser); the plain loops with `codegen-units=1`; a switch with more than 65,535 words of tables (the wide form of the op is covered by the encoder tests, not by a switch).

## 2026-11-20: a cheaper host call of the interface form (A1c cost rule)

Task: PR #762 (A1c) had rows over +0.5% under both allocators: `attr_load churn 1` and `churn 10`, `react 1` and `react 10` (+0.57% to +0.63%), and `select_load react 1000` (+0.775%). At `codegen-units=1` the row `attr_load churn 10` was on the limit. The owner's rule: make the call path cheaper; ask for no exception. Base: `6067b9fb` (the engine and browser crates are the same as origin/main `b0b12935`).

Where the cost was. `callgrind` on `attr_load churn 1` (14,204 converted calls): `call_api_host` 49 instructions a call, `Dom::call_scoped` 31, the old path (`call_host` + `Dom::call`) about 40 for the same work. In `call_api_host` the host pointer cost 6 instructions: `Rc<dyn Host>::as_deref` reads the alignment from the vtable. The checks of `nt` and `is_new` ran on every plain call. For `select_load react 1000` the call path was not the cause. The call path was equal to the old one (149,352 calls: +17.2 M instructions new, -16.3 M old). The cost was in the handler `NodeList.length`: three hash lookups of the list for each call (`list_of`, `prepare`, the read of the length), and the push of the result.

Levers. Each count is `hco_micro`: a loop of 200,000 calls of one handler; instructions a call = (count(200,000) - count(0)) / 200,000; `perf stat -e instructions:u`, minimum of 3 runs, release build. The loop itself costs 1,631 instructions an iteration. `hasChildNodes` (`has`), `isSameNode` (`same`), `hasAttributes` (`attrs`).

| State | `has` | `same` | `attrs` |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| Base `6067b9fb` (handlers of the old form) | 2404 | 3183 | 2401 |
| PR #762 head (`167e105a`, merged with main) | 2396 | 3321 | 2414 |
| Lever 1: `ApiState::host_ptr` (the host address, set in `set_host`) | 2391 | 3316 | 2409 |
| Lever 2: `call_api_plain`, the plain call has its own entry | 2383 | 3308 | 2401 |
| Lever 2 with `#[inline(never)]` in place of `#[cold]` (kept) | 2383 | 3308 | 2401 |

So the engine side now costs 13 instructions a call less than the PR head (5 for lever 1, 8 for lever 2). Lever 3 is the `NodeList.length` read in `browser_nodelist.rs`: one lookup of the list when its cache is fresh (`is_fresh`, the same test that `fill` used), and the old three lookups for a stale list. It is -1.3% on `select_load react 1000`.

Tried and not kept:

- A read of `this` first in `api_at` (`slot == WIN`), and a window test first (`slot - WIN < 2^30`): +30 instructions a call on `has` and `attrs`, 0 on `same`. The larger `api_at` stops LLVM from inlining `node_of` into `el_s` and the reads of the handlers. A smaller `api_at` is better than a faster `this` read.
- `this` stored by pointer in `Win` (`*const Value`): +3. The call saves the copy of 16 bytes, but every read of `this` loads one more.
- `#[inline(always)]` on the closure of `enter` in the call: 0 (it was inlined already). `#[inline(always)]` on `api_at`: 0.
- Not tried: no bounds check of `Dom::scoped[id]` (2 instructions; the id is safe only while every id comes from `add_fn_s`), the `style.cur` write (the handlers read it), and one flag for `ce.on` and `mo.armed()` (two structs; 2 instructions).

Matrix. Machine archMachine, `tools/js/cost_matrix.sh -j4`, 817 rows, base `6067b9fb`, new = the head of this branch. The soundness test `a_panic_in_a_host_call_unlinks_its_window` and the GC-root tests pass. The window is unlinked on panic as before (`WinGuard` is unchanged).

| Row | Before, default | Now, default | Before, cgu=1 | Now, cgu=1 |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| `attr_load churn 1` | +0.573% | +0.376% | +0.474% | +0.241% |
| `attr_load churn 10` | +0.576% | +0.355% | +0.441% to +0.514% | +0.214% |
| `attr_load react 1` | +0.610% | +0.296% | +0.358% | -0.018% |
| `attr_load react 10` | +0.633% | +0.282% | +0.384% | -0.017% |
| `select_load react 1000` | +0.775% | -1.295% | +0.496% | -1.680% |

- Default flags: over +0.5% under both allocators: 0 rows. Over under glibc only: `scripts_load reject 1` +0.618% (jemalloc +0.004%) and `fetch_load bytes 10` +0.513% (jemalloc +0.309%). `parse_load deep 1` and `10` fail to run on both trees (known). Mean change: glibc -0.019%.
- `codegen-units=1` on both trees (glibc): over +0.5% under both: 0 rows. The highest rows: `scripts_load reject 1` +0.624% (glibc only; jemalloc -0.003% at default flags and the same row at both settings, so a layout effect of the allocator), `session_load chain 10` +0.487%. Mean change -0.027%. The same 2 `parse_load` rows fail on both trees.
- The first matrix of this head showed `nodelist_load scan 10` at +0.648% under both allocators. A first version of the `length` change looked up the list again for a stale list. The second version (this one) gives `scan 10` -0.376%.

Tests. Linux: `cargo test --locked -p bare-js-api -p bare-js -p bare --lib`: 32, 1104 (1 ignored) and 1714 (6 ignored) pass. The filters `attr nodelist dataset element elements html reflect nodecmp chardata fragment namespace slot shadow table details svg gaps shims basics handlers cookie scoped custom domexception mutation range select browser_tests` on `bare --lib` (600 tests, 1 ignored): pass plain, with `BARE_GC_STRESS=1` and with `BARE_ALL_API=1`. `bare-js` filters `api_tests host_nt` (50 tests): pass plain and with `BARE_GC_STRESS=1`. Windows 11 VM (`cargo xwin test --no-run`, `winssh`): `bare-js-api` 32, `bare-js` filters `api_tests host_nt` 50, `bare` the same 600-test filters (1 ignored): pass.

- A bug found by the feature tests and fixed: the table of jump targets was keyed by the address of the words, and a freed code and a new one at the same address shared an entry (index out of bounds in 16 tests). It is keyed by address and length now, and `reset` clears it. A program that frees code while it runs is still not counted right.

## 2026-11-20: js2 steps 1 to 4 of the superinstruction design (build)

Design: `docs/design-js2-superinstructions.md`, section 5, with the owner decisions of section 10. One PR for each step, in order, each measured before the next. Fusion (step 5) waits for the histogram taken after step 4.

Method of every step. Machine: archMachine, AMD Ryzen 9 5900HX, Linux. Release builds of `script_run` (a separate `CARGO_TARGET_DIR` for each step). Instructions are `instructions:u` of `perf stat`, with `GLIBC_TUNABLES=glibc.malloc.tcache_count=65535` as in `tools/js/instr.sh`, 3 runs of each cell; the table gives the minimum and the spread `(max - min) / min` of the 3 runs. Inputs: the 9 `eval_load` programs at scale 1 and 10 (`eval_load CASE SCALE --source`), run as `script_run --eval FILE EXPECTED`; the bundle-like program (`crates/js2/examples/data/bundle_like.js`); an empty program. QuickJS `quickjs-2026-06-04`, `qjs` with `console.log(String((0, eval)(SRC)))`, same inputs. All program files sit under one short path: the QuickJS count of `throws` depends on the length of the file path (it builds a stack string with it), 85.1 M here against 88.5 M in the S2.9 entry. The gate of S2 is the net slope: instructions at scale 10 minus instructions at scale 1, at or below QuickJS (design question 1).

### Step 1: keep `__def` and hide it

Bug: `script::load` deleted the `__def` global after the prelude. `__def` was the first property added to the global object, so the delete put the object in dictionary mode, and a dictionary shape is never cached (`Shapes::cacheable`). Every `GetGlobal` and `SetGlobal` took the slow path. Fix (owner decision, question 2): the loader keeps the property and sets its value to `undefined` (`Realm::define`; no shape change). The property was already not enumerable. A script sees `typeof __def === "undefined"`, `Object.keys(globalThis)` does not list it, and `var __def = 5` still works. Limit: `"__def" in globalThis` is `true`, and a read of `__def` gives `undefined` where a missing name gives a `ReferenceError`.

Failing test first: `script::tests::load_keeps_the_global_object_in_the_shape_tree` failed on #765 ("the global object is in dictionary mode after load") and passes with the fix. `def_is_hidden_after_load` passes on both.

The "#765" column is the unfixed head of #765 (variant A of the S2.9 entry). Its numbers vary from run to run of one binary (S2.9 entry), so read its `loop`, `calls` and `objects` rows as one sample. The new column is the same as variant B of the S2.9 entry.
